title: Improved Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control With Disturbance Observer for Five-Phase Fault-Tolerant IPM Motor Drives
abstract: This paper presents a composite control strategy for five-phase fault-tolerant fractional-slot concentrated winding interior permanent magnet (FTFSCW-IPM) motor drives, aiming to alleviate the long-standing trade-off between fast dynamic response, chattering suppression, and disturbance rejection in sliding mode control. A variable exponential fast terminal reaching law with a continuous switching function is developed to explicitly shape the reaching dynamics, enabling rapid convergence when the system state is far from the sliding surface while ensuring smooth behavior near the surface. To further enhance robustness against load torque disturbances, a Luenberger torque disturbance observer (LTDO) with a slightly enhanced correction structure is incorporated as a feedforward compensation channel, thereby decoupling disturbance rejection from the sliding-mode switching gain design. In addition, a systematic comparative study involving four representative control schemes is conducted to clearly distinguish the individual and combined effects of the fast terminal sliding mode structure and the disturbance observer. Both simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy achieves excellent speed tracking performance and improved disturbance rejection under sudden load torque variations.

title: A New Approach for Predicting Modal Damping of the Laminated Motor Stator Considering Anisotropic Damping Properties in the Simulative Design Phase
abstract: The damping ratio of the motor seriously affects the peak value of radiated noise caused by structural resonance. However, affected by structural discontinuity and anisotropic material properties, predicting damping ratio of the laminated stator remains a research gap when there are no motor prototypes. To overcome the severe dependence of damping identification on motor prototypes and modal experiments, a new approach for predicting damping ratio of the laminated stator is proposed. Firstly, the calculation principles of material damping loss factors at the mesoscopic level and modal damping ratios at the macroscopic level are introduced. Then, the mesoscopic material model of the laminated stator is established and the anisotropic damping loss factors are further calculated, revealing the influence of laminating effect on material damping. Afterwards, an analytical structural dynamics model of the stator is established and natural frequencies, damping ratios and modal shapes are calculated simultaneously. Furthermore, the contribution of damping energy in six deformation states to the modal damping ratios of each modal order is investigated, revealing the influence mechanism of anisotropic damping loss factors on modal damping ratio. Finally, the computational accuracy of the proposed method is verified by modal experiments. The maximum relative error of natural frequencies is within 2% and the maximum absolute error of in-phase modal damping ratios is 0.06%.

title: Analysis of a Linear-Rotary Magnetic Field Modulation Generator for Wave Energy Conversion
abstract: In order to solve the problems of low ‘power/volume’ or low ‘power/cost’ caused by the low speed of wave energy converter (WEC), a linear-rotary magnetic field modulation generator (LMFMG) is proposed. The three-dimensional structure and working principle of LMFMG are introduced. The air gap flux density of the magnetic gear screw is calculated to verify the magnetic field modulation principle and the speed-up mechanism. After comparative analysis, the optimized parameters and output parameters of the LMFMG are given. The back EMF, loss and efficiency of the rotary generator are calculated. Through magnetic field modulation, the proposed LMFMG can convert the linear motion of 0.5 m/s into a high-speed rotational motion of 10000 rpm. Compared with the existing WEC, the proposed LMFMG has higher ‘power/volume’ and ‘power/cost’, which makes it very potential in WEC. The prototype is manufactured and the experimental platform is built. The thrust, torque, current and back EMF are measured to verify the theoretical calculation results of LMFMG.

title: Localized Asymmetric Behavior of Common-Mode Current Through Bearing Balls
abstract: The high-frequency pulse width modulation in voltage source inverters generates common-mode voltage and current in inverter-fed electrical machine drive systems, leading to high-frequency bearing currents and potential bearing damage. Due to the enclosed structure of bearings and the distributed nature of bearing currents, accurate measurement remains challenging. This paper reviews existing measurement methods and identifies a previously unreported bearing current component caused by uneven potential distribution on the end-caps, termed the “end-cap bearing current.” The “end-cap bearing current” occurs exclusively when the bearings are in a conducting state, which can happen during low-speed operation or bearing breakdown. Experimental results from a modified end-cap setup with multiple connection wires reveal asymmetric radial current flow through bearing balls, which is not captured by conventional single-wire measurement methods. A 3D finite element model and an enhanced circuit model are developed to illustrate the underlying mechanism. The study demonstrates that up to 25% of the high-frequency common-mode current in the end-cap may flow through the bearing balls under conductive conditions, highlighting the limitations of existing measurement techniques and the need for more accurate bearing current assessment.

title: Investigation of Post-Demagnetization Torque Ripple in Integer-Slot Surface-Mounted PM Wind Power Generators After Short-Circuit Faults
abstract: This article investigates the post-demagnetization torque ripple of integer-slot surface-mounted PM (SPM) wind power generators after three-phase short-circuit (3PSC) faults. Firstly, the demagnetization distribution pattern is analyzed by analytically modelling demagnetizing MMF from 3PSC currents. It is revealed that there exists a severest demagnetization line, which shifts from the PM pole axis in the rotating direction. The demagnetization level gradually decreases in the radial direction away from the airgap and along both sides in the circumferential direction. Thereafter, the article investigates the post-demagnetization torque ripple by analyzing cogging torque and back-EMF harmonics, respectively. It is found that, under low PM temperature, the cogging torque decreases when demagnetization deteriorates. With higher PM temperature, the cogging torque first decreases and then increases. Additionally, both back-EMF harmonic and the resulting torque ripple decrease with demagnetization aggravating. Although the harmonic torque ripple and cogging torque amplitude exhibit opposite phases, the former has a smaller amplitude. Therefore, the total torque ripple follows the variation trend of cogging torque with demagnetization level. Most importantly, the torque ripple is more likely to exceed the pre-demagnetization value when PM temperature increases. Furthermore, the influence of 3PSC start rotor position is investigated. It is found demagnetization is the least severe when 3PSC starts at 7π/6+kπ/3 (k = 1, 2, 3…), yet with the largest torque ripple. Finally, experiments are conducted to validate the theoretical analysis.

title: A Finite Element Analysis-Thermal Network Model Hybrid for Steady-State Heat Estimation of an On-Board HTS in Electromagnetic Launching System
abstract: In this article, a thermal network modeling method is proposed for an on-board HTS magnet, which functions as the moving magnet in a superconducting linear synchronous motor and electrodynamic suspension system used in electromagnetic launching applications. The on-board HTS magnet is cooled by cryogenic helium gas with solid-nitrogen (SN2) protection. The thermal network model (TNM) is coupled with the finite element analysis (FEA) method. First, the structure of and simplification method for the on-board HTS magnet are introduced in detail. Second, the thermal processes and corresponding thermal network of the on-board HTS magnet are presented. Third, to verify the effectiveness of the proposed FEA−TNM hybrid, an SN2-prorection HTS magnet prototype is fabricated, and its thermal characteristics are tested by different refrigeration experiments. The measured and calculated temperatures of the sensors installed in different temperature ranges agree well with each other. On the basis of the verified model, a thermal optimization strategy is discussed. The results of this article provide a fast simulation method for the thermal design and optimization of HTS magnets.

title: Homopolar Rotor Slot Harmonics for Inter-Turn Fault Detection in Induction Motors
abstract: Stator faults detection under normal operation is one of the most important open problems in Induction Motors (IMs): they start as Inter-Turn Faults (ITFs) and rapidly evolve into catastrophic failures, being one of the major causes of shutdown. Hence, continuous monitoring is essential for early detection. Regarding this, line current analysis is preferred due to ease of equipment installation. In this paper, a new ITF indicator is proposed: amplitude of the homopolar Rotor Slot Harmonics (RSHs); those that form a homopolar system in a symmetrical machine. These harmonics are proven as always highly sensitive, opposite to previously used RSHs, which appear as sensitive or completely insensitive, depending on the motor analyzed. It is shown how ITF detection can be reliably solved using homopolar RSHs: they dramatically rise under early ITFs. To achieve generality, a theoretical analysis is conducted to deduce which are these RSHs as a function of the number of bars per pole pairs of the IM. Moreover, the proposed approach automatically selects and detects these harmonics, and ensures robustness against load, eccentricity and voltage unbalance variations. Efficacy of this approach is confirmed through finite element simulations of three IMs covering all cases and laboratory tests.

title: A Computationally-Efficient, Finite-Position-Set Phase-Locked Loop Incorporating Harmonic-Suppression Capability for PMSM Sensorless Drives
abstract: The finite-position-set phase-locked loop (FPS-PLL) has been extensively studied due to its excellent dynamic response, but its high computational burden and insufficient steady-state accuracy need to be further overcome. To address these limitations, a computationally-efficient FPS-PLL incorporating harmonic-suppression capability is proposed for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) sensorless drives. Firstly, the mechanisms and drawbacks of conventional PLL and existing FPS-PLLs are analyzed. Afterwards, to address the FPS-PLL's susceptibility to direct current (DC) and harmonic interference, a novel cost function incorporating harmonic-suppression capability based on a modified integral segment is designed to improve the interference immunity. Subsequently, a simple initial sector boundary setting scheme based on the novel cost function is presented, providing the initial iteration value that satisfies the local convergence criteria and is close to the actual position. Further, the Newton iteration process is executed twice to obtain the accurate rotor position information, thereby achieving the low computational burden. A linear tracking differentiator-based speed observer is designed to extract the rotor speed, avoiding the noise amplification associated with a direct differential operator. Finally, the validity of the proposed FPS-PLL estimator is verified by experimental results.

title: Driving Parameters Optimization for Mitigating Voltage Reflection in SiC-Based Motor Drives
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) devices offer significantly faster switching speeds than traditional silicon devices, thereby improving motor drive efficiency. However, these high switching speeds can exacerbate voltage reflection issues, especially when the motor is connected via long cables. Although driving parameters are often tuned to address this, existing techniques struggle to balance effective voltage suppression with acceptable switching losses. This paper proposes an approach to simultaneously mitigate voltage reflection and reduce switching losses through optimized driving circuit design. Specifically, it analyzes the effects of key parameters: gate resistance and external Miller capacitance on voltage behavior and energy loss. A detailed model is developed to characterize both the voltage reflection process and the switching dynamics of SiC MOSFETs in a single phase-leg configuration. Based on this model, the study quantifies how voltage transition time and switching loss evolve under various drive conditions. Furthermore, a Pareto front-based optimization method is introduced to balance the trade-off between voltage slew rate and switching efficiency. Experimental validation on a 1.2 kW SiC-based motor drive shows that voltage overshoot can be reduced from 83.3% to 63.3% by optimizing the gate resistor, while adding an external Miller capacitor further reduces it to 23.3%, a 40% improvement over resistor adjustment alone, with only a 0.06% efficiency penalty.

title: Comparative Analysis of Pendulum and Flywheel Power Take-Off Mechanisms for Wave Energy Conversion
abstract: This study compares three power-take-off (PTO) mechanisms for wave energy converters—a flywheel-type pitch resonator and two pendulum variants (normal and inverted)—all designed to fit within a fixed envelope. Performance is assessed via linear frequency-domain models and bi-conjugate impedance matching under a representative sea state. The inverted-pendulum PTO achieves 27.9% of the incident wave energy, versus 16.5% for the normal pendulum and 4.2% for the flywheel—that is, 6.6 × and 3.9 × improvements, respectively. These gains arise because pendulum-based systems generate higher torque for a given buoy motion and maintain impedance matching across a wider frequency band. Parametric studies of mass, pendulum arm length, spring stiffness, generator friction, and motor constant quantify the impact of key design choices on power output. By locating the pendulum pivot near the buoy’s center of gravity and positioning the center of rotation below the COG, surge–pitch coupling is improved and energy transfer is further boosted.

title: Model-Free Predictive Current Control for PMSM Drives Using an Improved Dynamic Linearization Data Model
abstract: Model predictive control has attracted much attention in electric drives, but its parameter sensitivity on explicit models poses inherent challenges to the further application. This paper proposes an improved model-free predictive current control (MFPCC) based on a full-form dynamic linearization (FFDL) data model. Through the pseudo gradient (PG) and estimation algorithm, the FFDL modeling method only uses the input-output data of the system. However, the accuracy of the classic FFDL data model relies heavily on the PG initial value, which is related to the plant. In order to reduce the initial value dependence, this paper further improves the FFDL technique with a diagonal gain matrix, while the stability analysis and parameter design guidance are given. With only simple parameter design, the proposed method can establish a prediction model based on the input-output data to deal with uncertain systems. Finally, the performance of the proposed method is verified on a PMSM experimental platform with a three-level neutral-point-clamped inverter.

title: Improved Design-Oriented Analytical Model for Switched Reluctance Machines’ Unsaturated Inductance in Non-Overlap Conditions
abstract: Design-oriented analytical modelling of switched reluctance machines (SRMs) is currently an active field of research, as it significantly alleviates the computational burden of design processes by replacing or complementing finite element analysis. The modelling of saturated SRMs, including the determination of saturated flux loci and the calculation of torque and current waveforms, requires prior knowledge of the unsaturated inductance vs rotor position profile. This work proposes an improved analytical model to determine unsaturated inductances in non-overlap conditions, based on a twofold improvement of the permeance method: the use of elliptic flux tubes; and the ability to self-tailor the flux tube shapes to any machine geometry. Its accuracy is proven against finite element analysis applied to four designs and against experimental results of a full-scale prototype. Finally, it is shown how the model can be incorporated into a fully analytical design tool, whose accuracy in calculating performance and computational burden are evaluated.

title: Sensorless V/f Control With Arbitrary Power Sharing Capability for Six-Phase Induction Machines in Hybrid PV/Wind Water Pumping Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel hybrid renewable water pumping system (WPS) designed for remote areas, utilizing solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind energy to drive a six-phase induction machine (6PIM). Compared to conventional three-phase machines, the 6PIM offers improved fault tolerance, scalability, and reduced converter ratings. The proposed modular architecture assigns each three-phase winding set a dedicated power converter, enabling independent control and enhancing system reliability. To simplify implementation and reduce cost, a sensorless voltage-to-frequency (V/f) control strategy is adopted. This eliminates the need for current and speed sensors, making the approach especially suitable for off-grid water pumping applications where robustness is more critical than fast dynamic response. A key contribution of this work is the integration of flexible power-sharing control into the V/f framework, marking, to the best of the authors’ knowledge, its first application in multiphase drives. The system is validated through simulations on a 200 HP model under realistic solar and wind profiles, as well as experimental tests on a 1.5 HP prototype with an emulated centrifugal pump load. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme in achieving stable operation and efficient energy utilization under varying input and load conditions.

title: Influence of Rotor Back-Iron on Optimal Halbach PM Machines
abstract: Due to transition permanent magnets (PMs) with high tangential magnetization component and located between main PMs, i.e., N and S poles, Halbach machines are featured for self-shielding effect. Consequently, rotor back-iron is not essential. In this paper, Halbach machines with optimal PM widths and optimal magnetization angles for the maximum torque are investigated. It is found that regardless of PM segment number per pole, in optimal air-cored Halbach machines, PM widths are almost equal and magnetization angle shifts between adjacent PMs are almost equal too. Therefore, the equal air-cored machines can be regarded as the optimal machines. In optimal Halbach machines with rotor back-iron, main PM widths are much larger than transition PM widths and magnetization angle shifts between main and transition PMs are lower than corresponding equal magnetization angle shifts. Therefore, the airgap field in optimal iron-cored Halbach machines exhibits a significant 3rd harmonic field component and higher fundamental airgap field, and consequently the larger torque. Meanwhile, as the PM becomes thicker and the split ratio becomes lower, PM widths and magnetization angle shifts between adjacent PMs in optimal iron-cored machines both change from corresponding unequal values to almost equal. A prototype of optimal air-cored Halbach machine is fabricated and tested to verify the finite element analysis results.

title: Additional AC Copper Losses in the Field Winding of Converter-Fed Synchronous Machines for Pumped Storage Hydropower Plants
abstract: Converter-fed synchronous machines for variable speed pumped storage hydropower plants are becoming increasingly important as the share of fluctuating renewable energy increases. The inverter connected to the stator terminals causes additional harmonic currents in the stator winding, which induce additional harmonic currents in the field winding. Due to the eddy current effects and the typical form-wound coil design, these additional harmonic currents in the field winding can lead to significant additional losses, even with relatively small amplitudes. The aim of this paper is to calculate these additional losses. Therefore, numerical calculations are used to determine the resistance factor for a frequency band from $\text{0}\,\text{Hz}$ to $\text{15}\,\text{kHz}$ while also considering saturation. In addition, two measurements are carried out on a research hydro generator at different inverter switching frequencies. Using the measured currents and determined resistance factors, the additional losses due to the switching frequency are calculated and validated using a temperature measurement in the field winding. The results of this work are important for the future design and cooling of large converter-fed synchronous machines with form-wound field coils, as the additional AC losses in the field winding are usually neglected.

title: Controllability and Small-Signal Oscillations of Magnetic Flux Linkages in Doubly Fed Induction Machines
abstract: This paper examines the controllability of the stator and rotor magnetic flux linkages of doubly fed induction machines (DFIMs), considering small-signal oscillations and their relationship with electromagnetic machine design. To this aim, we first analyze 66 sets of lumped parameters from the dynamic model of a DFIM. Based on this, we classify DFIMs into three categories based on their modal parameters, namely, two for wind applications and one for pumped-hydro applications. Additionally, we identify reciprocal relationships between the damping of both identified oscillatory modes and the largest eigenvalues of the stator and rotor controllability Gramian matrices. Among the different lumped parameters, the winding resistances are found to influence these relationships the most. All analyzed DFIMs for wind applications were found to be less controllable and to exhibit better damping of oscillatory modes than DFIMs for pumped-hydro applications. Furthermore, based on the results of the controllability analysis, we selected three objective function candidates suitable for an optimization procedure aimed at minimizing the energy required to control the rotor flux linkages. An example objective function was evaluated in a multi-objective DFIM design process for wind applications that enables the design of more controllable machines that provide the desired damping of oscillations, which can consequently contribute to improving grid resilience.

title: Analysis and Elimination of Current Measurement Scaling Error for High-Frequency Voltage Injection-Based Sensorless Control
abstract: Current measurement scaling error (CMSE) is a common problem in permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) drive systems. It can be categorized into current measurement scaling difference error (CMSDE) and current measurement scaling average error (CMSAE). This research aims to analyze and eliminate the effects of the CMSE on rotating high-frequency voltage injection (HFVI)-based sensorless control. Firstly, a detailed analysis of the CMSE-induced position estimation error is presented, revealing the relationship between the position estimation error and the CMSE. It indicates that the CMSE introduces both a DC offset and a 2nd harmonic into the position estimation. Secondly, an effective sequential elimination strategy is proposed to address the CMSDE as its first step, and then the CMSAE as the second step. A moving average filter (MAF) is designed to extract the error signal, followed by a sliding mode controller (SMC) to eliminate the CMSDE and CMSAE. Finally, the theoretical analysis and the elimination methods of the CMSE have been validated by the experimental results.

title: Detent Force Reduction of a Permanent Magnet Linear Motor With Composite Mover Core by Changing the Magnetic Distribution
abstract: To reduce the thrust ripple of permanent magnet synchronous linear motor (PMSLM), a composite mover core is proposed, consisting of a silicon steel core at the center and amorphous alloy cores at both ends along the stacking direction. A transverse magnetic circuit model is established to investigate the influence of air-gap magnetic field distribution on thrust performance. In addition, a coupled model that incorporates eddy current loss, magnetic phase difference, and detent force is developed to analyze the interaction between the composite core materials and their electromagnetic characteristics. The analysis reveals that the detent force is highly dependent on the proportion of different core materials. By optimizing the composite mover structure, both thrust ripple and the peak-to-peak detent force can be significantly reduced. For a 9-slot/10-pole PMSLM, the thrust ripple decreases from 12.05% to 4.32% while maintaining the original thrust and volume. Furthermore, compared with traditional end auxiliary structures, the PMSLM with a composite mover core has advantages of higher power and thrust densities, as well as reduced normal electromagnetic force fluctuations.

title: Data-Driven Reduced Order Modeling of Induction Motors Using Dynamic Mode Decomposition and Deep Koopman Theory
abstract: The presence of unbalances modifies the nonlinear dynamics of an induction motor drive. Data-driven models are becoming increasingly relevant for model predictive control as they can infer dynamics directly from data, thereby automatically calibrating to the system at hand. In this work, dynamic mode decomposition with control is improved for induction motors by learning a time-variant system. Hereafter, Koopman theory is applied to linearise the state nonlinearity. The algorithms are trained on simulation data using Direct Torque Control. Time-invariant dynamic mode decomposition with control and a symmetrical multiple coupled circuit model are used as reference models. Two orders of magnitude improvement of the stator current prediction is achieved, which is maintained for extensive prediction distances. Moreover, Koopman theory increases long-term stability. The proposed models are validated for torque control in a simulated environment. They are found to be useful for situations where high accuracy is required or where drive dynamics are particularly unknown. In future work, neural architecture optimisation and experimental validation will be explored.

title: Performance Analysis of a Rare-Earth-Free Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Motor Using a PCB Stator
abstract: Simplicity in structure and minimal material usage are key factors in reducing manufacturing costs, which is essential for staying competitive in the global market of mass-produced sub-fractional horsepower brushless permanent magnet motors. This paper analyzes the performance of an axial flux permanent magnet motor using a printed circuit board (PCB) stator for sub-fractional horsepower drives that – in contrast to the coreless PCB motors – employs a ferrite core. The investigation shows that, despite this seemingly added cost, the overall motor not only exhibits superior performance compared to the conventional structure but actually comes at reduced cost. This is due to low-cost ferrite magnets can be used instead of rare- earth magnets, and the core shape being optimized for cost-efficient PCB integration. The motor structure and key design considerations are described, and a specialized test rig is introduced to address the unique measurement challenges of sub-fractional horsepower machines. The motor's performance is analyzed theoretically and experimentally under both no-load and load conditions. The findings confirm the potential of the investigated motor topology for radial fan applications.

title: Time-Domain Modeling of IPMSM Considering Magnet Eddy Current Reaction Effect and Cross Coupling
abstract: In interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs), accurately predicting the armature currents under PWM voltage supply is challenging, particularly for the harmonic components, due to a number of issues including magnetic saturation, spatial harmonics, cross coupling, and magnet eddy current reaction. In this paper, an improved time-domain model of the IPMSM with rotor virtual short-circuit windings is proposed to incorporate all these relevant effects, especially the magnet eddy current reaction effect and cross coupling in both stator windings and rotor virtual windings. The parameters of the rotor virtual windings can be identified through a standstill time-domain response (SSTR) test using the finite element (FE) method. FE simulation results and experiments of a 2.4 kW, 12 krpm 9-slot 6-pole IPMSM confirm that the proposed time-domain model has rather high accuracy in armature current prediction. The simulations of electromagnetic performance and temperature field further demonstrate that the more accurate prediction of armature currents provided by the proposed model result in a more accurate evaluation of electromagnetic performance and temperature rise for the IPMSM.

title: An Improved Radial Displacement Control Considering Mass Difference Between Two Shaft Ends to Increase the Rotor Fatigue Life
abstract: Notch filters (NFs) are widely applied in the five-degrees of freedom (5-DoFs) magnetic levitation motors to reduce the vibration near the resonant frequency. However, due to the existence of axial thrust disk, rotor masses at the two ends of the shaft are generally different. It not only increases the difficulty of NF design, but also reduces of fatigue life of rotor system. Therefore, a cross displacement control (CDC) method is proposed in this paper to synchronize the displacements at the two ends, which reduces the number of NFs and improves the fatigue life of rotor system. Simulation and experimental results show that the fatigue life of rotor system can be improved by 17.70 times, 21% and 10% at 4000 r/min, 10000 r/min and 20000 r/min, respectively. On the basis of that, the phase-shift NF can also be added to reduce the vibration near the resonant frequency. Experimental results verify that the fatigue life of rotor system can be improved by 26.5% near the resonant frequency with proposed strategy, and the adjustable time of displacement can also be reduced by 51.7%.

title: The Viability of DC-VRM Synchronous Condensers
abstract: In this paper, the feasibility of using DC excited vernier reluctance machines (DC-VRMs) as brushless synchronous condensers (SC) is assessed with a 12/10 DC-VRM prototype as a case study. Although the 12/10 DC-VRM topology has characteristics auspicious for SC operations, discrepancies between measured and expected prototype performances, especially with increasing excitation, are illustrated. Also, strong vibrations which are proportional to the level of excitation were experienced while testing, and these are highlighted. Possible saturation and the nature of forces in the 12/10 DC-VRM are first examined to determine the cause of the under-performance and vibrations. Modal analysis of the prototype structure is also conducted to investigate possible cases of resonance. Although, there is evidence of some resonance, the dynamic concentration of radial forces in sections of the air-gap is identified as the main cause of the poor performances and vibrations. Different skewing methods are then investigated to reduce the radial force concentration, but they are largely inadequate. However, it is highlighted that the 24/10 DC-VRM topology can be a practical alternative with similar output as the 12/10 topology and better force distribution.

title: Transfer Learning for Data-Efficient Magnetic Core Loss Modeling in Electrical Machines via Parametric Homogenization and Neural Networks
abstract: Despite the urgent demand in industry, there do not yet exist practical and accurate simulation methods for calculating the magnetic losses of ferromagnetic laminated cores in electrical machine (EM) simulations. Transfer learning, a machine learning technique, utilizes a model developed for one task as a starting point for developing a model for another task. This study innovatively integrates parametric homogenized material laws with deep learning (DL) approaches. Firstly, the intrinsic resistance parameters characterizing core material properties are investigated through the combined application of the Bertotti model and an improved equivalent circuit model. Experimental data from prototypes are then used to visualize the influence patterns of different temperatures, harmonics, loads, and frequencies on these derived parameters. To both reduce the required data for improved performance and model the underlying mechanisms of mutual parameter impact, a sizeable auxiliary dataset was synthetically generated through the synergistic application of support vector machine, decision tree, and backpropagation (BP) neural network algorithms. By leveraging the pre-learned patterns of parameter variation, auxiliary data, and a small set of target data covering high-frequency, high-temperature, and high-load conditions, a two-stage feature transfer learning process is implemented using deep sparse autoencoder and BP neural network. Finally, comparative experiments are designed to verify the limitations of existing loss evaluation methods and to emphasize the importance of comprehensively considering multi-factor coupling effects in EM core loss modeling. The results demonstrate that the proposed local material law can serve as a conventional constitutive relationship in two-dimensional or three-dimensional modeling, and, when combined with DL algorithms, achieves a massive speed-up compared to monolithic coupling.

title: General Selection Methodology for the Stator-Poles and Rotor Teeth Combinations of Stator-Permanent Magnet Flux-Switching Machines
abstract: This paper proposes a general selection methodology for the stator-poles and rotor teeth (Ps-Tr) combination of stator-permanent magnet flux-switching (SPM-FS) machines. With the purpose of establishing complementary mechanism, achieving the highest winding factor, and minimizing the cogging torque, this paper investigates the Ps-Tr combination of U-core SPM-FS machines at first to serve as a reference. Aiming to deduce a universal method, the feasible Ps-Tr combinations are generalized to SPM-FS machines with E-core, C-core, and V-shaped PM structures, respectively. During the process, the selection procedures are formed for the SPM-FS machines with different phase number and various structures. In addition, four representative cases are analyzed to verify the proposed methodology through finite element analysis and prototype experiments. The results not only indicate the convenience and feasibility of the proposed methodology, but also verify the universality on SPM-FS machines with different topologies.

title: Adaptive Pump Fault Detection for Vanadium Redox Flow Batteries Based on CNN-BiGRU and Transfer Learning
abstract: Vanadium redox flow batteries (VRBs) are vulnerable to pump malfunctions, which can cause severe problems like overcharging, overdischarging, and irreversible damage to the battery stack. Effective real-time fault detection methods for VRBs are essential but underdeveloped. This study proposes a data-driven approach for VRB pump fault detection using a convolutional neural network combined with bi-directional gated recurrent units to predict voltage based on measurable current, flow rate, and state of charge without relying on complex electrochemical models. To address the impact of battery aging and system variability, which are often overlooked in the literature, an offline transfer learning strategy with model tail fine-tuning is employed to adapt the parameters of the pre-trained model using a small amount of newly collected data. Pump faults are identified by comparing voltage prediction errors against a threshold derived from the 3σ criterion. Experimental results across six fault scenarios encompassing three distinct pump fault modes under two operational conditions demonstrate that the proposed method achieves timely and accurate fault detection, significantly improving the reliability of VRB systems.

title: Adaptive Phase Selection for Stator High-Impedance Grounding Fault Considering Winding Parameter Asymmetry and Nonlinear Potential Distribution
abstract: Accurate faulty phase selection is a prerequisite for reliable operation of stator grounding protection functions in pumped storage generator-motor (PSGM). Conventional methods overlook the natural asymmetry of the three-phase grounding parameters and the nonlinear distribution characteristics of phase potential, which causes coupling between the system inherent imbalance and the grounding fault feature. This oversight frequently leads to phase misjudgment, particularly in high-impedance grounding fault (HIGF). To address this issue, an adaptive phase selection method for stator grounding fault is proposed. First, a zero-sequence model considering parameter asymmetry of stator winding is established. An online measurement technique for asymmetric grounding parameters is developed to quantify the inherent imbalance. Then, based on winding potential distribution under different topologies, the dynamic range of phase angle for the faulty winding potential is defined. On this basis, a phase selection characteristic quantity capable of eliminating interference from random parameter asymmetry is constructed, and its mapping to the faulty phase is established. Finally, the faulty phase selection method that automatically adapts to the winding parameters and topologies is formed. Simulation, experiment and field fault data verify the feasibility of the method and its adaptability in engineering applications.

title: On the Application of the IEC 60034-2-1 Standard to Line-Start Synchronous Reluctance Motors
abstract: The IEC 60034-2-1 standard does not specify a method for three-phase line-start synchronous motors (LS-SynRMs). Although the direct input-output method can be easily applied, it does not specify how to correct the losses to a reference ambient temperature. This paper analyzes the applicability of the methods specified in the IEC 60034-2-1 standard to LS-SynRMs. The impact of ambient temperature on the full-load efficiency of LS-SynRMs is assessed. A method for segregating motor losses and correcting the average temperature and losses of the stator windings to a reference ambient temperature is proposed, ensuring that the stated full-load efficiency of the motor is determined accurately regardless of the ambient temperature in the laboratory where the tests are performed. Results from experiments conducted on two commercial LS-SynRMs are provided. It was observed that reducing the ambient temperature from 45 °C to 5 °C may increase the full-load efficiency of the tested LS-SynRMs by more than 1 percentage point, mainly due to the reduction of stator winding losses. Consequently, a motor manufacturer may consider testing this type of motor at lower ambient temperatures to achieve a higher efficiency class. Therefore, it is necessary to define a method for determining the efficiency of LS SynRMs that accounts for the correction of stator winding conduction losses to the standard reference ambient temperature of 25 °C. This paper intends to offer information that may contribute to overcoming the shortcomings and omissions of the IEC 60034-2-1 standard concerning the efficiency determination of LS-SynRMs, which is a relatively new technology on the market that is believed to be able to compete with line-operated induction motors in the low-power range, offering higher efficiency and constant operating speed.

title: Method for Identifying Equivalent Orthotropic Material Parameters of Motor for Analysis of Electromagnetic Vibrations
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid analytical–optimization framework for identifying the equivalent orthotropic material parameters of stator core and winding assemblies in electrical machines. An analytical cylindrical model is developed based on first-order shear deformation theory and Love's shell theory to establish the relationship between material properties and modal characteristics. The stator core and its components are modeled using equivalent layered cylindrical shells, incorporating structural features such as longitudinal ribs. The Firefly Algorithm is employed to solve the inverse identification problem by minimizing the discrepancy between predicted and measured natural frequencies. The material parameters of epoxy resin and winding insulation are identified, and the corresponding equivalent orthotropic material parameters are derived using composite material theory. The proposed method is validated through both analytical and finite element analyses, showing good agreement with experimental results, with relative errors within 3%. Compared with conventional optimization and data-driven approaches, the proposed framework demonstrates improved accuracy, convergence stability, and computational efficiency. The developed method provides an effective tool for vibration analysis and parameter identification in electromagnetic devices and offers potential for application in structural optimization and noise reduction design.

title: Sensorless Rotor Flux Linkage Identification for PMSMs Under Inductance Mismatches and Loaded Conditions
abstract: Achieving robust and precise identification methods for rotor flux linkage identification in permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) remains a critical challenge in electromechanical systems, especially during sensorless operation, under loaded motor conditions, and with significant mismatches in dq-axis inductance. Conventional rotor flux linkage identification methods often lack the necessary accuracy under these difficult operational constraints. To address this issue, this paper proposes a sensorless rotor flux linkage identification method based on triple current injection. The implementation involves two main stages: (1) Data Acquisition Phase: The PMSM is driven by an inverter to maintain a constant speed in sensorless I/f control mode, using a specific current amplitude in three distinct operational modes. During this phase, datasets for voltage, current, and speed commands are collected for further analysis; (2) Offline Identification Phase: A Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is applied to simultaneously estimate the rotor flux linkage and dq-axis inductances using the experimental data obtained in the previous phase. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves absolute rotor flux linkage identification errors of less than 2%, even under challenging conditions such as position-sensorless control, loaded motor operation, and dq-axis inductance mismatches of up to ±80% . These outcomes significantly outperform conventional methods, confirming the practical applicability of this approach in industrial drive systems.

title: Control Parameter Identification Method of DFIG Rotor-Side Converter Considering Fault Ride-Through
abstract: In light of the integration of large-scale wind turbine generators (WTGs) to the grid, it is very important to establish a detailed model of WTGs with consistent external characteristics of real grid-connected WTGs. However, the controller of WTGs is a ‘black box’ model with unknown control logic and control parameters. To address these issues, this paper establishes the detailed model through typical control logic and identification control parameters. In the fault ride-through process, the change in control logic of the WTGs controller leads to a change in control parameters. Consequently, a control parameter identification method considering fault ride-through is proposed. The control parameters are divided into normal control parameters (NCPs) and fault control parameters (FCPs), based on the operation state of the WTGs. A challenge in NCPs is the issue of low sensitivity parameter identification. The enhanced whale optimization algorithm is employed to identify NCPs, thereby achieving accurate identification of NCPs. The identification of FCPs is affected by the limiting link. Thus, the proposed identification method is based on voltage conditions division to realize the independent identification of FCPs. The proposed identification method is verified by MATLAB/Simulink and RT-LAB, and the results demonstrated that the proposed method realizes the accurate identification of control parameters.

title: Electropermanent Magnet Eddy Current Separator to Recycle Non-Ferrous Metals
abstract: This paper proposes and demonstrates the idea of using electropermanent magnet (EPM)-based actuator in the structure of eddy current separator to recycle non-ferrous metals. It uses a coil excited by a full-bridge inverter to statically switch the direction of magnetic flux in the EPM, inducing eddy current within metal particles. This provides a pulsating magnetic actuator to repel non-ferrous metals mixed with other materials on a recycling conveyor. Conventional eddy current separators typically use a costly and bulky rotating permanent magnet drum or a static electromagnetic coil to generate the required repulsive forces. The static EPM-based separator eliminates the need for the expensive rotating drum structure. Furthermore, it reduces power losses compared to static electromagnetic coils by using narrow-band current pulses instead of continuous sinusoidal current. A quadratic approximation of the magnetic flux density is proposed to improve the accuracy of the repulsive force calculation. The paper also elaborates on a core optimization and electromagnetic heating analysis. A proof-of-concept EPM separator is developed and experimentally tested to calculate the repulsive force based on measured deviations in particle angle and distance. Comparing the test results shows an average error of less than 5%, confirming the improved accuracy of the quadratic approximation.

title: Battery Storage in More- and All-Electric Fishing Vessels: Real-Time Simulation and Experimental Verification
abstract: The transition of fuel-reliant fishing vessels to more- and all-electric alternatives is essential to reduce the fishing industry's dependence on fuel. Most research on the energy transition in the maritime industry has focused on larger vessels. Larger vessels typically have multiple generation units; however, fishing vessels have fewer onboard resources, making control and operation more challenging. This paper introduces the development of a real-time simulation testbed for small fishing vessels using two Typhoon HIL 604 real-time simulators. Data obtained from an actual purse seine fishing vessel are applied in developing, validating, and benchmarking models for vessel dynamics, propeller behavior, and hydraulic performance. The models are adaptable and represent a 58-foot fishing vessel, including its propulsion system, hydraulic load, and battery storage capable of operating in both grid-forming and grid-following modes. The testbed is then used to examine integration of a battery energy storage system (BESS): during transit, during fishing operations, and during both transit and fishing operations. The results demonstrate the distinct benefits of both small and large battery installations on fishing vessels, including shorter travel time between the harbor and fishing grounds, stable voltage and frequency across operating modes, and reduced noise during fishing operations.

title: Sensorless Vector Controlled Multi-Induction Motor Drive Using Stator-Current Based Phase-Locked Loop for Pump Application
abstract: Multi-induction motor drive system wherein several induction motors are coupled together mechanically to drive a common load is becoming popular for high-power application. However, speed sensorless operation of such a drive is challenging specially at low operating frequency $(f_{s})$ primarily due to the issues related to flux estimation. This paper proposes a simple technique to improve the sensorless operation of an IM based multi-motor drive system (MMDS) at lower $f_{s}$, specifically for applications such as industrial pumps and fans, where the torque demand from the drive, is low at lower speed. For such loads, atleast one machine in the MMDS may not be required to produce any torque at low $f_{s}$. Since the accuracy of the speed ($\tilde{\omega }_{m}$) estimated using the voltage model of induction machine is poor at low $f_{s}$, the technique proposed here uses the stator current vector $(\overrightarrow{i}_{s})$ of zero torque producing machine to implement a phase-locked loop (PLL) in order to improve its accuracy. As $f_{s}$ increases, accuracy of $\tilde{\omega }_{m}$ improves and beyond a certain value of $f_{s}$, the PLL is no longer required. When that happens, all the motors in the MMDS may contribute to meet the load demand. The proposed technique is computationally less intensive and works satisfactorily upto very low speed of operation. The same is validated through experiments on an MMDS consisting of two 3.7-kW induction motors coupled together to a common shaft.

title: Diode Open-Circuit Fault Detection for Rotating Rectifiers of Brushless Exciters
abstract: The rotating rectifier represents a vulnerable link within the brushless excitation generator and is prone to diode open-circuit faults. A multi-diode fault will lead to significant fluctuations in the generator's excitation current, thereby inducing power oscillations in the unit. Investigating the characteristics and detection approaches of open-circuit diode faults is of great significance. In this study, a typical brushless exciter is taken as an example for examination. First, an analysis is conducted on the diode conduction behavior of the rotating rectifier in the exciter. According to the variations in the air-gap magnetic field of the exciter under normal and single-diode open circuit conditions of the rotating rectifier, it is observed that the fault might introduce fractional harmonics into the air-gap magnetic field. Based on the structural characteristics of the exciter stator and the spillover effect of the main magnetic field, a U-shaped iron core wound with coils is placed in the vicinity of the stator shell to achieve magnetic flux diversion and signal collection. The diode open-circuit fault is identified by the variations in harmonic components of the voltage induced in the coil. Subsequently, a two-dimensional finite element simulation model for a 5.8 MW three-phase brushless exciter is established. A three-phase, 14-pole brushless exciter and a rotating rectifier experimental platform were built for method validation. The results indicate that the induced voltage in the U-shaped core coil can effectively reflect the characteristics of diode open-circuit faults. This method is applicable to the online diagnosis of diode open-circuit faults in brushless exciters, enabling non-invasive detection, reducing the complexity of sensor installation, and exhibiting significant advantages in terms of high convenience and low risk.

title: Real-Time Reactive Power Limits of Synchronous Generators: Application to the New Spanish Voltage Control System
abstract: The voltage control of the Spanish transmission network faces growing challenges due to the high penetration of renewable energy sources, as evidenced by the Iberian Peninsula blackout on April 28, 2025. Synchronous generators have traditionally ensured voltage stability, but their role becomes even more critical in low-inertia systems with limited synchronous generation. This paper presents a real-time method for computing the reactive power limits of synchronous generators at the network connection point, aligned with the new Spanish voltage control system. The proposed approach determines maximum and minimum reactive power capabilities as functions of active power, network voltage, transformer tap position, and key generator constraints, including armature current, excitation system and stability limits, and admissible voltage ranges. Unlike the conventional p–q representation used by manufacturers, European transmission system operators now define reactive power requirements in the q–v plane. The method reflects this shift by computing and displaying reactive limits in the q–v plane to ensure compliance. The approach is validated with a field test of a 213 MVA hydropower plant, and a simulation test of a 450 MVA single-shaft combined-cycle gas turbine, with sensitivity analyses exploring the impact of key parameters on q–v compliance. Time-domain simulations demonstrate how reactive power limits evolve dynamically in response to changing operating conditions, supporting more accurate and robust voltage control in real time.

title: Fault-Tolerant Sensorless Position Estimation for Synchronous Reluctance Motor under Stator Inter-Turn Faults
abstract: Unbalanced phase inductance due to Stator Inter-Turn Faults (SITF) significantly affects the accuracy of sensorless rotor position estimation in Synchronous Reluctance Motors (SynRMs). Traditional sensorless estimation schemes assume balanced inductance and often fail under fault conditions. This paper presents a modified inductance-based position estimation method that accounts for unbalanced inductance variations. The proposed method introduces an Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Inductance Segmentation (AFTIS) approach to identify and compensate for phase inductance deviations. Theoretical analysis is provided to quantify the position estimation error introduced by inductance imbalance. The method is validated through finite element simulations and experimental results on a SynRM prototype, demonstrating significant effectiveness under faulty conditions. The proposed scheme enhances the fault tolerance of sensorless SynRM drives without requiring additional sensors or complex computational resources.

title: Brushless Doubly-Fed Generator With Reconfigured 3Y/3Y Pole-Changing Rotor Winding Using Unequal Turn Coils
abstract: The single winding pole-changing rotor structure can be applied in a brushless doubly-fed generator (BDFG) to couple two magnetic fields produced by stator. However, the traditional scheme employing equal turn coils may result in an asymmetric distribution of the magnetomotive force (MMF) phase angles among the parallel branches within each phase. Through comprehensive circuit analysis, it is further revealed that three branches exhibit distinct characteristics in terms of the slots number and spatial arrangement, leading to unbalanced current amplitudes. The structural asymmetries and current imbalance may significantly enrich magnetic field harmonic contents, amplify electromagnetic vibration and noise, generate parasitic circulating current, and increase copper losses. To address these limitations, an improved scheme with unequal turn coils is developed by reconfiguring the rotor wiring mode. The operational characteristics of BDFG with equal turn, unequal turn, and improved schemes are investigated through finite element (FE). Analysis results imply that the improved scheme significantly reduces the MMF angles discrepancies, ensures balanced current distribution across all branches, and simplifies the circuit connection. Finally, experimental results of a prototype BDFG validate the superior of the proposed scheme.

title: Elimination of Current and Position Sensors in Switched Reluctance Motor Drives Using Direct Sensing of Leaking Flux
abstract: One of the primary challenges in widespread use of Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) drives is the need to monitor rotor position for proper commutation of the stator phases. Additionally, the current magnitude in each phase must be measured and accurately controlled within a specific band. The sensors required to satisfy these functions are bulky, expensive, and prone to errors. Moreover, the position sensor, which is mounted on the shaft of the machine, reduces the compactness of the overall system. Rather than relying on current sensors for control or using complex methods to estimate rotor position, this paper presents a low-cost alternative that directly senses the leakage flux of the stator windings using Hall effect sensors that are mounted axially from the end wings of the stator. Each Hall effect sensor is positioned in front of one of the concentrated end windings of the stator phases. Since the sensed magnetic leakage flux offers a one-to-one correspondence with phase current and position of the rotor, a seamless control of the SRM is possible. The proposed control method is significantly more cost-effective, compact, and robust, enabling the development of a fully integrated inverter for SRMs. Additionally, the proposed method can detect the initial rotor position without requiring any extra devices, thereby providing a reliable startup process. Simulation and experimental results are provided to validate the claims.

title: Design Framework Incorporating Topology Optimization for Halbach Array In-Wheel Motors
abstract: This study presents a design framework incorporating topology optimization developed for Halbach array in-wheel motors. The proposed topology optimization method simultaneously optimizes the complicated features of the Halbach array, including the shape, arrangement, and magnetization directions of permanent magnet (PM) segments, as well as the back-iron shape. The design objective for topology optimization is set as to maximize the average torque, with constraints applied to torque ripple, base speed, and the volumes of PMs and iron materials. Unlike conventional parametric optimization methods, topology optimization enables the exploration of diverse configurations of iron and PM segments without relying on predetermined design settings. Thus, it is employed as a conceptual design tool to identify preliminary configurations and material distributions. This is followed by a detailed design process that refines the conceptual design, ensuring manufacturability and meeting additional performance requirements, ultimately producing CAD models ready for fabrication. The final design is then validated through prototype fabrication and experimental testing. The effectiveness of the proposed design framework integrating topology optimization is demonstrated through its application to Halbach array in-wheel motors.

title: Region-Based Robust Stability Analysis for Droop Coefficients Considering SoC Balance in BESSs
abstract: Although battery energy storage systems (BESSs) are being deployed at scale, droop coefficient tuning remains challenging when these coefficients drift with state of charge (SoC) and charge/discharge modes. Furthermore, accurately characterizing the robust stability region becomes challenging. To address this issue, this paper proposes a region-based robust stability analysis method for droop coefficients to achieve margin-aware selection. Different from existing studies that mainly target stand alone settings, the proposed method explicitly embeds the dynamics of multiagent SoC balancing and incorporates gain and phase margin constraints. First, an improved SoC balancing strategy based on a multiagent system is developed. Its corresponding $dq$-frame small signal state space model for BESS is then established, in which the proposed control dynamics are explicitly incorporated to facilitate subsequent stability analysis. Furthermore, a trapezoid like robust stability region is constructed by introducing gain and phase margins, and its certification is reformulated as a Hurwitz matrix verification problem. In addition, this paper develops a guardian map approach grounded in the bialternate product, enabling efficient boundary construction without iterative numerical tracing. Finally, simulation and experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Advanced Band-Constrained Direct Torque Control Strategy for SPMSM Drive for Torque and Flux Ripple Reduction
abstract: Band-constrained direct torque control (BC-DTC) of surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motors (SPMSMs) is known to maintain the simple control implementation of the conventional DTC with better steady-state torque performance at a relatively low sampling frequency. However, it lacks the theoretical basis for setting the hysteresis band limit that ensures selecting the proper voltage vector under different operating conditions. Also, this selection does not consider the flux control behavior, leading to high stator flux ripple and current distortions. To overcome these issues, this paper presents an advanced BC-DTC strategy with adjustable band limits and adaptive voltage vector selection. The proposed strategy optimizes the switching instant not only to restrict the torque within the hysteresis bounds but also to minimize the torque ripple without increasing the sampling frequency. Experimental evaluations for the proposed and conventional solutions verify the considerable reductions in torque ripple, stator flux ripple, and current distortion.

title: A Novel Digital Twin for Diesel Generator in Microgrids
abstract: Diesel generators (DiGs) play a vital role in Micro grids (MG) to ensure resiliency and reliability; however, accurate modeling of their behavior in both grid-connected and islanded modes is challenging due to limited experimental and manufacturer data. Standard simulation models often fail to capture real world dynamics, leading to inaccurate results. To address these limitations, this paper presents an adaptive digital twin (DT) model for the 62.5kVA DiG unit at the Center for Microgrid Research (CMR). The DT model, capable of grid-connected and islanded operations, is developed and experimentally validated within the CMR's Microgrid infrastructure. The proposed DT leverages a novel adaptive parameter methodology to dynamically reflect the generator's behavior in varying operating conditions for both transient and steady-state responses. The results confirm that the adaptive DT accurately replicates the dynamic response of the real-world industry-grade DiG. The DT offers a robust modeling platform for advanced MG studies that involve DiGs under multiple operation modes.

title: Economic Benefits of Hydrogenerator Rotor Pole Redesign and Field Winding Refurbishment to Accommodate Future Operational Regimes
abstract: Over the last decade, large hydropower plants have shifted their operational regimes from nominal conditions to more diversified load cycles owing to the increasing share of intermittent renewables that have necessitated more flexible hydropower operations. However, increased load variability has made the hydrogenerator efficiency a more important economic metric. This paper proposes a method for redesigning the hydrogenerator rotor pole and refurbishing the field winding to enhance the economic performance. The effectiveness of these changes was evaluated by estimating the levelized cost of non-optimal operation across various operating regimes. We present two alternative rotor redesigns for a 103-MVA hydrogenerator, which indicate significant economic benefits for a diverse set of load cycles. Generally, the net present value of these benefits is found to be four to five times greater than the material costs incurred during the refurbishment phase.

title: Maximum Torque Enhancement Capability for Stator Modular Machines with Single-Tooth- and Multi-Tooth-Wound Modules
abstract: Stator modular machines with torque enhancement capability have attracted broad attention. However, the maximum torque enhancement capability of modular machines with single-tooth- and multi-tooth-wound modules remains unclear. This paper develops an analytical model to quantitatively determine the maximum torque enhancement capability. Two parameters, Ka and Kb, are introduced in this paper to characterize the torque enhancement capability arising from the variation of MMF and the limitation of geometric parameters, respectively. The influence of geometric parameters on torque enhancement capability is analyzed. Analyses show that even with geometric optimization driving Kb toward 1, the torque improvement is fundamentally constrained by Ka. It is further demonstrated that modular machines with multi-tooth-wound modules, i.e., 2 tooth- or 3-tooth-wound in one module (e.g., 18-slot/14-pole and 24-slot/14-pole modular machines), can also improve average torque. Finite-element analysis and prototype experiments validate the proposed model and findings.

title: Structural Dynamics Modeling Method of High-Temperature Superconducting Linear Synchronous Motor Considering the Spatiotemporal Distribution of Electromagnetic Forces
abstract: In this paper, a structural dynamics modeling method for high-temperature superconducting linear synchronous motor (HTS-LSM) is proposed and verified. The proposed model innovatively adopts a blocking method for calculating the electromagnetic loads, which realizes the characterization of electromagnetic loads at different spatial positions and supports the efficient and accurate calculation of the structural dynamic characteristics. The accuracy of the proposed model is verified by comparing the electromagnetic vibration test. The influence mechanism of the block number of the metal components on the superconducting mover magnet structural vibration response is also revealed. The results of this paper could provide important information for modeling and analyzing the structural dynamics characteristics of HTS-LSMs.

title: Torque-based Electromechanical Coupling Analysis for Railway Vibration Energy Harvesting System
abstract: Vibration energy generated during train operations can be harvested to provide a stable power supply for distributed wireless sensor nodes. Existing research has primarily focused on optimizing energy harvesting structures and interface circuits, whereas mechanical damage under prolonged vibration exposure remains underexplored. This study invests the dynamics of the energy harvester to clarify how excitation forces influence structural stability. The irregular nature of track vibrations makes generator torque the primary means of controlling excitation force variations. Therefore, a torque prediction model was established by integrating the operating principles of buck converters. This model accurately forecasts dynamic torque changes based on load variations, thereby enabling the assessment of structural damage induced by load fluctuations. Experimental results show that at 100 r/min and load resistances from 3Ω to 4kΩ, model prediction errors remain below 5%. Additionally, comparative analysis with two types of DC-DC converter validates the model dynamic behavior. Reducing current and adopting high-efficiency converters both contribute to torque optimization. A low-torque current-limiting (LTCL) circuit is designed to mitigate high-torque durations and further validate the accuracy of the proposed model.

title: Uniform Dynamic Control for Nonlinear PV Power Systems via Small-Signal Modeling
abstract: This paper proposes a Uniform Dynamic Control (UDC) strategy to ensure consistent dynamic performance in nonlinear photovoltaic (PV) power systems. Conventional Static Gain Control (SGC), which applies fixed controller parameters, often results in bandwidth variation and undesired transient behavior due to the nonlinear voltage-power characteristics of PV arrays and their sensitivity to irradiance and load variations. These limitations become more critical in single-stage systems, where the lack of energy storage directly couples PV voltage to load dynamics. To address this, a small-signal model is developed to characterize the PV system’s operating-point-dependent behavior and is extended to capture the coupled dynamics between PV voltage and load-side rotor speed in motor-driven applications. Based on this model, UDC adaptively tunes the controller gains to maintain uniform control bandwidth and consistent transient response across a wide range of conditions. Experimental validation confirms that the proposed UDC improves voltage regulation, enhances speed response uniformity, reduces transient deviations and also verifies that the developed small-signal model accurately captures the system’s dynamic behavior.

title: Performance Improvement for Gradient-based Model Predictive Control with Optimized Switching Sequences using Adaptive Control Set Extension
abstract: The superiority of the control set extension in model predictive control (MPC) for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) leads to improved tracking performance of the control objectives in the transportation applications. From a geometric perspective, the extension of the control set can achieve smaller tracking deviations to the reference trajectory, but the improvement is accompanied by the sacrifice of increased switching action changes. To tackle this issue, an adaptive framework of extended control set based on judgment of gradient-based vector is implemented on the MPC scheme, for simultaneous improvement of current quality and switching sequence. Based on the above, a gradient-based formulation of a quadratic programming (QP) MPC problem is put forward. The judgment of relationship between optimal and reference gradient vectors in the consecutive periods is subsequently revealed. In this case, a current gradient-based MPC using consecutive optimal solutions is deployed, in which the tracking error is remarkably reduced without increment of switching changes. When the optimal vector in the former period is opposite to the direction of reference vector, the control set extension is adaptively shifted by applying two optimal vectors of current period in this circumstance. On the contrary, it is considered to avoid increased switching state changes by excluding the control set extension, as the optimal vector in the current sampling period is sufficiently close to the corresponding reference. The proposed adaptive extension framework is intended for the simultaneous enhancement of stator current and switching frequency performance for gradient-based MPC schemes. The proposed scheme is conducted on a 4.8 kW PMSM testbench for experimental verification, which confirms a concurrent optimization of current quality and switching changes in both steady and transient states.

title: A New Hybrid Control Approach for Optimizing Energy Efficiency in Open-End Winding Induction Motors
abstract: Induction motor drives dominate the industry and are among the most energy-intensive systems. Various energy efficiency enhancement strategies have been proposed. Open-End Winding Induction Motors (OEWIMs) with dual inverter topology are gaining popularity in industrial applications such as electric transportation and aeronautics. This paper proposes a new hybrid control approach to optimize the energy efficiency of an OEWIM. The design of the proposed control approach combines: (i) a control law derived from the OEWIM model, which accounts for all losses, (ii) online flux optimization using Loss Minimization Control (LMC) for each operating point (OP), and (iii) torque estimation using the Luenberger observer. The performance and robustness of this approach are demonstrated via simulations and experimentally. The results obtained show a significant improvement in energy efficiency over conventional techniques across a wide range of OPs. This research thus contributes to the advancement of high-efficiency electric drive systems, offering promising prospects for cost-effective industrial applications.

title: Analysis and Calculation of the Control Winding Current During Crowbarless Asymmetrical Low-Voltage Ride-Through for Brushless Doubly-Fed Induction Generators
abstract: The present control winding (CW) current calculations are inaccurate due to the incomplete consideration of the output limitation of the machine side converter (MSC) during the crowbarless asymmetrical low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) of the brushless doubly-fed induction generator (BDFIG). Furthermore, there is a paucity of literature on the relationship between the peak CW currents and the time of the fault occurrence, which has a distinct impact on the analysis and evaluation of the effectiveness of the BDFIG LVRT control strategy. To address this challenge, this paper considers the transient process in the MSC, provides an innovative approximate expression for the CW flux linkage in SVPWM overmodulation, and derives an expression for the CW transient current considering the time of fault occurrence for the first time. From the expression, the CW current of the BDFIG prototype was calculated when the fault occurs at different moments. The calculation results indicate that the peak value of CW is closely related to the time of the fault occurrence and the maximum peak value of the CW current is more than twice the minimum peak value when the fault occurs at different times. Extensive simulation and experimental results under different asymmetrical short-circuit fault have validated the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed expression.

title: Phase-Angle Decoupling and Coordinated Control Strategy for Grid-Connected Inverters in Parallel VSG Systems
abstract: This article establishes a multi-VSG parallel admittance model based on the control foundation of virtual synchronous generator (VSG). First, a detailed study is conducted on the influence of line parameters on the stability and oscillation mechanism of parallel systems, based on existing references. Second, a power-angle compensation control is designed using the equal-area method to enhance transient stability and is supported by power-angle equations that reveal dynamic interactions. Finally, for multi-VSG systems with parameter discrepancies, a phase-angle decoupling coordination strategy is proposed to eliminate cross-coupling in phase angle control loops. This improves regulation accuracy of phase deviations and suppresses transient/steady-state oscillations while optimizing power sharing. This strategy demonstrates superior stability margins over conventional methods after parameter-design via return-difference matrix singular value analysis and stability-verification through generalized Nyquist criterion. Simulations and experiments confirm enhanced dynamic and steady-state performance, addressing the fundamental synchronization issue in parallel systems.

title: Design and Analysis of a High-Power-Density Double-Sided Dual-Magnet Stator-Mover Linear Oscillatory Machine
abstract: Conventional E-type linear oscillatory machine (ELOM) suffers from insufficient utilization of air gap flux density and low power density, which limits their wider adoption. In order to improve the power density, this article proposes an innovative double-sided dual-magnet stator-mover LOM (DSLOM) featuring a composite mover structure of permanent magnet (PM)-iron core-PM and a flux switching topology on the stator side, which can greatly improve the overall output power by enhancing the air gap magnetic flux density. First, the topology and operating principle of the DSLOM are presented. Then, considering the differences between the PM magnetic circuit and the armature magnetic circuit of the proposed machine, two separate equivalent magnetic circuit (EMC) models are established, including a PM EMC accounting for center region saturation and an armature EMC considering slot leakage flux. Moreover, comprehensive design guidelines for the key dimensional parameters are established and analyzed in detail. Finally, simulation and experimental results demonstrate that, compared with the conventional ELOM, the proposed DSLOM achieves a 17.65% improvement in permanent-magnet utilization and a significant increase in output power density, thereby validating the superiority and correctness of the proposed topology.

title: Modeling and Experimental Validation of Flow-Thermal-Coupled Lumped-Parameter Network for Axial-Flux Permanent-Magnet Motor With Oil-Immersed Cooling System
abstract: With the increase of electrical load, the temperature rise in axial flux permanent magnet (AFPM) motor is gradually prominent. Excessive temperature rise directly affects the stable operation of the motor and limits its performance improvement. This article proposes an efficient immersion cooling system for high-torque AFPM motor. Comprehensively considering the cooling oil flow characteristics, oil baffle plates are installed between the end windings and the shell, which improve the cooling oil coverage and enhance the stator heat dissipation capability. Furthermore, flow channels are integrated in the sealing plate, reinforcing the cooling of winding regions with high eddy current losses. Based on computational fluid dynamics (CFD), the thermal analysis of the AFPM motor is carried out. The results show that compared to the conventional oil-immersed cooling structure, the stator core temperature decreases from 67 °C to 52 °C, and the winding temperature declines from 85 °C to 63 °C. Then, the flow network and thermal network are constructed and coupled iteratively to investigate the effect of key parameters on motor thermal performance. Finally, a 850 N·m AFPM motor is manufactured and tested. The experimental data for temperature rise are in good agreement with the proposed calculation method, with a deviation of within 5%.

title: Enhanced Speed Control of SPMSMs via Physics-Informed Neural Network-Based Active Disturbance Rejection Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) strategy enhanced by a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN), designed to compensate for the rotor speed derivative-i.e., speed acceleration, which is typically neglected in conventional ADRC implementations. Owing to the difficulty in accurately measuring speed acceleration and its inherent nonlinear characteristics, the motor's dynamic equations are embedded within the neural network, and automatic differentiation is utilized to estimate acceleration. A physics-guided loss function is constructed to ensure the convergence of the network output. The PINN architecture is specifically designed to address complex nonlinear mappings while operating within the computational constraints of microcontrollers. In comparison with two representative ADRC configurations, the proposed method demonstrates improved dynamic performance. Its effectiveness is experimentally verified on a 1-kW permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive platform.
