title: Investigation of the Flattening Effect on Heat Pipe Thermal Conductivity and Motor Performance
abstract: Heat pipes (HPs) are increasingly applied in electrical machines to improve their cooling effectiveness. Due to spatial constraints within motors, cylindrical HPs are commonly flattened into flat pipes to accommodate confined spaces such as interlayer gaps in windings. This alteration in cross-sectional geometry may reduce HP thermal conductivity and thereby impair motor cooling performance. However, the intrinsic degradation mechanism and flattening effect remain unclear, which could potentially diminish HP cooling benefits in motors. Therefore, this study aims to address the above knowledge gap from both theoretical and experimental sides. Initially, the flattening effect on HP thermal conductivity is quantitatively investigated via analytical modeling and experimental measurements. Further, the impact of flattened HPs on motor additional losses and thermal performance is comprehensively evaluated and verified. Finally, practical guidelines for the application of flattened HPs in electrical machines are proposed considering requirements for high efficiency and high power density.

title: Current Ripple Suppression for PMSM Predictive Control System Under DC-Link Voltage Fluctuation
abstract: In permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive systems, DC-link voltage fluctuations can severely affect the steady-state performance of the system. Although traditional model-free predictive current control (MF-PCC) can enhance system robustness and reduce the impact of current harmonics, its current harmonics caused by DC-link voltage fluctuations can not be suppressed effectively. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a current ripple suppression predictive current control strategy based on a dual second-order generalized integrator (DSOGI). This strategy utilizes the DSOGI to extract fluctuation signals from the current signals that have the same frequency as the DC-link voltage fluctuations, achieving dynamic reverse compensation of the current ripple. Additionally, to address the signal delay issue associated with the DSOGI algorithm, the Lagrange interpolation method is employed to predict the signal and, in doing so, the compensation accuracy is improved. The experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared to traditional methods, the proposed approach effectively reduces current ripple caused by DC-link voltage fluctuations and enhances the control system robustness.

title: Transient Stability of GFL Converters Subjected to Switching of Droop-Controlled GFM Converters
abstract: Integrating grid-forming converters (GFMCs) into grid-following converter (GFLC)-dominated power systems enhances the grid strength, but GFMCs' current-limiting characteristic triggers dynamic mode switching between constant voltage control (CVC) and current limit control (CLC). This switching feature poses critical transient stability risks to GFLCs, requiring urgent investigation. This paper first develops a mathematical model for this switched system. Then, it derives mode switching conditions for droop-controlled GFMCs, which are separately GFMC angle-dependent and GFLC angle-dependent. On this basis, the stability boundaries of GFLC within each subsystem are analyzed, and the impact of GFMC mode switching arising from GFLC angle oscillation is investigated. The findings reveal that the switched system's stability boundary coincides with that of the CLC subsystem. To enhance GFLC's transient stability and ensure GFMC converges to the CVC mode, this paper introduces a virtual fixed d-axis control (VFDC) strategy. Compared with existing methods, this method achieves decoupling and self-stabilization using only local state variables from individual converters. The conclusions are validated through simulations and Controller Hardware-in-the-Loop tests.

title: Contouring Control of Three-Linear-Motors-Driven Gantry System via an Adaptive Fast Terminal Synergetic Controller under Dynamic Load Conditions
abstract: High-precision contouring control for the three-linear-motors-driven gantry system (TLMDGS) is a fundamental requirement in advanced manufacturing. Most existing contouring control methods focus on static load conditions, while dynamic load scenarios involving sudden load changes or time-varying loads often lead to severe deterioration in contouring accuracy. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel adaptive fast terminal synergetic control (AFTSC) framework. Built upon synergetic control theory, the proposed approach inherently eliminates the chattering commonly observed in conventional robust methods while ensuring finite-time error convergence. To resolve the singularity problem in traditional terminal-type synergetic controllers, a redesigned macro variable is developed, which guarantees smooth control input and enhances contouring tracking accuracy under dynamic load conditions. Furthermore, a concise integrated contouring error model that explicitly incorporates synchronization performance is established. Compared to existing contouring error models for TLMDGS, the proposed model significantly alleviates the computational burden by avoiding intensive matrix operations and iterative solutions. Finally, drag experiments on a dual-TLMDGS platform are conducted to validate the effectiveness and demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method.

title: Scale-Decreasing Surrogate Modeling for Low-Deviation Optimization of Axial Flux Motors Considering Parameter Coupling
abstract: In this article, the reduced order model (ROM) assisted iterative scale-decreasing two-tier surrogate method is proposed for multi-objective optimization (MOO) of axial flux motors (AFMs). It can consider parameter interaction and realize a low-level deviation during the optimization process. Firstly, the ROM is applied to construct an accurate dataset for surrogate training. Subsequently, the two-tier surrogate is employed to accelerate the MOO process effectively. The first-tier surrogate model is trained using data generated from the ROM, enabling the construction of a rapid optimization framework. Next, a second-tier scale-decreasing surrogate model is established. This second-tier model improves the approximation precision with a more comprehensive and refined sampling space after considering the parameter coupling effect. Therefore, based on the studied machine, the proposed method achieves: (1) Reduction of the optimal set deviation error from ∼2% to ∼0.2% compared to the conventional surrogate method, with finite element method (FEM)-based optimization as the benchmark. (2) Significantly saves the computational burden compared with the high-fidelity FEM. Ultimately, the effectiveness of the scale-decreasing two-tier surrogate method is validated through FEM and experiments. The optimal design demonstrates that, compared to the conventional method, the proposed method achieves improved optimization accuracy, which further validates its potential for advanced motor design and optimization applications.

title: A Multidisciplinary Approach to the Geometrical Design of Axial Active Magnetic Bearings- Part II: Results and Validation
abstract: This paper presents the application of the design method introduced in Part I. Design of an axial active magnetic bearing (AMB) is implemented as part of a novel heat pump compressor design. The case study highlights the importance of integrating various design areas to streamline the overall design process. All results are produced exclusively through the design process and methodology outlined in Part I. The study presents geometries for two thrust bearing configurations in relation to the shaft diameter, highlighting the multidisciplinary nature of the design through a sensitivity analysis. Analytical calculation results are compared with finite element simulations, not only to validate the accuracy of the design, but also to generate data that can refine the design details. The key outcome of this study is not the precise design itself, but the clear improvement in the design process efficiency, resulting in a methodology where the bearing design lead time is measured in days rather than weeks or months. Although, not all steps in the design process are entirely accurate and could be further improved, the design method allows easy modification, illustrating the interactions between parameters in this multidisciplinary process.

title: Two-Level FEM-Based Inductance Modeling for Real-Time Simulation of Bar Breakages in Squirrel Cage Induction Machines
abstract: This paper presents an innovative two-level modeling approach for accurately simulating the inductance matrix of induction machines (IMs) under fault conditions. The first level uses Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations to extract the inductance matrix $L(\theta)$ of the healthy machine, achieving high spatial resolution with minimal computational resources. The second level enables the introduction of rotor asymmetry faults using tensor algebra, thus eliminating the need for repeated FEM simulations. This approach enhances the efficiency of fault simulations, making it suitable for real-time diagnostic applications. The model is validated through both steady-state and transient analysis, demonstrating its effectiveness in reproducing fault-related harmonics and offering significant improvements in computational performance compared to traditional time-stepping FEM models.

title: Split-Yoke Axial-Flux PM Machine With Ultra-Low Rotor Inertia for Enhanced Servo Dynamic Performance
abstract: This article introduces a novel axial-flux permanent magnet motor (AFPM) topology for servo applications. Although many papers focus on the good torque generation capability of dual rotor AFPM, the large rotor inertia is not ideal in servo drives. By increasing torque generation and reducing rotor inertia, motion control response can be improved. This article introduces a new AFPM topology with a split rotor yoke, which is simply a rolled steel plate fixed to the front cover of the machine. With this special and simple component, rotor inertia can be significantly reduced, and the manufacturing process is as simple as a regular single-rotor AFPM because there is only one winding stator. In this topology, the rotor is only composed of magnets and some structural components, thus exhibiting a very light rotor inertia. This article explains how to construct the rotor structure for a better motion performance and discusses design details. A prototype with this proposed structure was fabricated. Experimental verification includes the steady-state performance, motion response, and energy- conservation effect evaluation.

title: Suppression of Periodic Speed Fluctuations for PMSM Using Improved Gradient Descent Algorithm
abstract: An AC disturbance suppression method for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drives is proposed on the basis of a mathematical optimization algorithm. First, the AC disturbances of the system were equivalently moved to the controller input point (error feedback) according to the principle of shifting the introduction point of in a control flow diagram. Thus, additional harmonics with appropriate amplitudes and phase angles can be injected at this point to compensate for the effects of the AC disturbances. Second, a two-dimensional optimization method based on the gradient descent algorithm (GDA) was designed to obtain the injected harmonics with the optimal amplitude and phase angle. Furthermore, a reasonable evaluation function was designed to prevent the GDA from falling into a local optimum. Third, the iteration of the amplitude and phase angle was improved according to the evaluation function so that the two are approximately decoupled. This avoids the derivative calculations required by the traditional GDA and provides a better balance between the convergence speed and the accuracy. The method for selecting the initial value of the GDA iteration is also given, and the parameter robustness of the proposed GDA was analyzed. Finally, experimental validation was performed.

title: Design of Sensorless Bearingless Motors for Displacement Estimation Using Mutual Inductance
abstract: Bearingless motors can produce electromagnetic torque and force using a single machine. The forces are often used to actively levitate the rotor which requires high-bandwidth displacement sensor feedback. These sensors add undesired cost, bulk, and cabling to the drive system. To mitigate these issues, the motor itself can be used as the rotor displacement sensor in a “sensorless” or “self-sensing” approach. Based on electromagnetic variation due to rotor eccentricity, real-time self-sensing control algorithms can generate estimates of rotor displacement which can be used for levitation feedback signals. This work proposes a framework for motor design specifically to optimize for self-sensing capability. The main goal is to understand and maximize the displacement self-sensing sensitivity and linearity. A multi-objective optimization is used to explore the design space and quantify performance trade-offs in power conversion, force actuation, and self-sensing. Leveraging the optimization results, a prototype sensorless bearingless motor is fabricated and tested. Its eccentric-rotor inductance is measured statically versus frequency and rotor angle, showing less than 10% mutual inductance ripple. Real-time online self-sensing results are provided which demonstrate 15 µm resolution displacement estimates at 800 Hz bandwidth during transient motion.

title: Performance-Enhanced Adaptive Finite-Time Accurate Control of Uncertain Hydro Turbine Governing System with External Disturbances
abstract: The hydro turbine governing system (HTGS) plays a critical role in ensuring the overall stability and safe operation of hydropower stations. However, in the hydro turbine governing system, the rotor speed of the generator is the key factor affecting its performance. This paper proposes a finite time sliding mode control scheme aimed at achieving the accurate trajectory tracking of rotor speed to enhance the performance of the HTGS. To overcome the influence of external disturbances, a novel finite-time disturbance observer (FDO) is proposed. Unlike conventional high-order sliding-mode observers, the proposed FDO features a fully decoupled architecture that allows offline observer design and gain tuning independently of the controller synthesis. It requires only first-order differentiability of the lumped disturbances, and its estimation errors converge to zero strictly in finite time. This decoupled design enables exact trajectory tracking with stronger disturbance rejection, faster transient response, and lower online computational cost. Finally, a suite of extensive simulation outcomes is provided, which demonstrates the efficacy of the newly proposed control strategy. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves exact disturbance estimation within 1.2–1.5 s and drives the rotor speed tracking error to zero in 1.8–2.3 s, substantiating the finite-time convergence claim with quantitative metrics.

title: Equivalence of Grid-Tied Inverters Operating in the Grid-Following and Grid-Forming Modes Just Through Adapting the Control Parameters
abstract: With the continuous growth of renewable energy capacity, power electronic inverters have been widely deployed in power grids, and their total capacity has surpassed that of conventional synchronous generators. To maintain the stability of the power system, some inverters are operated in the grid-forming mode (GFM) instead of the conventional grid-following mode (GFL) mainly through switching over the synchronization schemes. In the GFL mode, the synchronous angle is generated by the phase-locked loop (PLL) scheme, while in the GFM mode, it is achieved through the power synchronization control (PSC). Generally, the GFL mode exhibits better adaptability to strong grid, whereas the GFM mode is more stable to weak grid. However, the specific boundary between these two modes remains ambiguous and varies with control parameters, which poses challenges both to the selection of operation modes and to parameter design for specific grid conditions. Unifying these two operation modes is crucial to dig out of this dilemma. Against this background, the small-signal dynamic performance equivalence between the GFL and GFM modes is established just through adapting control parameters properly, without the need for switching between synchronous schemes. As a result, the characteristics of the inverters adapt to grid strength continuously.

title: Maximum Torque per Ampere-Based Direct Torque Control of Five-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Under Open-Circuit Fault
abstract: Conventional direct torque control (DTC) with constant reference stator flux leads to inefficiency in permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs), since the optimal reference stator flux varies with load conditions and non-optimal values result in larger currents. This paper proposes a novel DTC strategy based on virtual square-wave injection (VSWI-DTC) to achieve maximum-torque-per-ampere (MTPA) operation and maintain high dynamic performance of five-phase PMSM under open-circuit fault. The novelty lies in detecting the optimal stator flux through virtual square-wave injection into the m-axis flux, integrated with a fault-tolerant transformation matrix to achieve enhanced MTPA-based DTC. Unified decoupled models are derived in the stator-flux reference frame for both healthy and fault conditions, in which the m-axis flux equals the stator flux amplitude. Based on the derived relationship between stator current and flux, the optimal m-axis flux is obtained online under varying operating conditions. Synergized with deadbeat-based DTC, the proposed strategy minimizes copper loss, enhances efficiency, and suppresses torque fluctuations caused by open-circuit fault. Furthermore, since no filters are required, the fast dynamic response of DTC is preserved. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

title: Sensorless Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Using Model Predictive Algorithm Based Back-EMF Observer
abstract: Back-electromotive force (back-EMF) based sensorless control is widely applied in permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drives. For high-gain back-EMF observers, the control law often leads to an inherent trade-off between steady-state accuracy and dynamic response. To address this issue, a model predictive control (MPC)-based observer designed in discrete-time domain is proposed in this article. In the studied observer, the optimal control action selected from a predetermined set is adopted to eliminate the current estimation error. Then, the estimated back-EMFs can be extracted from the applied control actions. By leveraging traversing optimization, the proposed method improves the current error and observation accuracy while maintaining fast response and robustness. Experimental results conducted on a 1-kW PMSM platform verify the effectiveness of the proposed observer.

title: Rotor Built-In Flux Barriers for Improving the Power Quality of Aircraft Wound Rotor Synchronous Generators
abstract: Improving terminal-voltage power quality under balanced and unbalanced loading is critical for high-reliability aircraft wound-rotor synchronous generators (WRSGs). This paper proposes a flux-path-guided systematic design methodology using built-in rotor flux barriers to enhance power quality without additional filtering hardware. By establishing a unified analytical link between rotor reluctance shaping and magnetic field behavior, the average tangential air-gap flux density (Btavg) is identified as a robust indicator for cross-magnetization induced harmonics, while negative-sequence d/q-axis permeances are shown to govern phase-voltage asymmetry. Sensitivity analysis reveals that radial barrier dimensions are the primary levers for mitigating voltage unbalance (ΔU) and phase displacement (ΔP), whereas tangential dimensions predominantly influence harmonic distortion (THD). To balance power-quality gains against fundamental-voltage retention, a Pareto-front-based knee-point selection strategy is employed. Structural finite-element (FE) analysis further verifies mechanical integrity at 1.2 × rated speed. Experimental validation on a prototype generator at 9000 r/min confirms that the selected design reduces ΔU from 7.29% to 4.21% and ΔP from 13.80° to 8.77° under extreme unbalance, while decreasing THD from 2.54% to 2.01%, with a marginal voltage penalty of less than 3%. The consistent effectiveness across various power factors and load unbalance degrees demonstrates that strategic rotor reluctance shaping provides a robust, mass efficient solution for airborne power systems.

title: A Non-Axisymmetric Winding-Based Sliding Mode Position Observer for Dual Three-Phase Permanent Magnet Motor Under Single Phase Open-Circuit Fault
abstract: After a single phase open-circuit fault occurs in dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor, the remaining healthy windings form a group of non-axisymmetric five-phase winding, which makes it difficult to estimate the position information accurately while performing the sensorless control scheme. For addressing the issue, a sliding mode position observer designed according to the non-axisymmetric winding is proposes in this paper. Twice decoupling operations were carried out on the main inductance matrix, the resistance matrix and the leakage inductance matrix, then the decoupled voltage equation of the non-axisymmetric five-phase winding is derived. For suppressing the fluctuations of the back-EMFs caused by the asymmetric inductance matrix, a nonlinear restoring-force coefficient sigmoid (RF-Sigmoid) is proposed to reduce the chattering of the estimated back-EMF. In addition, the stability analysis of the non-axisymmetric winding-based sliding mode position observer is also provided. The experimental and simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Multivariate Sensitivity Analysis of Electric Machine Efficiency Maps and Profiles Under Design Uncertainty
abstract: This work introduces the use of multivariate global sensitivity analysis for assessing the impact of uncertain electric machine design parameters on efficiency maps and profiles. Contrary to the common approach of applying variance-based (Sobol') sensitivity analysis elementwise, multivariate sensitivity analysis provides a single sensitivity index per parameter, thus allowing for a holistic estimation of parameter importance over the full efficiency map or profile. Its benefits are demonstrated on permanent magnet synchronous machine models of different fidelity. Computations based on Monte Carlo sampling and polynomial chaos expansions are compared in terms of computational cost. The sensitivity analysis results are subsequently used to simplify the models, by fixing non-influential parameters to their nominal values and allowing random variations only for influential parameters. Uncertainty estimates obtained with the full and reduced models confirm the validity of model simplification guided by multivariate sensitivity analysis.

title: Electromagnetic Design Algorithm for Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: The interest in axial flux machines has grown in recent years because of their high power density. Considering their geometry, 3D or quasi-3D Finite Element (FE) models are necessary to simulate their behavior: the analysis of such models is time-consuming, and the iterations needed to derive the finaldesign may require long computation times. This paper describes a fast design procedure for axial fluxPermanent Magnet (PM) machines based on simple closed expressions relating the main electromagnetic quantities to geometric parameters. Starting from the commonly used design constraints, the model derives, in about 0.4 s, the airgap magnetic flux density produced by the PMs, the value of the ampere-turns needed to develop the requested torque, the main geometric machine dimensions (i.e., rotor yoke, teeth geometry, PMs shape), and the efficiency. FE simulations of the obtained configuration have been performed to verify the effectiveness of the analytical model, assessing that the initial specifications are respected. Furthermore, a prototype was built and tested. The measured values of the no-load airgap magnetic flux density, induced voltages, developed torque, and efficiency were compared to the ones estimated by the proposed model, highlighting the good consistency between the analytical, FE, and experimental results.

title: Active Learning-Based Multiobjective Optimization of Electric Machines Using Probabilistic Metamodeling
abstract: While the data-driven optimization of electric machines shows promise, real-world applications still face challenges, including time-consuming data collection and reduced prediction reliability with limited data. To this end, this article first conducts a comparative study of five probabilistic metamodels (MMs) and one deterministic MM. With the help of predictions and uncertainty information, four iterative optimization strategies based on active learning are proposed. In each iteration, a quantity of key data is selected and added to the initial small dataset. The MMs are continually updated with the augmented dataset to obtain more accurate prediction capabilities. The results show that the proposed strategies can significantly enhance the forecast accuracy of the optimal designs in the case of limited data. Furthermore, using predictive uncertainty greatly reduces the overall computational burden for the entire optimization process.

title: Impact of d-axis Current on a Passively Levitated Self-Bearing PM Machines Considering Nonlinear Electrodynamic and Reluctant Effects
abstract: Self-bearing machines use rotor magnetic levitation to suppress friction and reach high rotation speeds. Recent studies have considered the integration of electrodynamic suspension in permanent magnet self-bearing machines in order to achieve fully passive levitation, improving the compactness and reliability. However, the influence of the d-axis current injected by the power supply on the dynamic behavior has not been addressed so far, as previous models were based on hypotheses that resulted in axial force and torque being independent of this current component. This paper develops an electromechanical model of an electrodynamic thrust self-bearing machine that accounts for the reluctant effects, both axial and angular, and the nonlinear evolution of magnetic flux linkage, revealing an impact of the d-axis current. Based on this model, quasi-static expressions of the suspension currents and the electromagnetic forces are derived and analyzed. A prototype is then tested in various conditions to compare model predictions with measurements. The results demonstrate that d-axis current injection can modulate the suspension force, even at zero speed.

title: Design and Construction of Permanent Magnet Linear Generator for Small-Scale Surface-Riding Wave Energy Converters
abstract: Wave energy converters (WEC) convert the energy from ocean waves into electricity. The surface-riding wave energy converter (SR-WEC) is a type of WEC that uses adaptive resonance to overcome the challenges faced by point absorber WECs. SR-WEC operates by using movable masses in the floating structure to adaptively change its natural frequency to match the incoming waves. The energy is captured using pitch motion of the SR-WEC. A tubular permanent magnet linear generator (PMLG) is used the energy from this pitch motion and convert it into electrical energy. The PMLG consists of a tubular stator on the outside and a moving permanent magnet translator inside. This work describes the development of a PMLG rated for 300N of power take-off force for use in a small-scale SR-WEC system. The design trends are illustrated through parametric two-dimensional finite element simulations results. Important practical design considerations of the prototype have also been discussed. Experimental analysis on the prototype design show that a good agreement between the simulated and measured values back EMF and phase currents of the PMLG. An actuated testbed was used to validate the performance of the PMLG. This work helps establish the proof of concept of PMLG designs for use in SR-WEC systems.

title: Analysis of Stator-Controlled Doubly-Fed Induction Wind Generator for Fractional Frequency Transmission System
abstract: In this paper, a stator-controlled doubly-fed induction wind generator (SC-DFIG) designed for fractional frequency transmission system (FFTS) is presented. To accommodate the low-frequency voltage of the FFTS, the SC-DFIG connects the rotor winding directly to the grid, while the stator winding is linked through a back-to-back AC/AC converter. The system topology and unique operating principles of this innovative winding and control scheme are thoroughly analyzed, along with the mathematical model of the SC-DFIG. Based on theoretical analysis, the effectiveness and feasibility of the stator-controlled scheme are verified through multi-condition simulations and prototype experiments. Contrary to traditional rotor-controlled doubly-fed induction generator (RC-DFIG), this novel stator-controlled fractional frequency generator features a constant-frequency rotor and a variable-frequency stator. The proposed system maintains high-speed operation even at low frequencies, delivers excellent electromagnetic performance, and achieves low per-unit power cost for whole generator system.

title: Armature Motion Characteristics of Electromagnetic Propulsion Devices Considering Dynamic Armature Conductivity
abstract: In electromagnetic propulsion devices (EPD), the equivalent armature conductivity varies dynamically with bulk conductivity and contact resistance, which directly affects the motion characteristics of devices. However, under extreme electromagnetic, thermal, and force shock conditions, real-time in-situ measurement of armature conductivity remains challenging. To improve the computational accuracy of numerical models, this paper proposes a method for analyzing the motion characteristics of EPD based on dynamic armature conductivity inversion. First, real-time armature velocity and spatial magnetic field information at measurement points are obtained through electromagnetic propulsion experiments. Subsequently, a dynamic armature conductivity inversion model is developed by integrating deep neural networks (DNN) with an improved gradient descent method (DGD). This model utilizes the measured magnetic flux density to correct the computed values of the parameterized model, thereby obtaining spatiotemporal characteristics of armature conductivity. Next, a transient electromagnetic, thermal, and force coupling finite element model of the armature-rail is developed based on the inversion results, enabling the analysis of the impact of dynamic armature conductivity on the device’s motion characteristics. Finally, experimental validation shows that the method considering dynamic armature conductivity significantly improves the computational accuracy of the finite element model. This work provides theoretical support for further reliability prediction and structural optimization design of EPD. It also offers new solutions for real-time in-situ measurement of material properties under extreme conditions.

title: Multi-Objective Optimization of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Considering Electromagnetic-Structural Coupling
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-objective optimization method based on electromagnetic-structural coupling for permanent magnet synchronous motor. The proposed method is aimed at simultaneously meeting the electromagnetic and structural performance requirements of aerospace motors. An analytical model is established for the strength and stiffness of each component in a permanent magnet synchronous motor. The analytical model is combined with the electromagnetic finite element model. A multi-objective genetic algorithm is used for the coupled electromagnetic-structural optimization. This method ensures high torque density, high efficiency, and high mechanical reliability. The optimized motor can withstand three times the mechanical overload, achieving 94.5% efficiency and a torque density of 8.2 N·m/kg. Finally, a prototype is manufactured and experiments are conducted to validate both the theoretical analysis and the proposed optimization method.

title: An Analytical Computational Model for Bearingless Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Based on Distributed Magnetic Circuit Method
abstract: Bearingless permanent magnet synchronous motors (BPMSMs) demonstrate considerable potential for application in high-speed and high-power-density scenarios. However, their electromagnetic characteristics and design methods are comparatively more complex than those of traditional motors. The intricate nonlinear saturation within the motor and the multi-source excitation nature of the magnetic field present substantial challenges to the accurate modeling of BPMSMs. To enable efficient and precise computation of BPMSMs, this paper proposes an analytical model for the electromagnetic performance of BPMSMs that combines the distributed magnetic circuit method (DMCM) with the airgap relative permeance. This approach not only accounts for magnetic field coupling and core material saturation effects via iterative correlation of multiple magnetic circuits but also characterizes the spatiotemporal variation features of multi-source excitation, cogging effects, and asymmetric magnetic field distributions induced by rotor eccentricity through time-step calculations and relative permeability. The effectiveness of the method is finally verified using the finite element method (FEM) and experiments. In comparison with the FEM, the error in calculating the no-load air gap magnetic flux density using this method is within 0.01T. When evaluated against experimental results, the error in calculating the no-load back Electromotive force is within 2.5%, and the error in calculating the radial suspension force is within 5%.

title: Additively Manufactured Spoke-Type Permanent Magnet Rotors: Solutions to Multidisciplinary Design Challenges and Comparison With Traditional Design
abstract: Sustainability in electrical machines demands minimizing material waste, eliminating rare-earth permanent magnets (PMs), and improving efficiency and reliability. Additive manufacturing (AM) offers a promising pathway toward these goals by enabling near-zero material waste, streamlined production, and enhanced design freedom. This study leverages the compatibility of spoke-type rotor configurations with non-rare-earth PMs and the unique advantages of AM to achieve a highly sustainable design. The paper proposes innovative solutions to address the existing challenges of using AM for developing ferrite PM rotor topologies and provides a comprehensive comparison with traditional laminated topology. A novel technique is presented, reducing torque ripple from 42% to 16%, and voltage THD from 11% to 5%. The proposed solution not only maintains the average torque but also avoids added manufacturing complexity and cost, unlike skewing techniques. Moreover, a new grooving technique is implemented, reducing the eddy current loss in the bulk rotor by more than 40%. A spoke-type design with open bridges is selected over the closed-bridge design, and a comprehensive multidisciplinary analysis is conducted. Two spoke-type rotors are 3D printed, and one traditional laminated rotor is manufactured. The experimental comparisons show that the proposed 3D printed rotors outperform the laminated design in terms of torque ripple, voltage THD, and material usage, while offering comparable power rating and back-emf.

title: Proof of Concept of a Two-Phase Thermal Management System for Railway Traction Motors
abstract: The paper proposes the implementation of a loop thermosiphon (LTS) as a potential thermal management system to replace the conventional forced-air cooling system in railway traction motors. This aims to address issues such as reducing motor sizes and maintenance costs. The LTS, identified as a two-phase passive cooling system with high thermal conductance, has not been widely used in electric motors. The experimental investigation of the LTS performance in various positions aims to provide comprehensive insights into the impact of different orientations on the LTS system and its heat transfer capabilities. The LTS setup, designed at a 1/12 of the electric motor housing, was tested in different inclinations with a heat load of 470 W. The system’s performance in each position was evaluated based on predefined criteria. The findings indicate that the LTS system did not operate in two positions, but in other orientations, it demonstrated overall satisfactory performance.

title: Air-Gap Eccentricity Detection in Symmetrical Six-Phase Induction Motor Drives With Model Predictive Control
abstract: Fault diagnostics in induction motors drives with closed-loop controls have been particularly challenging, predominantly due to the mitigating effect of the controller actions on fault symptoms. This paper presents a new fault diagnostic technique, to detect mixed air-gap eccentricity in symmetrical six-phase induction motor drives, based on the spectrum analysis of a non-integer harmonic component presented in the αβ-plane stator current modulus. This online approach, able to perform the fault diagnostic in motors driven by a model predictive control, relies on the evaluation of a non-integer harmonic component resultant from the interaction between a time harmonic of the stator magnetic flux and the rotor slot harmonics. Experimental results, including different load torques and fault severities, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed technique in detecting and evaluating the fault.

title: Short-Circuit Current and Torque Output Analysis of Multi-Phase Permanent Magnet Machine With Compound Magnet Array
abstract: Multi-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is especially useful for aerospace engineering due to its winding redundancy and high-power density etc. One major challenge for dual three-phase PMSM is to reduce the short-circuit current while maintaining high torque generation. Traditional solutions usually suppress the short-circuit current by increasing winding leakage inductance through stator slot design, which not only compromises the depression of short-circuit current, but also reduces the torque output of electric machines. Therefore, the objective of this study is to propose a novel short-circuit current suppression method by applying compound magnet array. The compound magnet array can reduce the short-circuit current and maintain the high torque output of electric machine well. Analytical, numerical and experimental approaches are carried out to verify the proposed system design concept. Initially, the schematic structures of the dual three-phase PMSM and the magnet array are introduced. Subsequently, the magnetic field, torque and short-circuit current are derived through analytical formulations. These results are then validated through numerical simulations to confirm the accuracy of the analytical formulations. The torque performance and short-circuit current of the compound magnet array are evaluated in comparison to other common magnet configurations and traditional short-circuit suppression techniques. Following that, a research prototype of a dual three-phase PMSM and experimental test platforms are constructed. A series of experiments are carried out, focusing on the magnetic field, torque output, and short-circuit current. The experimental findings effectively validate both the analytical models and the proposed system design.

title: Comprehensive Optimization of RPMFS Motors Considering Variable Numbers of Slots and Poles
abstract: A new method is proposed for optimized design of rotor permanent magnet flux switching motors with high specific torque and low torque ripple. Slot and pole numbers are treated as independent optimization variables during the design process, alongside magnetic core dimensions to enable a fair comparison between machines having different slot/pole combinations and pole ratios, including Vernier machines. The method includes procedures for automated generation of the finite element model, winding distribution in slots and the end-winding arrangement for each machine based on its slot/pole combination. Since the level of the steel degradation due to punching and cutting differs significantly with slot and pole numbers, corresponding magnetic properties are adjusted for each machine. The proposed method ology also includes an algorithm for estimating and increasing the slot filling factor of all machines on each generation of the optimization procedure, providing an additional mechanism for increasing specific torque. As such, the proposed approach significantly reduces the amount of empirical input data, widens the optimization search domain and avoids suboptimal designs. Ac curacy of employed models and practical applicability of the developed method are experimentally verified on a 1.3 kW motor with an optimized slot/pole combination of 24 slots and 26 poles.

title: Radial-Electromagnetic-Force and Vibration Analysis of Hybrid-Excitation Doubly-Salient Machine
abstract: Hybrid excitation doubly salient machine (HEDSM) has been considered to have good application prospects in electric vehicles and aerospace due to its advantage of high power density. However, HEDSM suffers from serious vibration because of the doubly salient poles structure. Therefore, a detailed analysis of the electromagnetic force and vibration characteristics of HEDSM is presented. Firstly, the spatial distribution and frequency characteristics of the radial electromagnetic force acting on the stator tooth surface are derived analytically and validated using two-dimensional fast Fourier transform (FFT-2D). Furthermore, a comparison is made between the natural frequency and modal shape of the single stator core and the composite stator core which contains windings and permanent magnets (PMs). A multiphysics model is established to calculate the vibration of the HEDSM. Through the mode superposition method, the vibration acceleration on the motor surface under the rated operating conditions is computed. Finally, an 18/11 pole HEDSM prototype is fabricated. Experimental measurements of the natural frequency of the assembled stator core and the vibration acceleration are conducted, demonstrating good agreement with the theoretical analysis and simulation results.

title: A Novel Battery Electrochemical Impedance Spectrum Measuring Method in Cascaded Energy Storage Systems
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) enables critical battery state estimation, yet conventional techniques require idle-time harmonic injection, distorting grid waveforms during operation and precluding real-time monitoring. To resolve this limitation, this paper proposes a novel current modulation method for online EIS measurement in cascaded energy storage systems (CHB-BESS). By exploiting the time-frequency duality principle (where time-domain multiplication corresponds to frequency-domain convolution), the proposed method generates target excitation frequencies through real-time current modulation in energy storage converter legs. This approach seamlessly integrates with the nearest level modulation (NLM) strategy of cascaded H-bridge systems, enabling online EIS measuring during normal operation – all while eliminating operational disruption and maintaining grid-side waveform integrity. Validation in MATLAB/Simulink and a down-scaled H-bridge prototype confirms the feasibility of the proposed method, demonstrating disturbance-free operation during normal system functioning while achieving multi-frequency EIS measurements with a mean average percentage error (MAPE) below 2.53%.

title: Topology Optimization for Generating Optimal Free-Form Rotor Structures in PMSMs
abstract: To achieve high performance in the rotor design of permanent magnet synchronous motors(PMSMs), it is essential to optimally arrange materials and magnetic flux paths from a structural design perspective. This paper proposes a multi-material topology optimization(MMTO)approach, based on the Solid Isotropic Material with Penalization(SIMP)method, to automatically generate optimal PMSM rotor structures with high design freedom. The proposed method employs a multi-material interpolation technique to represent the spatial distribution of ferromagnetic materials, permanent magnets (PMs), and air, while comprehensively considering electromagnetic and mechanical performance. In addition, the magnetization and current angles are independently optimized to maximize output performance. An optimization framework is established using the Augmented Lagrangian method, with sensitivities of the design variables derived. A variable filter-radius strategy is introduced to ensure effective convergence of the optimization process. Compared with classical parameter optimization based on heuristic methods, the proposed method achieves superior PMSM designs. Experimental validation confirms its effectiveness.

title: Speed-Sensorless Control of Pole Transition for Variable Phase-Pole Induction Machines
abstract: Variable phase-pole induction machines appear to offer the potential for use in electromobility applications due to their capability of electronically changing the number of magnetic poles, thus extending the torque-speed operation of the machine. This work presents a model reference adaptive system solution for the sensorless speed operation of a nine-phase variable phase-pole induction machine. The same adaptive full-order observer is used to estimate the mechanical speed in two different ways, one for each pole pair configuration of interest. The sensorless operation of the drive is maintained during the pole-pair configuration change with a suitable transition between the two speed-estimation laws, guaranteeing precise rotor flux linkage information for achieving high-performance control. The simulation and experimental results of the proposed method demonstrate a high degree of agreement, indicating the effectiveness of the proposed sensorless methodology under varying load conditions and positive/negative speed transitions.

title: Sensorless Control of Dual Three-Phase IPMSM With High-Frequency Pulsating Voltage Injection in Harmonic Sub-Space in the Low-Speed Region
abstract: According to the vector space decomposition (VSD) theory, the variables of dual three-phase interior permanent magnet synchronous machine (DTP-IPMSM) in cartesian coordinates can be converted to the mutually orthogonal fundamental sub-space (FSS) and harmonic sub-space (HSS). The high-frequency (HF) pulsating voltage injection method based on the saliency of the HSS for the sensorless control of DTP-IPMSM in low-speed region is proposed in this paper. As the FSS and HSS are decoupled, no additional filters are required for the current feedback loop in the FSS no matter what kind of HF signals are employed. Therefore, the dynamic performance of the control system can be enhanced. Meanwhile, the proposed method can reduce the HF torque ripple significantly in theory, which is also verified by the measured torque results. Finally, experiments are conducted on a prototype DTP-IPMSM platform to validate its feasibility and effectiveness.

title: Phase-Locked Principal Component Analysis
abstract: Multi-phase AC systems are widely used in energy conversion applications. In multi-phase AC systems, coordinate transformations, such as Clarke transformation, are commonly introduced to reduce the dimensions of multi-phase AC signals, thereby simplifying subsequent control. However, Clarke transformation and its variants are model-based, making them only suitable for systems whose model structures are already known. While for model-unknown systems, these model-based methods are no longer applicable. In this paper, a model-free method, called Phase-Locked Principal Component Analysis (Phase-Locked PCA), is proposed, to extend Clarke-like transformations to model-unknown scenarios. Phase-Locked PCA performs dimensionality reduction in a phase-locked and orthogonal manner, thereby achieving similar functions to that of Clarke. However, unlike Clarke transformation, Phase-Locked PCA does not rely on any prior model knowledge, but extracts information solely from system data, making it well-suited for scenarios where system model knowledge is unknown but system data is available. The effectiveness of Phase-Locked PCA is validated on a real-world model-unknown system, and the results show that Phase-Locked PCA performs well in coordinate transformations under model-unknown scenarios, particularly showing distinct advantages in conditions containing unbalanced signals or harmonic components.

title: Result Identification and Error Repair Method for Generator Stator Ground Fault Active Arc Suppression
abstract: The active arc suppression method based on an external injection source is now the primary technique for mitigating the hazards of generator single-phase ground faults. It can precisely compensate for the double-frequency fault current caused by ground faults. However, when the injected compensation is inaccurate, the method may fail to suppress the arc or even worsen the fault. Current research lacks methods for identifying active arc suppression results and the corresponding error repair. This paper proposes a method for identifying arc suppression results and error repair in generator stator ground faults based on variation in phase leakage current. The identification criterion is built on the variation characteristic of the phase leakage current during the entire fault process. This allows accurate judgment of the arc suppression results, with differentiated treatment strategies applied accordingly. In cases of unsuccessful arc suppression, the compensation error is calculated, and compensation is dynamically adjusted for reliable suppression. PSCAD/EMTDC simulation platform tests and dynamic model experiments verify that the proposed arc suppression result identification method can accurately identify the arc suppression result, and that the error of the arc suppression error calculated by the proposed error repair method is below 1%, which validates the accuracy and engineering practicality of the proposed method.

title: Accurate Rotor Kinetic Energy-Based Power Smoothing Control Using Speed Increment Dynamic Compensation for PMSG-WECS
abstract: Smoothing wind power output can effectively reduce the negative impacts of wind power fluctuations on the power grid. Compared with other methods, rotor kinetic energy-based power smoothing control has the advantages of low cost and fast response. This paper proposes an accurate rotor kinetic energy-based power smoothing method using speed increment dynamic compensation for permanent magnet synchronous generator wind energy conversion systems (PMSG-WECS). Firstly, starting from the transfer function of the PMSG-WECS, the rotor kinetic energy control structure is optimized, and an accurate mathematical mapping between power and rotational speed is established. Secondly, a speed increment dynamic compensation method is designed to effectively suppress the mechanical impact of the system under critical rotational speed conditions, ensuring the operational stability while smoothing wind power fluctuations and guaranteeing wind energy utilization. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed novel power smoothing control method are verified through the establishment of the simulation model and construction of an experimental platform.

title: A Novel Magnetic Integrated Three-Phase EMI Filter for Differential-Mode and Common-Mode Interference Suppression in PMSM Drive Systems
abstract: The application of three-phase electromagnetic interference (EMI) filters in permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive systems can reduce common-mode (CM) interference while filtering out differential-mode (DM) interference in phase currents. Conventional filters will increase the volume and weight of the system. This article proposes a fully magnetic integrated three-phase EMI filter, with a magnetic core consisting of a toroid and a Y-branch limb. The toroid is primarily employed to concentrate the CM flux while providing the path for the DM flux. The Y-branch limb is used to carry the DM flux. The distribution of the flux in the proposed filter under different winding distribution patterns is analyzed. The DM and CM inductances are derived. The optimal winding distribution pattern is determined through quantitative and qualitative comparison. The magnetic saturation analysis is provided by deriving the maximum magnetic flux density of the proposed filter. The magnetic flux density of the proposed filter is verified through ANSYS simulation. The experiment is conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed filter. The results show that the proposed filter can significantly reduce the volume and weight of the system compared to the conventional filter under the same DM and CM suppression performance. In addition, a DC side EMI filter is manufactured to assess its impact on the electrical performance of the motor side. The results indicate that the DC side EMI filter cannot replace the proposed filter. The proposed filter can enhance the performance and reliability of the PMSM drive system.

title: Voltage-Behind-Reactance Model of Hybrid-Excitation Dual Three-Phase Main Machine in Aircraft Synchronous Starter Generator Based on Equivalent Field Current of Permanent Magnet
abstract: Accurate modeling for the hybrid-excitation dual three-phase main machine (HEDTP-MM) in aircraft synchronous starter-generator system serves as the foundation for system analysis and control strategy research. Considering the complex hybrid-excitation characteristics of the HEDTP-MM and the requirement that both the stator and rotor windings can be directly interfaced with the external power circuit, the air gap flux characteristics generated by the permanent-magnet (PM) excitation is first analyzed based on the equivalent magnetic circuit method in this paper. Then, the PM excitation is converted into an equivalent field current, which enables a unified description of PM excitation and wound field (WF) excitation in the HEDTP-MM. Based on this equivalent field current of PM, a decoupled constant-parameter double-side voltage-behind reactance (VBR) model of the HEDTP-MM considering magnetic saturation is derived and established. This model enables the direct connection of stator and rotor windings to external circuits and maintains high modeling accuracy. Experimental results under steady-state and transient operating conditions verified the validity and accuracy of the proposed VBR model in this paper.

title: Design Optimization of Large-Capacity High-Speed Permanent-Magnet Generator Based on Surrogate-Assisted Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm
abstract: The large-capacity high-speed permanent-magnet generator, with its unique design, plays a crucial role in special applications such as aviation and integrated power system. However, it has strict requirements for power quality, and there is a problem of design optimization efficiency. In this article, a 2.5 MW, 7000 r/min large-capacity high-speed permanent-magnet generator is designed. To enhance the power quality and optimization efficiency, an efficient optimization method based on surrogate-assisted non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (SANSGA-II) is proposed. Initially, the surrogate model of the generator is constructed by using Latin hypercube sampling, and the relationship between optimization variables and objectives is explored. Subsequently, the surrogate model is utilized to predict and sort the objective values in the variable space. The variable values in the high-value area are taken as the adjustment directions for crossover and mutation, thereby improving the optimization efficiency and diversity of the algorithm. In addition, the dynamic point addition strategy is implemented. Then, the accuracy of the model is ensured and the reliability of the algorithm is enhanced. These improvements provide a theoretical basis for the optimization method of the generator. By using the proposed and traditional methods, the generator performance is optimized. The results show that the proposed method achieves faster iteration speed and higher solution quality than traditional method. Finally, the prototype is manufactured based on the design parameters and tested. The optimization results are validated for both accuracy and reliability.

title: White-Box High-Frequency Modeling of Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines with Hairpin Windings
abstract: This paper further details the process of constructing a high-frequency (HF) white-box model for interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) with hairpin windings based on the small-signal time-harmonic finite element analysis method. The model employs complex differential reluctivity tensors that vary with dc-biased magnetic induction and frequency, enabling accurate simulation of hysteresis, eddy current, and saturation effects in electrical steel sheets. To enhance modeling accuracy, the frequency-dependent resistance and leakage inductance of the end windings are calculated using the three-dimensional finite element method. More importantly, this study combines simulation and experimental methods to conduct a detailed comparative analysis of the influence of impregnation on motor parasitic capacitance and HF impedance characteristics, as well as the impact of rotor presence and position on motor HF impedance characteristics. Experimental results validate that the model established in this paper can accurately predict the differential-mode and common-mode impedance characteristics of IPMSMs with hairpin windings during the design stage.

title: Temperature-Field Analysis of an Air-Cooled Line-Start Solid-Rotor PMSM With Alternating-Hollow-Solid Slot Arrangement
abstract: The Line-Start-Solid-Rotor PMSM (LSSR-PMSM) has the characteristics of simple supporting equipment and low cost compared with the ordinary frequency conversion PMSM system, and has the characteristics of excellent starting performance and high efficiency compared with the induction motor, which has the potential to replace the traditional frequency conversion PMSM system in the applications such as oilfield pumping machines and coal mills in power plants, etc., which require the motor to have excellent starting performance. Due to the structure of solid rotor and cage bars, the rotor of LSSR-PMSM generates more eddy current loss, which leads to higher temperature rise. The magnitude of eddy currents is also related to the starting capacity of the LSSR-PMSM. Considering the actual situation of the compact mechanical structure of the LSSR-PMSM with small and medium capacity, a novel alternating-hollow-solid rotor topology without additional mechanical structure is proposed to suppress the temperature rise of the LSSR-PMSM. Besides, the solid slots of the structure serve to provide starting torque, and the hollow groove serves to change the state of fluid motion in the air gap and enhance the thermal dissipation on the rotor surface. This paper reveal the air motion law in the hollow slot and analyze the influence of the air slot on solid rotor heat transfer path. And the prototype with the scheme that optimizes the motor performance and heat transfer efficiency was machined to verify the conclusions. The research content of this paper provides ideas for the design of LSSR-PMSM.

title: Sensorless Control of Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Improved Synchronous Reference Frame Filter in Double Angle Axis
abstract: In the medium-to-high-speed speed control system of the interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM), to address the issues of large harmonic component of the expanded back electromotive force (EMF) observed by conventional sliding mode observer (SMO) and the phase lag caused by the low-pass filter (LPF), a sensorless control method based on an improved synchronous reference frame filter (ISRFF) in double angle axis is proposed. Firstly, the extended back EMF in double angle and αβ-axis are processed through the LPF with same cut-off frequency to generate leading and lagging phase shifts. Secondly, the phase shifts are transformed to dq-axis, and the harmonics are filtered out by LPF. Then, the phase shifts are eliminated by a triangular transformation. The position observation accuracy of the SMO is improved while the rotor position error signal is constructed, thus the heterodyne method is omitted. Finally, the experimental results confirm that compared with conventional methods, the proposed method effectively filters out harmonics, reduces the maximum position error under steady-state conditions, and mitigates speed fluctuations during dynamic operation.

title: Partitioned Orthotropic Equivalent Thermal Modeling and Validation for Distributed Hairpin Windings in Permanent Magnet Motors
abstract: Distributed hairpin windings in permanent magnet (PM) motors feature complex three-dimensional (3-D) structures, which bring great challenges to efficient thermal modeling and temperature prediction. High-fidelity thermal simulations of such windings suffer from excessive computational costs, hindering rapid thermal design optimization. To address this issue, a partitioned equivalent thermal modeling method is proposed for hairpin windings, with a focus on the structurally intricate end-winding regions. Based on heat transfer theory and orthotropic material properties, the equivalent orthotropic thermal conductivities of in-slot and end-winding regions are rigorously derived, and the tensor transformation of orthotropic thermal conductivity is employed to account for the non-orthogonal arrangement of end-windings. Comparative simulations of the detailed hairpin model and the proposed equivalent model demonstrate that the latter achieves high predictive accuracy while reducing computational resources by over 95%. Experimental tests on a distributed hairpin winding PM motor prototype further validate the accuracy of the detailed model and the reliability of the equivalent model (relative error < 5%).

title: Influence of End Structure Optimization on 3D Electromagnetic Field and Losses of a Novel Double-Side Counter-Flow Turbogenerator
abstract: Turbogenerators are crucial equipment in power generation. Unreasonable design of the end of such generators can lead increased end losses that can impact the safety and stability of the system in operation. In this study, a 350-MW novel double-side counter-flow large turbogenerator is proposed. A three-dimensional transient nonlinear electromagnetic field model of the end region of the turbogenerator is established to analyze the electromagnetic field. In order to reduce the losses of end components, the novel structural optimization design is proposed. The influence of the modified end structure on the flux density of the end components is investigated by varying the relative lengths of the stator and rotor cores and the distances between the copper screen and windings. The losses of the end components are obtained under different end structures. The results show that a reasonable relative length between the stator and rotor cores and distance between the copper screen and winding effectively reduced losses from end components in the proposed design. The results of the calculation are verified experimentally. Thus, this study provides an important reference for the optimization of the end structures of turbogenerators.

title: Nuclear-Powered Hybrid Energy System for Clean Hydrogen Production: Time-Step-Optimized Real-Time Multi-Domain Hardware Emulation
abstract: Increasing global emphasis on decarbonization and the proliferation of renewable energy, energy storage, and nuclear power is driving a surge of research interest into integrated sustainable energy modeling, simulation, operation and control. Traditional electromagnetic transient (EMT) methods typically discretize electrical networks using the trapezoidal rule. When coupled with the ordinary differential equations (ODEs) of other physical domains, however, the absolute stability region of the numerical integration scheme can shift, and discrepancies in time constants across subsystems further complicate integration of disparate models. While the demand for integrating EMT with multi-domain co-simulations is increasing, existing commercial EMT simulation tools either lack support for multi-domain physical coupling or are not specifically optimized for such hybrid simulations. To address this gap, this paper proposes a robust multiscale time-step estimation (RMTE) framework that enables real-time co-simulation of EMT networks and multi-domain subsystems. The framework includes a fast, efficient, and adaptive approach for selecting the optimal maximum time-step across heterogeneous physical domains. The proposed method is validated through a case study involving small modular reactors (SMRs), wind farm, photovoltaics (PV) and low-temperature proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolysis for clean hydrogen production. Real-time hardware co-emulation is achieved on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based platform. The results demonstrate significant improvements in simulation efficiency and execution time.

title: A Multidisciplinary Approach to the Geometrical Design of Axial Active Magnetic Bearings - Part I: Methodology
abstract: Approximately 25% of all electricity worldwide is consumed by pumps, compressors, and blowers in industrial applications. High-speed electric machines based on magnetic suspension technology present a significant opportunity to improve the efficiency of these drivelines, thus reducing total energy consumption, costs, and pollution levels. However, a major challenge in adopting the high-speed drivelines in industrial applications lies in their implementation. The design lead time for such machines typically spans years, whereas an ideal time-frame would be mere weeks. This study presents a systematic multidisciplinary design process for thrust active magnetic bearing to accelerate design work. By structuring the design steps in a precise order, automation can be integrated to develop the design space, which can then be directly utilized in the system level design analysis. In practice, when another design area is modified, a thrust bearing design that fulfils the overall design requirements can be automatically updated from the design space. Consequently, non-viable solutions are directly excluded, reducing the iterative nature of high-speed machine system design. Part I of this paper details the methodology of the multidisciplinary design process, while Part II illustrates the application of the proposed design method using a one-megawatt high-speed electric machine for a heat pump compressor.

title: Torque Calculation Error Compensation for Spherical Reluctance Motor Based on Dynamic Weighted PSO-GWO
abstract: To improve the torque modeling accuracy of spherical reluctance motors (SPRMs), this paper proposes a torque calculation error compensation model based on the dynamic weighted particle swarm-gray wolf optimization (DW PG) algorithm. First, the calculation errors generated by different analytical methods are analyzed. Subsequently, based on the error characteristics, extreme learning machine (ELM) is adopted to compensate for the torque calculation error. To optimize the input weights and biases of ELM, a dynamic weighting factor is proposed to balance the global search capability of the particle swarm optimization (PSO) and the local exploration capability of the grey wolf optimization (GWO). The model takes the excitation current and rotor angle as the inputs and the errors as outputs. Finally, the experimental and simulation results show that, compared with the traditional compensation models, the proposed compensation model has higher compensation accuracy, stronger stability and better real time performance, which is suitable for SPRM with different parameter structures and different working conditions.

title: Optimization of Air-gap Profile in Dual-Permanent-Magnet Vernier Motor for Torque Ripple Reduction
abstract: Dual-permanent-magnet vernier motors (DPMVMs) have garnered significant attention due to their high torque density and high efficiency in low-speed applications compared with conventional surface-mounted permanent magnet motors (SMPMM). However, studies show that DPMVMs exhibit higher torque ripple than SMPMM. The ripple in DPMVMs is primarily influenced by harmonics generated by bidirectional flux modulation. The geometry of air-gap-side surface of stator and rotor plays a pivotal role in harmonic generation and magnetic field modulation performance. In order to reduce the torque ripple of the DPMVM while still maintaining a high torque, an air-gap profile optimization method for DPMVM is proposed and investigated in this paper. The proposed method introduces two layers of grids composed of different materials on the air-gap-side surface of rotor and stator of a typical DPMVM. During the optimization process, the material type of each grid in the two layers can be adjusted, enabling the identification of optimal material combinations that enhance torque characteristics. The electromagnetic performances of the initial and optimized models are compared. Furthermore, the proposed method is refined and applied to a turbine motor, taking cost into consideration. The results demonstrate that the torque ripple of the modified turbine motor is decreased by 32.8% and the output torque is improved by 1.4%. Meanwhile, the material cost of the motor is further reduced.

title: Spatial-Constrained Structure Optimization of the Mover for Minimizing Power Consumption in Maglev Planar Motors
abstract: This paper presents a novel spatial-structure optimization method for the coils of moving-coil magnetically levitated planar motors (MLPMs) to address the coupled challenges of power consumption and spatial constraints. The proposed framework systematically determines the optimal coil geometry and arrangement to minimize power consumption under a required force output and a strictly confined mover volume. A harmonic-based electromagnetic force model is employed to guide a compact coil layout by defining the number, length, and spacing of coils. These parameters are subsequently incorporated into a power-minimization model to determine the coil and beam widths. A final trade-off optimization is performed to balance high-order harmonic suppression and manufacturing tolerance, resulting in a comprehensive design strategy. Experimental results validate the superiority of the proposed method: under identical motor dimensions and magnetic pole pitch, the optimized design achieves more than a 40% increase in thrust-to-weight ratio (TWR) while reducing thrust fluctuation to below 15%. Furthermore, at a constant levitation height, the proposed design reduces power consumption by 10% to 25% compared with conventional systems. These findings demonstrate significant improvements in system stability and force efficiency, offering a generalized and practical design guideline for high-performance moving-coil MLPM.

title: Analysis and Calculation of Circumferential Winding Tension in High-Speed Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor With a Novel Composite Rotor
abstract: The permanent magnets in the rotor of conventional surface-mounted high-speed permanent-magnet synchronous motor (HSPMSM) are vulnerable to centrifugal forces during high-speed rotation, which has long limited their rotational speed. This paper presents a novel composite rotor design for HSPMSMs that significantly improves the allowable rotational speed. The composite rotor is wound around the shaft to replace sintered permanent magnets. Therefore, for stable motor operation, it is crucial to analyze the required tension during the winding of composite magnetic materials (CMM). Based on the elasticity theory, this paper derives the analytical model for the mechanical strength of the composite rotor. According to the strength requirements, a forming calculation method for reducing the circumferential winding tension that meets the strength design requirements of the composite rotor is established. Analytical results confirm that this method accurately predicts the stress distribution of each carbon fiber winding layer. Finally, a composite rotor for high-speed permanent magnet motors was fabricated based on the winding tension analysis and verified through experiments.

title: Characteristics of Sideband Current and Noise Induced by Periodic Modulation Techniques in PMSMs
abstract: This study investigates the sideband currents generated by periodic-switching-frequency pulse width modulation (PSFPWM) strategies and their impact on the high-frequency sideband noise of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). The harmonics of these sideband currents are analytically derived for PSFPWM strategies. Then, the influence of PSFPWM on the sideband force and acoustic noise in PMSMs with various pole/slot combinations is deduced. The features of sideband current and noise under these strategies are revealed and validated by experiment results. Selection criteria for the switching frequency variation rate and frequency extension width of PSFPWM are also discussed. The results indicate that PSFPWM introduces additional frequency components into the spectrum, thereby dispersing the concentrated energy. With appropriate parameter selection, PSFPWM strategies can effectively suppress the high-frequency sideband current and noise across the full speed range.

title: Investigation on Non-Uniform Teeth Application in Counter-Rotating Axial-Flux Hybrid-Excitation Permanent Magnet Machine With Low Cogging Torque
abstract: The counter-rotating axial-flux hybrid-excitation permanent magnet (PM) machine is a novel power device specifically designed for counter-rotating propeller (CRP) systems. Cogging torque (CT) can induce vibrations and noise, adversely affecting its dynamic performance and stealth characteristics, necessitating strict suppression. However, the variable-flux and consequent-pole (CP) structure obscure the characteristics of the CT, leading to a lack of a clear theoretical basis for its suppression. To address this challenge, this paper investigates CT suppression in the counter-rotating axial-flux hybrid-excitation PM machines using non-uniform teeth (NUT) and comprehensively analyzes the implementation consequences. Firstly, a general CT model of the counter-rotating axial-flux hybrid-excitation PM machine is established, and the fundamental principles of NUT are derived. Subsequently, the constraints required to achieve a beneficial effect while preventing phase-phase asymmetry are proposed. Furthermore, the impact of the proposed method on the electromagnetic performance of counter-rotating axial-flux hybrid-excitation PM machine is examined, leading to the formulation of optimal angle allocation principles and recalculation of the winding factor. Finally, theoretical analysis is validated through experimental results, demonstrating that the research work effectively guides the application of NUT and enhances the robustness of counter-rotating axial-flux hybrid-excitation PM machine in CRP drive systems.

title: Design Optimization of a Spoke-Type Permanent Magnet Motor for Torque Performance Improvement
abstract: This paper introduces an optimized spoke-type interior permanent magnet (IPM) motor featuring a flux-concentrating rotor, which can be used to reduce leakage magnetic flux and increase efficiency. The output torque is increased by improved PM utilization ratio. Then, an improved Taguchi iterative optimization method coupled with finite element analysis (FEA) is applied to optimize structural parameters by rationally narrowing the range of variables. Compared to the initial spoke-type and U-type motors, the optimal flux-concentrating motor can obtain higher airgap flux-density in main flux path without additional magnet material usage. This is made possible by elevation of working point of the PMs and reduction of the PM leakage magnetic flux. In addition, a comprehensive analysis of the optimal motor, including open-circuit characteristics, load characteristics, temperature distribution, and mechanical integrity, has been carried out to validate the rationality of the optimal scheme. The results show that the proposed scheme can increase the output torque by up to 25% and the efficiency by 1% with a fairly small raise in torque ripple. Finally, two 3000 r/min 10 kW prototypes are fabricated to validate the superiority of the proposed design.

title: Comparative Study of Torque Production Mechanism in Rotor-PM and Stator-PM Vernier Machines
abstract: In recent years, permanent magnet vernier (PMV) machines have gained more and more research interest owing to their superior torque density. However, rotor-PM vernier (RPMV) and stator-PM vernier (SPMV) machines, differing in the position of PMs, exhibit significant differences in torque performance. To reveal the underlying cause, this study begins with an analysis of the phase characteristics of three basic parts: the armature, flux modulator, and PMs, with particular attention to the phase angles of the resulting air-gap flux density harmonics. Then, based on the Maxwell stress tensor (MST) method, the torque contributions of the dominant harmonics in RPMV and SPMV machines, such as the Path, Pmth, and (Pm+Z)th harmonics, are quantified to display their torque differences. The results indicate that torque in RPMV machines is primarily generated by the Pmth harmonic, while both the Path and Pmth harmonics contribute torque together in SPMV machines. In addition, the torque generated by the Pmth harmonic in RPMV machines markedly exceeds that in SPMV machines. To verify these theoretical findings, two representative machines with the same winding pole-pair number and machine dimension are compared. Finally, a prototype of the RPMV machine is tested to confirm the accuracy of the analytical and simulation results.
