title: Stage-Wise Analytical Modeling of the Stray Magnetic Field in Surface-Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Under Mixed Eccentricity
abstract: Conventional subdomain methods face challenges in calculating the stray magnetic field of surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motors (SPMSMs) under eccentric conditions due to their inability to handle complex boundaries, leading to low computational efficiency. To address these issues, this paper proposes a cell-based Schwarz-Christoffel (SC) mapping method and a stage-wise calculation strategy to improve computational efficiency while maintaining accuracy. First, an analytical model (AM) integrating equivalent surface current, conformal transformation method is established. Based on magnetic field superposition, the load air-gap magnetic field is derived. Second, a stage-wise subdomain-based computational strategy is employed to decouple the magnetic field calculations for the air-gap region and the outer air region. The stray magnetic field is analytically modeled using SC mapping and separation of variables. Finally, the proposed method is validated through experiments on an 8-pole 18-slot interior-rotor SPMSM with mixed eccentricity. Results show that the TM achieves a computational error of only 3.49% and that the computational speed is 136 times faster than that of the finite element method (FEM).

title: A Subdivision Analytical Model for Accurate Prediction, Rapid Positioning and Degree Evaluation of Irreversible Demagnetization of Permanent Magnets in Surface-Mounted Permanent Magnet Motors
abstract: In response to the drawbacks of long time consumption of finite element method (FEM) and poor universality of traditional analytical models for irreversible demagnetization of permanent magnets (PMs) in surface-mounted permanent magnet motors (SPMMs), a subdivision analytical model (SAM) is proposed. The proposed analytical model not only has strong universality and high accuracy in analyzing irreversible demagnetization of PMs of SPMMs, the calculation errors of fundamental amplitudes of no-load back electromotive forces (EMFs) before and after irreversible demagnetization of PMs are less than 1.40% and 3.00%, but also can greatly reduce calculation time compared to the FEM. Afterwards, a fast fault location and degree evaluation method for local irreversible demagnetization of PMs based on coil no-load back EMF is proposed, which can quickly locate the local irreversible demagnetization and evaluate demagnetization degree under common demagnetization conditions, including local irreversible demagnetization of a single magnetic pole and all magnetic poles. The width angle of local irreversible demagnetization of the trailing edge of PMs can be quickly determined by combining the waveform of the coil no-load back EMF and the phase of the typical component, and the average demagnetization rate can be quickly estimated based on the amplitude of the typical component.

title: Iron Loss Separation Between Stator and Rotor of a Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Motor via a Temperature-Based Loss Observer
abstract: Accurate measurement and separation of losses in electric drive motors is critical for iterative prototyping, enabling the development of high-precision cooling systems, loss-minimizing motor topologies, and energy-efficient control strategies. Although the total iron loss in permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) can be determined experimentally, the precise allocation of this loss between the stator and rotor has long been a challenge. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel methodology with two key innovations. First, an experimental calibration strategy for the PMSM thermal model is developed that eliminates the dependence on prior knowledge of the precise loss distribution and allows independent model calibration. Second, based on this calibrated thermal model, we introduce an innovative temperature-based loss observer that improves the accuracy of the iron loss separation between the stator and rotor by using measured temperature data. Through these innovations, the proposed methodology, the proposed methodology simplifies the thermal modeling workflow, but also enables the generation of accurate iron loss profiles.

title: Parallelizable Complex Neural Dynamics Models for PMSM Temperature Estimation with Hardware Acceleration
abstract: Accurate and efficient thermal dynamics models of permanent magnet synchronous motors are vital to efficient thermal management strategies. Physics-informed methods combine model-based and data-driven methods, offering greater flexibility than model-based methods and superior explainability compared to data-driven methods. Nonetheless, there are still challenges in balancing real-time performance, estimation accuracy, and explainability. This paper presents a hardware-efficient complex neural dynamics model achieved through the linear decoupling, diagonalization, and reparameterization of the state-space model, introducing a novel paradigm for the physics-informed method that offers high explainability and accuracy in electric motor temperature estimation tasks. We validate this physics-informed method on an NVIDIA A800 GPU using the JAX machine learning framework, the parallel prefix-sum algorithm, and the Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) platform. We demonstrate its superior estimation performance and paralleliz able hardware acceleration capabilities through experimental evaluation on a real electric motor.

title: Low Copper Loss High-Resistance Connection Fault Tolerant Method in Five-phase PMSM with Current and Voltage Reconfiguration
abstract: The high-resistance connection (HRC) fault in the five-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) leads to increased copper losses and reduced efficiency due to impedance imbalance. The impedance model under HRC fault is incorporated into the proposed fault-tolerant control method. A current and voltage reconfiguration is also adopted with the constraint of minimizing copper loss (MCL). Additionally, the maximization of torque output range with low copper loss (MTMCL) constraint is also proposed for more torque output capability. Combined with the above two constraints and proposed fault tolerant control method, a fault tolerant coefficient switching strategy following electromagnetic torque is also summarized for minimization copper loss without overheating. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed control method achieves a significant reduction in copper loss compared to original method.

title: Improved Loss Analysis Method Considering Core Anisotropy and AC Copper Loss in Linear Oscillating Actuator
abstract: The linear oscillating actuator (LOA) operates as the driving mechanism for linear compressor, which shows high power density and efficiency. To ensure the high efficiency of linear compressor, it is important to accurately calculate the loss of LOA. Due to the complex structure of LOA with segmented outer core and permanent magnet, normally, 3D finite element analysis (FEA) was executed to accurately analyze the loss of LOA. However, since 3D FEA requires significant computational time, 2D FEA is sometimes employed by simplifying the 3D model of the LOA into an equivalent 2D model, even at the cost of some accuracy, to reduce analysis time. This paper briefly introduces the correction factor that corrects the results from 2D axisymmetric FEA and implies limitations. This paper introduces additional losses, core anisotropy and AC copper loss and proposes a comprehensive loss analysis method that combines two approaches: the iron loss calculation for anisotropic materials and the AC copper loss correction in 2D FEA. Each method's validity was confirmed by comparing loss with 2D and 3D FEA. Finally, the total loss and computational cost between 2D FEA, 3D FEA, the proposed method and experiment were compared.

title: Adaptive Virtual Capacitor Control Based on LADRC for Voltage Regulation in Industrial DC Microgrids
abstract: To address the critical voltage stability of industrial DC microgrids serving sensitive loads, virtual capacitor control is a promising technique for inertia enhancement. However, conventional virtual capacitor control, with its fixed parameters and limited disturbance rejection capability, struggles to maintain qualified voltage quality, threatening the reliable operation of industrial equipment. This paper proposes a novel adaptive virtual capacitor control strategy based on linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC). The key contribution is a novel control architecture where the virtual capacitor is not predetermined but is adaptively modulated by real-time disturbance estimated by LADRC. This unique feedback mechanism allows the system to proactively counteract both external load changes and internal parameter uncertainties, achieving superior voltage regulation. Furthermore, an integrated sliding time window filter ensures smooth control action by mitigating oscillations from voltage ripple. The proposed strategy's effectiveness in simultaneously enhancing voltage deviation suppression, ripple mitigation, and dynamic inertia support is validated through simulation and hardware-in the-loop (HIL) experiments.

title: Indirect Predictive Power Control of Grid-Following Inverters Using the Grid-Side Measurements
abstract: The grid-following inverters (GFLs) in microgrids require active and reactive power control. While the predictive power control (PPC) has shown effective performance due to its flexibility and fast response, it needs the system model and measured signals of the inverter and load. The high numbers of sensors and model dependency reduce the reliability of the PPC. To address these issues, this article proposes two PPC schemes, referred to as direct and indirect PPCs. The direct PPC utilizes the ultralocal model theory to reduce the parameter dependency of the prediction algorithm. Thus, novel models for predicting active and reactive power are presented here. To further increase the system reliability, an indirect PPC is presented, which employs the grid-side current measurements to control the active and reactive power. This reduces the number of sensors required in the direct PPC, which requires the GFL and load measurements. The results have shown that the GFL control system can be switched between the indirect and direct PPC modes promptly. This feature is useful when the sensors are faulty or need maintenance. Both proposed control methods have been verified using an experimental setup and compared with the model-based PPC. The results confirm the improved performance of the proposed PPCs and easy transitions between them.

title: DFIG-Based Wind Turbine Interturn Fault Modeling With Comprehensive Winding Failure Identification
abstract: Modern wind turbines are a complex electromechanical energy conversion system that is prone to mechanical and electrical faults. This article addresses a common type of electrical fault that affects turbines with Doubly-Fed Induction Generator, which is winding failure inside the generator, such as short-circuits between turns, also called interturn faults. A simplified electrical model of the generator with interturn fault is presented and validated with experimental data in a laboratory, and then used as support to develop a method for fault identification. Firstly, we analyzed the experimental and simulation data of stator and rotor currents, under both healthy and faulty conditions, and the negative-sequence current is observed to be an indicator of interturn faults. Furthermore, it is shown that the position of the vector of the negative-sequence current in the “dq” domain changes according to the affected phase, and this feature can be used to identify the faulty phase. Another contribution of this work, which was developed through the analysis of model-based and experimental data, is a machine learning method capable of identifying and locating the faulty winding affected by a short circuit, designed to ensure traceability in the decision process and to improve the ability to interpret the results. In addition, we introduce a generalized approach aimed at reducing the need for frequent retraining under different operational conditions. The model achieved 98% accuracy on experimental test data collected in various wind turbine operating scenarios, having been trained solely on simulated data generated simplified DFIG model. These contributions aim to promote less effort with adequate accuracy in the processes of training models, identifying faults and understanding the results for different operational conditions and different DFIG wind turbines.

title: Analysis and Optimization of a New Consequent Pole Hybrid Excited Machine Applied for Electric Vehicles
abstract: In this article, a new consequent-pole hybrid excited machine with segmented stator (CPHES machine) is proposed for electric vehicles (EVs). The stator is segmented into two parts to eliminate even-order harmonic fields in the air-gap. The stator tooth is divided into two types, in which the armature tooth is larger in size than the modulation tooth. Both the armature winding and the excitation winding housed in the stator are concentrated windings. Eight U-type permanent magnets (PMs) with the same polarity are housed in the consequent-pole rotor. The machine topology of this proposed machine is illustrated. The characteristics of the CPHES machine, such as the field coupling effect and the segmented stator, are discussed by the analytical model. The multi-objective optimization with sensitivity analysis is used to improve the output capability of the CPHES machine. The optimal outcomes can be obtained by a set of Pareto front. The finite element (FE) method is used to analyze the electromagnetic performances of the CPHES machine, including the air-gap flux density, the flux linkage, the no-load back electromagnetic force (back-EMF), the electromagnetic torque and the cogging torque. A prototype is manufactured and measured to verify the analytical method and the FE-predictions.

title: Harmonic Localization Analysis of Radial Electromagnetic Force in Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Influenced by Saliency Effect
abstract: This study investigates the challenges posed by electromagnetic (EM) vibration noise in interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSMs), specifically focusing on the rotor saliency effect. Comprehensive harmonic localization models that incorporate the saliency effect have been developed to analyze magnetic flux density and radial EM force density (REMFD) in IPMSMs. An 8-pole, 12-slot spoke-type IPMSM serves as the primary model, exploring both temporal and spatial harmonic characteristics influenced by the saliency effect under no-load and load conditions through finite element quantitative analysis while tracing their origins to the magnetic field. A novel rapid layered traced optimization strategy for multiple objectives of further reducing REMFD under both no-load and load conditions while maintaining torque performance is proposed on the key rotor dimensions, based on the traceability of REMFD harmonics. Validation is conducted using multi-physics vibration noise prediction models and experimental measurements. The results indicate that reducing the saliency effect mitigates the harmonics of the main pole magnetic field under load, effectively reducing low-order REMFD and EM noise across various loading conditions. This study not only enhances the theoretical understanding of EM noise and vibration in IPMSMs but also offers a more straightforward optimization strategy for IPMSM design.

title: Multi-Stage Optimization Scheme for Partitioned Magnet Pole Variable-Leakage-Flux Machine Considering Flux-Adjustable Range
abstract: This paper focuses on a multi-stage optimization scheme for variable-leakage-flux machines (VLFMs), where the leakage flux is passively controlled by armature-reaction-induced magnetic saturation. In VLFMs, the magnetic flux is regulated by the flux weakening (FW) method and controllable leakage flux. This intrinsic coupling complicates the consideration in the flux-adjustable range during the optimization procedure, thereby limiting the full utilization of the inherent advantages of the VLF property to optimize the overall performance. Therefore, a novel design optimization scheme is developed for the VLFM in this paper, which can well decouple the armature reaction and VLF property by employing a three-stage field-circuit coupled model. The proposed model accounts for three representative operating conditions. In the first stage, key performance requirements like peak torque at low speed are considered. In the second and third stages, the minimum and maximum q-axis currents are applied, respectively, allowing direct acquisition of the PM flux linkage while eliminating the influence of the d-axis armature reaction. Consequently, the flux-adjustable range can be directly calculated and optimized in the optimization procedure. Afterwards, the proposed design optimization scheme is implemented on a recently developed partitioned magnet pole VLFM (PMP-VLFM) to obtain an optimal design. Finally, finite element (FE) simulations and experimental tests are carried out to verify the feasibility of the proposed design optimization scheme.

title: Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Control Based on Model-Free Predictive Current Control for PMSM with Dual Star-Delta Windings
abstract: This paper proposes a model-free predictive current control combined with an adaptive fault-tolerant control (AFTC-MFPCC) strategy for dual star-delta windings permanent magnet synchronous motor (DSDW-PMSM) under different phase shift angles. The proposed strategy enhances the operational performance of this motor when current sensor fault or open-phase fault occur in any star-connected winding phase, showing strong adaptability and robustness. Firstly, the invariance of the fundamental magnetomotive force (MMF) under single open-phase fault in DSDW-PMSM with different phase shift angles is analytically derived. Secondly, an adaptive fault-tolerant control strategy is proposed. Upon detecting a persistent zero current in any phase, it switches the adaptive fault-tolerant transformation matrix without explicit fault diagnosis, thereby avoiding the impact of current sensor faults and reducing the fault detection time. Subsequently, the xy-axis reference values are modified through current feedback, enabling the motor to adaptively transition from the fault state to the normal operation state. Furthermore, model-free predictive current control is employed to replace traditional PI control or deadbeat predictive current control in the current loop module of the vector control structure, which outputs four voltage vectors. This method avoids current tracking errors and severe waveform distortion caused by inaccuracies in motor parameter inputs. Finally, tests are conducted on a 24-slot/10-pole DSDW-PMSM with a 15° phase shift to validate the feasibility of the proposed method.

title: A Hybrid Flexible Arc Suppression Method for Generator Stator Ground Faults Based on Slot Potential Analysis Unit
abstract: For generator stator ground faults, the active arc suppression method typically needs the large-capacity inverter, leading to huge size and high cost. Moreover, the existing compensated parameter calculation method based on coil potentials cannot suppress arc at the non-coil connection points. To address these limitations, a hybrid flexible arc suppression method is proposed in this paper. By combining with the arc suppression coil grounding method, only the third harmonic and partial fundamental currents need to be compensated by the active arc suppression device, which significantly reduces the inverter capacity requirement. Instead of the coil potential analysis unit, slot potential analysis unit is used to characterize the winding potential distribution. Analytical equations are formulated to precisely calculate the fundamental and the third-harmonic fault potentials across the entire windings. The calculation results are used to determine the compensated parameters, enabling reliable arc suppression at any fault position within the entire windings. Effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by simulation and experiment.

title: Winding and Magnet Temperature Decoupled Tracking for PMSM Eliminating Saturation using Small Position Signal Injection and Kalman Filter
abstract: This paper proposes a Kalman filter-based stator winding (SW) and permanent magnet (PM) temperature tracking approach for PM synchronous motors (PMSMs), where temperature tracking of SW and PM is decoupled and free from magnetic saturation and thus achieves improved performance. In the proposed approach, a small position signal is added to extract two decoupled temperature-sensitive measurements, a linear state-space model is constructed from the thermal model, and the Kalman filter is employed to accurately track the SW and PM temperatures by using the state-space model and measurements. The small position signal will not affect machine operation, while the temperature tracking can effectively avoid the cross influence between SW and PM. Moreover, there is no need for machine inductances and thus the temperature tracking is not affected by saturation as well as inverter distortion. In the proposed approach, the temperature tracking model includes secant and cosine operations of the current angle, which can effectively improve the signal-to-noise ratio especially under low-load conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated on a laboratory test machine with extensive experiments under various load and speed conditions.

title: Energy-Optimal Motion Trajectory Accounting for Machine Efficiency for a Servo Motor Drive
abstract: This article addresses the energy-optimal trajectory planning problem for servomotor systems. Previous research typically considers only the copper losses of the motor in the cost function, neglecting iron losses and mechanical losses, or incorporates iron losses using empirical formulas. However, the loss mechanisms of the motor are complex, and empirical formulas often fail to accurately model motor losses, resulting in suboptimal trajectory planning. In contrast, motor efficiency maps, obtained through experimental measurements or finite element analysis (FEA), can accurately represent motor efficiency across various combinations of torque and speed, facilitating a comprehensive evaluation of overall motor losses. In this article, the efficiency map of a surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) is experimentally measured. With the measured efficiency map, total motor losses are incorporated into the cost function. However, integrating the efficiency map into the cost function complicates the optimal control problem. To address this challenge, a dynamic programming (DP) approach is introduced, transforming the optimal control problem into a multi-stage decision-making process, thereby ensuring an effective and accurate solution. Experimental results demonstrate that the energy-optimal trajectory, accounting for total machine losses, is more energy-efficient than one considering only copper losses.

title: Improved 3-D Hybrid Models for Open-Circuit Field Prediction in SPM Machines With Overhang Structures
abstract: This article proposes two improved 3-D hybrid models (HMs) combining subdomain (SD) and equivalent magnetic network (EMN) methods for open-circuit field prediction in two surface-mounted permanent magnet (SPM) machines with distinct overhang structures, simultaneously accounting for saturation effects and leakage flux influences. The 3-D HMs iteratively update the equivalent saturation surface current, which is used as part of the 2-D SD boundary conditions to characterize the saturation effect. The key lies in modifying the 2-D SD model to derive flux sources specific to overhang structures within the 3-D EMN model. Firstly, depending on the types of leakage flux, the machines are divided into several regions along the axial direction. Each subregion includes several slices. Then, for the PM overhang machine (POM), the flux source correction factor for each slice considering end and air-gap leakage fluxes is derived using the magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) model. Additionally, the linkage fluxes supplied by the overhang PMs are calculated and injected into the EMN units corresponding to end slices. Meanwhile, in the stator overhang machine (SOM), the axial distribution of air-gap flux density is solved using the magnetic charge model, with both leakage flux types incorporated for flux source modification. Two prototypes are fabricated, and the high accuracy and efficiency of both proposed 3-D HMs are verified by 3-D finite element analysis (FEA) and experimental results.

title: Analytical Model for Predicting Rotor Eddy Current Loss of PMSMs Considering Magnetic Saturation and Diffusion Effect
abstract: Rotor eddy-current loss (RECL) in permanent-magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) is strongly influenced by magnetic core saturation and diffusion effect (eddy-current reaction) in conducting parts. Many analytical models omit one of these, leading to errors at high load or under rich harmonics. This paper proposes a nonlinear hybrid analytical framework that couples a magnetostatic model (MSM) with a frequency-domain model (FDM) via an equivalent current-sheet (ECS) interface. The MSM computes the load-dependent magnetic field under nonlinear core permeability. Over one electrical period, the tangential field at the inner stator surface is sampled and decomposed by fast Fourier transform (FFT) into ECSs with explicit space-time orders. These ECSs are subsequently fed to the FDM, which solves the diffusion problem in conductive rotor regions, yielding per-harmonic RECL estimates. Compared with 2D finite-element analysis (FEA), the method maintains high accuracy across saturation levels and frequencies while requiring substantially lower computational effort. Experimental validation is carried out on a PMSM using a thermal-based method to infer rotor losses. The proposed model using a 3D correction shows good agreement with the test results. This model provides a transparent loss mechanism and is suitable for early-stage design studies where both saturation and diffusion are significant.

title: Suppression of Surge Disturbance for AMB-Supported Hydrogen Circulation Pumps Based on Disturbance Observer
abstract: Magnetically suspended hydrogen circulation pumps (MSHCPs) are highly susceptible to surge, a catastrophic aerodynamic instability that induces severe low-frequency vibrations and threatens rotor stability. This paper proposes a surge disturbance suppression method for the active magnetic bearing (AMB) rotor system based on a frequency-selective disturbance observer. First, an online surge frequency estimation method is proposed using the inherent rotor displacement signal, eliminating the need for additional sensors. Then, by exploiting the narrowband harmonic characteristic of surge disturbance, an exogenous system model is established and integrated with the AMB rotor dynamics to construct a disturbance observer. The relationship between estimation error and observer bandwidth is analyzed, revealing that frequency-selective estimation and accurate compensation can be achieved without excessively increasing the observer bandwidth. Furthermore, a tracking differentiator is employed to obtain the displacement derivative while suppressing noise amplification. Finally, simulation and experimental results validate that, compared with linear active disturbance rejection control, the proposed method provides superior vibration attenuation and maintains effective suppression performance even under frequency estimation errors.

title: Usage of motor windings as oil preheater for air conditioner compressors
abstract: Cost optimization is a key issue for successful competition in today's home appliance markets. Therefore, many manufacturers focus on exclusion of some physical parts or circuits, which allows do decrease cost. However, in order to keep the functionality unchanged, the functions of the excluded parts are implemented using control system. This study focuses on the abovementioned direction and proposes the exclusion of the compressor oil preheater, implemented as a separate unit or circuit. In order to perform preheating, this paper proposes the usage of windings of the electrical motor, which drives the compressor and is located inside its shell. The motor windings are heated by the injected current via an inverter, and transmits the heat energy to the oil inside the compressor. Furthermore, in order to prevent motor rotation this paper recommends injection of DC current. As a result of the proposed technique, the preheater may be excluded, while the device functionality remains unchanged. The proposed manuscript analyses the pros and cons of the proposed substitution, evaluates its operation and compares it with the conventional solution.

title: A Multi-Objective Global Optimization Method for Linear-Rotary PMSM Using an Improved Kriging Model
abstract: To address the challenges of quick optimization of linear-rotary permanent magnet synchronous motor (LRPMSM) due to complicate two-degree-of-freedom(2-DoF) structure, this paper proposes a multi-objective global optimization method with Kriging-assistance. First, the topology structure of LRPMSM is introduced, and a global optimization method based on parameter layering is proposed. By sensitivity analysis, the 9 parameters are stratified into three subspaces. Low-sensitivity 3 parameters are optimized via finite element analysis (FEA) or assigned fixed values, reducing optimization variables by 33.33%. For remaining 6 highly sensitive key parameters, an improved Kriging model is developed, integrating adaptive kernel function selection and Bayesian optimization. With only 400 samples, the accurate surrogate model is obtained, and then the optimization is performed by adopting multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO). Based on the optimized design, the no-load back-EMF and detent force are measured, which are consistent with the predicted results. Experimental results on a prototype confirm the accuracy of the predictions, demonstrating that the proposed method is a fast and effective global optimization framework for complex multi-DoF motors.

title: Adaptive Power Tracking and Control for Single-Stage Solar Water Pumping Systems
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive power tracking and control strategy to address the limitations of conventional voltage-based control in solar water pumping (SWP) systems. Traditional maximum power point tracking (MPPT) methods, such as Perturb and Observe (P&O) and Incremental Conductance (INC), suffer from slow convergence, oscillations, and instability under varying environmental conditions. In particular, these voltage-regulated approaches adjust load power based on photovoltaic (PV) voltage, increasing the risk of convergence to low-voltage conditions where the DC voltage becomes insufficient to sustain motor operation, resulting in excessive power loss or even system failure. To address this, an adaptive power tracking (APT) algorithm is introduced, which directly regulates power to ensure reliable operation and prevent instability. The proposed method adapts power variations based on the nonlinear voltage–current characteristics of the PV system and avoids unstable operating points without additional sensors or complex computations. Experimental results verify that the algorithm achieves fast and accurate MPPT and stable constant power control, while significantly enhancing robustness, improving system stability, and eliminating steady-state oscillations. These findings demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed approach for achieving reliable and energy-efficient SWP system operation.

title: Efficient and Accurate Electromagnetic-Analysis Model for Asymmetric-End Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Motor
abstract: This paper introduces an improved subdomain analytical model to efficiently predict the electromagnetic performance of complex primary-end Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Motors (PMLSMs) under various load conditions. Specifically, the study focuses on a novel slotted single-sided asymmetric-end permanent magnet linear synchronous motor (SSAE-PMLSM). Based on periodic boundary conditions, the motor model is segmented and reconstructed in the tooth region, achieving minimal subdomain division for the complex primary-end structure. The solution process fully leverages the Neumann boundary conditions, significantly reducing computational complexity and enabling rapid, accurate calculation of the SSAE-PMLSM magnetic field. By reversing the reconstructed model and applying the superposition principle, the actual on-load magnetic field distribution is obtained. Then the detent force, thrust force, and back-electromotive force (EMF) are calculated based on magnetic field calculations. Numerical results from finite element methods (FEM) validate the effectiveness of the analytical model. Finally, a prototype of the SSAE-PMLSM was manufactured, and experimental results confirm the accuracy of the developed analytical model in predicting both magnetic fields and forces.

title: A Robust Position Sensor Offset Correction Method Based on Harmonic Current Injection for SPMSM
abstract: The performance of the surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) drive system under the rotor field orientation (RFO) control scheme may significantly deteriorate in the presence of position sensor offset (PSO). To address this problem, first, the effects of the SPMSM drive system under PSO are investigated. Furthermore, a robust online PSO correction method based on d-axis harmonic current injection is proposed. Compared with existing schemes, the proposed scheme is independent of motor parameters so that exhibits high robustness to parametric uncertainties. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by experiments.

title: Physics-Guided Time-Series Generation for High-Fidelity Fault Data Augmentation in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
abstract: The reliability of data-driven fault diagnosis in electric machines is critically constrained by the scarcity and imbalance of real-world fault data. Existing generative models often fail to preserve the temporal coherence, physical consistency, and long-range dependencies that are essential for synthesizing high-fidelity current and voltage signals. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes the Physics-Guided Bidirectional Mamba TimeGAN (PGBi-TimeGAN), a novel framework for generating physically plausible fault data. The framework's core is a custom SEBi-Mamba generator, which employs a bidirectional state-space model to precisely capture complex temporal dynamics and fault signatures. Physical fidelity is enforced through a physics-informed loss function derived from the current imbalance principle of inter-turn short-circuits. Furthermore, a temporal-difference regularization term ensures the generated signals exhibit a natural smoothness, mimicking physical sensor readings. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PGBi-TimeGAN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in generation fidelity, confirmed by Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) metrics. Consequently, the synthetic data enhances downstream classification accuracy for inter-turn short-circuit faults to over 95%, validating the framework's capability to build robust diagnostic models for this specific fault class, especially under challenging industrial conditions involving limited data and significant noise.

title: A Discrete Space Vector Modulation-based Model-Free Predictive Control with Improved Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Observer for Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Machine
abstract: Due to its simple implementation and excellent performance, model predictive control (MPC) is applied to permanent magnet linear synchronous machine (PMLSM) drive systems. However, the selected voltage vector (VV) in conventional MPC has large error and thrust fluctuation. In addition, it also exhibits strong parameter dependency, and mismatched parameters can deteriorate control performance. Thereof, to further improve control performance, a discrete space vector modulation based MPC (DSVM-MPC) strategy is proposed, which redefined the action region of the VV and redesigned the optimal VV search algorithm based on the action region. Compared with conventional methods, the proposed method can obtain more accurate VV under similar computational burden. Moreover, a model free predictive control (MFPC) strategy based on an improved super-twist sliding mode observer (ST-SMO) is designed, which introduces an exponential term in the convergence rate function, not only has higher control accuracy, but also improves convergence speed. To filter out the dc-offset signals in the sampling currents, a two-degree of-freedom (TDF) filter is also designed for DSVM-MFPC. Finally, the superiority of the proposed method is verified through simulations and experiments on the prototype.

title: Multi-stress Aging of Service-Aged and Backup Hydrogenerator Stator Coils Under Load Cycling
abstract: Frequent start-stops in hydrogenerators impose increased thermal, mechanical, and electrical stresses on stator winding insulation, accelerating degradation and potentially leading to failure. To emulate such operating conditions, a multi-stress, single-phase stator-slot model was built to cycle stator coils between 40 and 110****C while simultaneously applying 1.5 times the rated phase-to-ground voltage (${U\_{0}}$). Service-aged and backup coil groups taken from the same hydrogenerator were tested, with partial discharge (PD) recorded during cycling (on-cycle) and off-cycle diagnostics at room temperature, including PD inception voltage, PD measurements at 1.5 $U\_{0}$, and loss tangent. The on-cycle results show distinct aging trajectories: the service-aged coils entered a stable-degradation regime with limited, similar discharge magnitudes during heating and cooling, whereas the backup coils exhibited larger, more frequent discharges, with PD markedly higher during cooling than during heating at the same temperature. Off-cycle measurements indicate similar trends but with lower magnitudes, suggesting that room-temperature tests alone cannot probe multi-stress degradation. The study demonstrates that reliable assessment requires the use of combined on-cycle and off-cycle diagnostics under representative loading conditions.

title: Radial Displacement Sensorless Control of Permanent Magnet Assisted Bearingless Synchronous Reluctance Motor in Full Speed Range
abstract: The displacement sensors utilized in the control system of the permanent magnet assisted bearingless synchronous reluctance motor (PMa-BSynRM) are associated with high cost and low reliability. To address this, this paper proposes a radial displacement sensorless control method in the full speed range. Firstly, the rotor suspension principle is expounded, and the voltage and current equations of the system are derived. Secondly, in the low speed range, the rotor displacement is estimated using high frequency square wave injection (HFSWI) combined with a phase-locked loop (PLL) for accurate signal demodulation. Thirdly, a left inverse observer is constructed using an improved radial basis function (RBF) neural network, and the initial parameters of the neural network are optimized by the weighted mean of vectors algorithm (INFO), ultimately achieving accurate displacement estimation. Furthermore, the transition boundaries between operational modes are determined through deceleration simulation, incorporating a weighted fusion algorithm to guarantee seamless switching across speed regions. Finally, the proposed approach is verified through simulation and comparative experiments. Experimental results demonstrate a maximum steady-state estimation error of 7 μm, while the settling time extends by only 11 ms under external disturbances. Overall, the proposed method exhibits superior estimation precision and robust disturbance rejection capability.

title: Detection Method of Rotor Inter-Turn Short Circuit in Synchronous Generator Based on Leakage Flux of Peripheral Components
abstract: Rotor winding faults in synchronous generators can significantly degrade operational performance, efficiency, and reliability. This study addresses inter-turn short circuit (ITSC) fault detection in synchronous generator rotor windings by analyzing the leakage magnetic fields in peripheral components, which contain fault-related harmonics following ITSC. A detection coil is circumferentially wound on the stator casing to capture these harmonics. A theoretical analysis is conducted to investigate the air gap magnetic field fault characteristics and main magnetic flux leakage mechanism in a salient-pole generator. Finite element simulations of the SAV620/275/18 hydro-generator model reveal the distributions of leakage fields and the evolution of harmonics under fault conditions. Experimental validation using the MJF-30-6 non-salient pole generator confirms the coil’s effectiveness in detecting spillover flux. Both simulation and experimental results show that (k/P)th fractional harmonic amplitudes in induced voltages correlate with fault severity, providing a robust diagnostic criterion.

title: Fault-Tolerant Control Method for Five-phase PMSM with Multi-mode Configuration and Mode Switching Restriction under Single Open-switch fault
abstract: The single open-switch fault is a type of open-circuit fault in electrical machines, which results in the phase current being divided into healthy and fault half cycle, thereby preventing the maintenance of a healthy magnetic field. Based on the motor operation analysis of this fault, this paper proposes a fault tolerant control method for five-phase machine with non-sinusoidal back EMF. A set of multi-mode configuration is proposed to reconstruct a healthy magnetic field distribution in single open-switch fault. It also eliminates the instantaneous torque fluctuations that occur during mode switching between the faulty and healthy half cycle. Besides, the proposed method incorporates both the minimization of copper loss (ML) and the maximization of torque output (MT) as constraints for current reconfiguration, along with their corresponding reconfiguration and derating factors. After the experimental verification, the proposed universal fault-tolerant control method for five-phase motors has the advantages of low torque fluctuation and low copper loss with different constraints.

title: Neural Network-Based Dynamic Modeling of Synchronous Generator Using Data Augmentation
abstract: Synchronous generators (SGs) are the cornerstone of modern power systems. However, achieving accurate dynamic modeling of SGs, particularly when considering their complex nonlinear characteristics, has been a persistent challenge for over a century. Neural networks are a promising alternative for SG dynamic modeling, but their training typically lacks sufficient data. To address this, a neural network-based approach for SG dynamic modeling using data augmentation is proposed. The proposed method employs an improved recurrent neural network (RNN) and a practical two-stage learning strategy. In the data augmentation and initial training stage, comprehensive data augmentation is performed using physics-based simulations for initial training, and the tailored improved RNN architecture further enables the model to effectively learn and capture dynamics that closely align with physical principles. In the measurement-driven fine-tuning stage, scarce real-world measurement data from an in-service generator are used to fine-tune the model, further enhancing its accuracy in real-world operating conditions. Following initial training, the proposed model exhibits generalization ability across diverse fault scenarios, including challenging worst-case and marginal stabilization conditions, accurately replicating physical principles to ensure baseline accuracy and further validating its reliability. Finally, the proposed model achieves a significant relative error reduction compared to the state-of-the-art SG dynamic model, GENQEC, highlighting its potential as a superior alternative for precise SG dynamic representation.

title: Induction Machine Equivalent Circuit With a Tunable Core Loss Resistance Location and its Offline Parameter Identification Method
abstract: An equivalent circuit incorporating the core loss is important for accurate analysis of induction machines(IMs). This paper proposes a novel IM equivalent circuit with an extra degree of freedom, which allows the location of the core loss resistance to be adjusted. By tuning the core loss resistance location, two mostly-used existing IM equivalent circuits can be regarded as special cases of the proposed model. To facilitate accurate parameter identification, a stator flux linkage controller is designed to maintain constant amplitude and frequency of the stator flux linkage during experiments. Based on this constraint, the stator current locus is derived and used to identify the location of the core loss resistance and other parameters offline. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed equivalent circuit with identified parameters can accurately predict the states of the induction machine across a wide range of operating conditions.

title: Modeling and Experimental Approaches for Diagnosis of Magnet Defect in External Rotor Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Motor
abstract: This paper proposes an analytical model to assess the specific impact of a complete demagnetization fault affecting two adjacent permanent-magnets, influencing various parameters of an external rotor permanent-magnet synchronous motor. This work aims to provide a comprehensive assessment of the machine's condition, identify failure levels, and offer valuable information for diagnosis, monitoring, and predictive maintenance through the identification of sensitive harmonics. The model is further validated by 2D finite element simulations and by analysis based on experimental results under healthy and faulty conditions. It validates and demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach to fault detection and diagnosis, thus providing a solid basis for potential implementation in the industrial application. The proposed analytical model significantly reduces computation time while maintaining adequate accuracy, and so facilitating magnet fault simulation.

title: Analytical Calculation of an Axial Flux Multi-Rotor Magnetic Gear Generator and Analysis of Its Harmonic Speed-Up Effect
abstract: In order to solve the problem of low power density of traditional wave energy converters (WECs) due to low wave frequency and low speed, a multi-port magnetic field modulation axial flux generator (MPMFM-AFG) for WECs is proposed. The three-dimensional structure and working principle are introduced. Based on the proposed analytical method, the harmonic components of the air gap flux density before modulation and after modulation are calculated and analyzed. The accuracy of the analytical model was verified by the finite element method (FEM). The no-load back EMF, static torque, flux density, loss and efficiency of the proposed MPMFM-AFG are calculated. Compared with the existing WECs, the proposed MPMFM-AFG can achieve higher power density at lower linear speed. The experimental results and calculation results are compared and analyzed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed MPMFM-AFG and the accuracy of the calculation method.

title: A 3-D Equivalent Magnetic Network Model for Performance Analysis of Modular Permanent Magnet Claw Pole Machines with Spliced Air Gaps
abstract: Due to the small size of the spliced air gap caused by modular design, it is time-consuming to predict the performance of modular permanent magnet claw pole machines (MPMCPM) by using finite element method. Therefore, a three-dimensional equivalent magnetic network (3-D EMN) model is proposed to predict the performance of MPMCPM with spliced air gaps in this paper. First, the permeance calculation methods for different 3-D mesh cells are presented. By using these specific mesh cells, permeances of claw pole meshes can be accurately calculated. Second, hexahedron meshes are laid out in areas with severe leakage flux, then leakage magnetic fields can be considered and the accuracy of the model can be improved. The high accuracy of the proposed 3-D EMN model is verified by comparing with finite element results and experiments conducted on a small-scale prototype machine. Meanwhile, the core loss is calculated and the influence of the rotating magnetic field on claw poles is also taken into account. Finally, the influence of spliced air gaps with different lengths on the performance of MPMCPM is predicted by adding spliced air gap permeances to the 3-D EMN model.

title: An Efficient Data Generation Method Based on Flow Matching for Bearing Fault Diagnosis Under Imbalanced Data Conditions
abstract: The process of fault diagnosis is greatly constrained by imbalanced datasets, as a lack of fault data results in models with poor diagnostic performance. To overcome this issue, generative adversarial networks (GANs) have been utilized. However, they often suffer from training instability and are prone to mode collapse, where this critical issue causes the generator to produce a very limited variety of outputs. Consequently, this article proposes an efficient data augmentation framework based on flow matching for the domain of bearing fault diagnosis under imbalanced data. First, the continuous wavelet transform of vibration signals is employed to train a conditional flow matching model. After training, the model can generate new synthetic data by transforming a random Gaussian noise vector into a high-fidelity time–frequency spectrum. A key advantage of this approach is its computational efficiency, where the model produces diverse and authentic samples with as few as 5-15 generation steps, significantly reducing the generation time compared to traditional diffusion models. Furthermore, to comprehensively evaluate the diversity and fidelity of synthesized samples, various evaluation techniques, such as kernel inception distance (KID), the GAN-test/GAN-train metric and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) visualizations of the learned feature space, are employed. Ultimately, a series of imbalanced fault diagnosis experiments was conducted to validate the practical effectiveness of the proposed method, resulting in final diagnosis accuracies of 95.90% and 97.31% on two widely used datasets and 98.81% on an actual test bed.

title: A Precise Nonlinear Eddy-Current Magnetic Network Model for the Analysis of Electromagnetic Buffer
abstract: In this paper, a precise nonlinear eddy-current magnetic network (PNEMN) model is proposed to analyze the performance of the cylindrical permanent magnet (PM) electromagnetic buffer (EB). In this EB, the permanent magnet is radially magnetized and separated by iron teeth. When the EB is working, intense eddy currents are induced, severely distorting the original magnetic field, so that conventional magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) models can no longer provide an accurate solution. To solve this problem, this paper adopted refined magnetic reluctance elements and incorporated eddy currents into the magnetic network model, fully coupling them with the original magnetic field. The convergence of this method is discussed in detail. To make this model more comprehensive, nonlinear magnetic saturation, end effects, and slot effects have also been taken into account. Optimal computational efficiency is achieved by judiciously selecting boundary conditions. A finite element model and the experiments on a prototype were built to verify the accuracy of the proposed model. Finally, the operating characteristics of the eddy current brake are analyzed, and its critical speed is about 7.5 m/s.

title: Dynamic Current Control Strategy of Grid-Connected Voltage Source Converters Feeding Constant Power Loads for Transient Stability Enhancement
abstract: The negative impedance characteristic of constant power loads (CPLs) can destabilize grid-connected voltage source converters (VSCs) by introducing positive feedback loops. To this end, this paper proposes a dynamic current control strategy for grid-connected VSCs with CPLs to enhance system transient synchronous stability (TSS). Firstly, a nonlinear phase-locked loop dynamic model is developed for VSCs. It explicitly incorporates the CPL impact, which indicates CPLs introduce coupling between the d-axis and q-axis components of VSC terminal voltage, and a positive feedback loop in VSC control scheme. Secondly, equal area criterion and phase-portrait analysis are used for qualitative and quantitative analysis to assess the CPL impact on TSS, respectively. The findings indicate the impact is related to the VSC output current. Therefore, a dynamic current control strategy for VSCs is proposed. It adds the current compensation term to neutralize CPL-induced destabilizing effects, guaranteeing the existence of stable equilibrium points that ensure both TSS and CPLs operation at rated power under grid faults. Meanwhile, a simple and fast VSC capacity calculation method is proposed. It can accurately calculate the required VSC capacity for achieving the above control objectives. Finally, simulation and experimental comparisons with existing methods verify the validity of the proposed strategy.

title: A dv/dt Output Filter for Mitigating Motor Terminal Overvoltage in SiC-based Motor Drive Systems
abstract: The Silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFET, as a prominent wide bandgap device, is extensively used in motor drive systems due to its high-speed switching characteristic. However, higher dv/dt will cause overvoltage at the motor terminals, accelerate the aging of windings and bearings, seriously threaten the insulation of motor windings, and shorten the service life of the motor. To address the critical challenge, this paper proposes a novel third-order LCRL dv/dt filter topology, which introduces parallel inductance to improve the flexibility of cable matching and shunts damping resistors to reduce damping loss, thereby significantly reducing the volume and cost of the heat sink. A parameter design method suitable for high-order filters and a multi-dimensional design optimization strategy based on the optimal loss model are proposed to simultaneously find the best solution to minimize motor terminal overvoltage and total system loss, providing theoretical guidance for the application of high-order dv/dt filters. A series of experimental results demonstrate that the motor terminal overvoltage, damping loss, and volume of the proposed filter are reduced by 81.5%, 43.7%, and 33.3%, respectively, compared with the conventional LCR filter, which improves motor reliability in high-speed switching applications without compromising system efficiency.

title: Two-Switching-Sequence PWM-Based Simple Three-Phase Current Reconstruction Strategy for Single DC-Link Shunt PMSM Drives
abstract: This paper proposes a novel two-switching-sequence pulse width modulation (TSSPWM) strategy to solve the current reconstruction dead zone (CRDZ) problem for single DC-link shunt permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drives. The switch conduction sequence and voltage vector synthesis principles of TSSPWM are first analyzed, which is different from the existing methods. TSSPWM contains measured voltage vectors and compensated voltage vectors in one switching period. It has symmetric PWM and mid-cycle current sampling structure. Based on the current error analysis, the phase currents reconstructed using this structure are close to the average current of a PWM cycle. Then, the implementation and CRDZ of TSSPWM are also provided. Since TSSPWM only applies one strategy to different CRDZs, it has the characteristics of small memory footprint and fast running speed. Finally, the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is lighter, faster and simpler than other methods under various operating conditions.

title: Comprehensive Switching-Gain-Based Sliding Mode Control of PMSM Subject to Fast Time-Varying Disturbances
abstract: To accelerate the dynamic convergence speed of the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) control system and enhance its ability to resist fast time-varying disturbances, a novel sliding mode control method is proposed by constructing switching gain with the system state information and environment information. Firstly, employing the extended state observer (ESO) to estimate and compensate for low-frequency disturbance, thereby effectively reducing the upper bound of disturbance impacting the system. Secondly, the fuzzy system is constructed by using the rate of speed error change and high-frequency disturbance change. The fuzzy system output and the estimate of high-frequency disturbance generate adjustable switching gain, which ensures disturbances is suppressed in time and the small chattering amplitude when the system is running dynamically. The stability of the system is proved by using the Lyapunov theory and the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by numerical simulations and platform experiments.

title: Admittance Reshaping Method for Charging Current Ripple Suppression of the Battery Energy Storage System under Distorted Grid Conditions
abstract: Grid voltage background harmonics can induce harmonic currents in the energy storage converter (ESC). Furthermore, the frequency-coupling characteristic of the battery energy storage system (BESS), which induces new harmonic current components, can result in current ripple during battery charging. This paper proposes an admittance-reshaping method to mitigate the influence of grid background harmonics on the battery charging current of the BESS. Firstly, the small-signal admittance model of the ESC is established. Then, a theoretical analysis and mathematical derivation of the charging current ripple are conducted. The general forms of the inner current-control loop and outer power-control loop admittance-reshaping factors are then developed to reshape the admittance model into a symmetrical system within the dq frame, as a result, the harmonic components are reduced. Furthermore, the admittance-reshaping factors' parameters are appropriately selected to reduce the magnitude of harmonics. By decoupling the system and lowering the admittance value of the ESC, the quality of the grid-connected current is improved, while simultaneously suppressing the charging current ripple. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed admittance-reshaping method are verified by the presented simulation and experimental results.

title: Development of a Novel Bistable Self-Holding Electromagnetic Actuator with Low Power Consumption for Electric Directional Valves
abstract: This paper presents a fixed magnet bistable electromagnetic actuator (FMBEA) with low power consumption for electric directional valves. The mover's self-holding capability is achieved by the magnet fixed on the stator, thereby eliminating the need for holding excitation. Thus, the energy consumption typically required to maintain the mover position in conventional solenoid actuators is effectively eliminated. In addition, the armature flux does not pass through the magnet during switching process, thereby effectively preventing irreversible demagnetization caused by the strong electromagnetic field. Furthermore, the multi-segment composite air-gap topology increases the equivalent working area within a confined space, thereby enhancing the output force density. Firstly, the structure and operating principle of the FMBEA are presented. Then, an equivalent magnetic-circuit model is established by considering leakage flux and the magnetic saturation of soft magnetic materials. Subsequently, a multi-objective optimization method based on the analytical model is implemented to comprehensively improve the output force density and reduce power consumption. Finally, a prototype based on the optimized design is manufactured and tested. The experimental results validate the proposed design and the analytical method.

title: Magnetic-Flux Balance Control to Eliminate Voltage Deviation on Split Phase Capacitor for 4-DOF Bearingless SRM
abstract: The four degrees of freedom (4-DOF) 12/4 bearingless switched reluctance motor (BSRM) generally requires 48 power devices, 24 current sensors, and 2 microchips to simultaneously achieve rotation and levitation. To reduce the number of power devices and sensors used in the system, a split-phase converter and a multiplexed-sensor method are employed. However, significant voltage deviation occurs on the two split-phase capacitors due to the inconsistent levitation currents, which deteriorates the levitation performance. Therefore, this paper proposes a magnetic-flux balance control (MFBC) method to solve this problem. The method constrains the total current of all windings in each phase to form a balanced bias magnetic flux. By balancing the discharge depth of the two split-phase capacitors, voltage deviation is eliminated and stable levitation operation is ensured. Moreover, an improved multiplexed-sensor method is developed to enhance levitation stability at high speeds. Finally, the demonstrated performance of the proposed scheme is verified on a test rig of a 4-DOF 12/4 BSRM-type magnetic levitation system.

title: Three-Dimensional Thermal and Stress Analysis of Synchronous Reluctance Motor by an Improved Hybrid Method
abstract: While various methods accurately and efficiently address motor thermal and stress analyses separately, effectively solving this dual field problem for complex rotor structures in synchronous reluctance motors (SynRMs) remains challenging. This work presents an improved hybrid method (HM) for comprehensive three-dimensional thermal and rotor stress performance prediction in SynRMs. The proposed improved HM integrates the improved finite difference method (IFDM), subdomain method (SDM), and lumped parameter thermal networks (LPTNs). The key advantages of the proposed improved HM are fourfold: First, incorporating the variable density method into the IFDM eliminates inner boundary conditions, simplifying rotor dual-field computation. Second, integrating the SDM and LPTN significantly enhances the accuracy and efficiency of three-dimensional thermal field calculations, particularly facilitating solutions for axially asymmetric thermal performance. Third, leveraging steady-state temperatures from the improved HM enables rapid prediction of transient temperature characteristics. Fourth, the improved HM uniquely solves coupled dual fields using a unified model, streamlining computational procedures. Finite element analysis and prototype testing validate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed improved HM, demonstrating over 90% improvement in computational efficiency, especially for transient thermal prediction.

title: PLL-Free Approach: Reactive Power-Based Synchronization in Grid-Following Inverters
abstract: The rapid growth in inverter-based resource penetration is leading to the widespread integration of grid-following and grid-forming inverters within ac grids. Despite their distinct operational characteristics, these two inverter modes share fundamental similarities, motivating joint investigations into their attributes. Building on the identified symmetry between these devices, this paper proposes a novel phase-locked loop-free grid-following control strategy inspired by the grid-forming control architecture. The proposed approach simplifies the grid-following inverter control structure while retaining its inherent capabilities and enabling the intuitive configuration of synchronous inertia and damping. Analytical, experimental, and simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

title: Global Fast Control for Finite-Time Consensus in Multi-Linear Motor Systems
abstract: Position and speed inconsistencies of multi-linear motor systems (M-LMS) may lead to uneven load distribution, low collaborative precision, and even failure to achieve the preset motion planning. We propose an observer-based finite time consensus control protocol, aimed at realizing global fast consensus for M-LMS. Specifically, a finite-time disturbance observer (FTDO) is designed to estimate unknown disturbances in M-LMS, and incorporate it into the subsequent protocol design. Then, the protocol employs the global fast cooperative terminal sliding mode control (GFCTSMC) algorithm with the super twisting reaching law. Methods based on linear sliding surfaces can only guarantee the asymptotic convergence of the consensus error in M-LMS. In contrast, the proposed protocol improves the cooperative precision of M-LMS and ensures that the consensus error can converge within a finite time. Experimental results on consensus cooperative control of M-LMS demonstrate that, in comparison with the representative approaches, the consensus error index of this method is reduced by 95% and 64% on average, respectively.

title: Robust Diagnosis Method for Open-Circuit Faults in Wind Power System Converters With Special Attention to Wind Speed Fluctuations
abstract: This paper proposes a robust fault diagnosis framework for open-circuit faults (OCF) in wind power converters, focusing on addressing the impact of two major challenges on fault diagnosis: wind speed fluctuations (induced by tower shadow effects, wind shear, and complex environmental conditions) and noise interference. The key contributions of this paper include: 1) A real-time current amplitude normalization (RCAN) mechanism using Park transformation for dynamic signal correction, 2) A wind-adaptive sampling (WAS) strategy for synchronized data acquisition, and 3) A novel hybrid deep learning architecture combining improved Gated Recurrent Neural Network (IGRNN) for temporal analysis and Markov Transfer Field Residual Network (MTF-ResNet) for spatial feature extraction. The method processes RCAN normalized three-phase current through WAS sampling, followed by parallel temporal-spatial feature extraction via IGRNN and MTF-ResNet branches. An attention mechanism integrates these features for final fault classification. Experimental results demonstrate significant performance improvements, achieving over 97% accuracy at 10 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) under fluctuating wind conditions, outperforming conventional approaches in reliability and robustness.

title: A Novel Hybrid Model for Magnetic Field Analysis of Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines Combining Subdomain Methods and Simplified Magnetic Equivalent Circuits
abstract: Axial flux permanent magnet synchronous motor (AFPMSM) exhibit broad application prospects due to its advantages of high torque density and high efficiency, and compact structure. However, the existing analytical models for the magnetic field analysis of AFPMSMs suffer from unsatisfactory generality. In this paper, a novel subdomain and magnetic equivalent network (MEC) hybrid model is proposed for the magnetic field analysis of AFPMSMs considering magnetic saturation. Firstly, the model adopts a tooth-pitch segment as the fundamental unit and iteratively solves the simplified MEC under magnetic saturation conditions to determine the magnetic flux from both permanent magnet remanence and armature current, thereby obtaining the air gap magnetic flux density. Secondly, finite element analysis is performed on two motors to validate the proposed hybrid model, showing that it significantly reduces errors in the axial magnetic flux density under heavy magnetic saturation. Prototype experiments verify the accuracy of the proposed hybrid model in calculating back EMF and torque. In summary, the proposed model features high accuracy and strong generality, offering an efficient computational approach for magnetic field analysis and performance optimization of AFPMSMs.

title: Low-Speed Active Disturbance Rejection Control Based on Disturbance Foresight Compensation for Multi-Unit Distributed Permanent Magnet Arc Motor
abstract: This article proposes a model predictive speed control with disturbance foresight compensation (DFC-MPSC) based on generalized proportional integral iterative learning observer (GILO) to reduce the speed fluctuation caused by periodic end torque, cogging torque and flux harmonics existing in multi-unit distributed permanent magnet arc motor (arc motor). A novel position- and velocity-based iterative learning law has been developed and extended to the general form of a generalized proportional integral observer. Compared to existing observers, this approach effectively addresses the trade-off between high-frequency periodic disturbance observation and noise suppression. Its higher-order formulation, based on the position equation, significantly reduces the impact of speed measurement noise on observation accuracy, particularly at low speeds. GILO can also improve the observation performance of the generalized proportional integral observer for periodic disturbances in sinusoidal form. Theoretical analysis has verified the stability of GILO. Iterative learning can record periodic disturbance sequences, therefore the observations of disturbances and their future performance can be embedded into the prediction model according to the prediction horizon, which enhances the steady-state and dynamic performance of MPSC, especially at very low speed. The comparatively experimental results have validated the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

title: Multi-Source Energy Management in a Grid-Synchronized Bi-Directional EV Charging Architecture With Error-Modified Adaptive Control
abstract: This paper presents a robust error-modified (E-Mod) adaptive tracking control algorithm designed for fundamental grid frequency estimation and multi-resonant direct power control, which regulates bi-directional EV charging operations under distorted grid voltage conditions. The non-linear phase and frequency detection algorithm self-updates with each analog signal sample, ensuring rapid reference command tracking even in the presence of grid non-idealities. The algorithm’s robust and stable controller enhances the charging profile by reducing DC offset error, switching noise, harmonic distortion, and sensor measurement error. The resonant control architecture incorporates both phase and frequency information at dominant harmonic multiples, enabling regulated EV charging with unity power factor (UPF) in resilient grid conditions. A linear state model with current-regulated phase-shift operation facilitates DC-DC power conversion for variable battery charging. The phase-shift operation in the second stage is updated by equivalent voltage feed-forward compensation to improve EV charging dynamics. The charging architecture and related control implementation are designed, simulated, and validated using a laboratory prototype of a 3.3 kW Level-I bi-directional EV charger.

title: Interturn Short-Circuit Fault Diagnosis of A BLDC Hub Motor Via Graph Neural Networks with Multiscale Feature Distillation
abstract: Brushless DC motors (BLDCMs) have become the preferred choice for hub motor drives because of their high efficiency, high power density, and excellent speed–torque characteristics. As latent faults in motors, interturn short circuits (ITSCs) cause the spatial electromagnetic distribution to exhibit differential responses, which leads to scattered electromagnetic information distribution and excessive redundant information, and poses challenges for state assessment. These issues are addressed in this study by proposing a multiscale feature distillation-based graph neural network (MSFD-GNN) architecture for noninvasive online diagnosis of ITSC. First, the correlation between leakage magnetic signals and winding states under ITSC is analyzed by establishing an equivalent magnetic circuit model and incorporating finite element analysis. Second, spatially dispersed multichannel leakage magnetic signals are transformed into information-dense electromagnetic field feature maps by integrating recursive phase space reconstruction techniques. The designed MSFD module subsequently performs adaptive refinement and enhancement of fault features, followed by cascading GNNs to learn global topological features by aggregating node neighborhood information. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively identifies the severity and location of ITSC faults, achieving a comprehensive diagnostic accuracy of 99.62% across multiple operating conditions.

title: Design of a 2/6-Pole Combined Pitch Wound Rotor Brushless Doubly-Fed Generator and its Comparative Study with an 8-Pole Doubly-Fed Induction Generator
abstract: The brushless doubly-fed generator (BDFG) is especially well-suited for constant-frequency, constant-voltage power generation in small hydropower plants utilizing variable speed hydraulic turbines. This paper presents a novel wound rotor design that combines long and short pitch coils to consider both the power winding (PW) and control winding (CW) pole pair pitches selection, thereby improving the chording factors and enhancing the overall winding factors through harmonic analysis. First, this study investigates the rotor speed regulation characteristics, analyzes the composition and magnitude of the radial electromagnetic forces density under harmonic-free condition, presents the stator PW and CW connection methods. Subsequently, the principle of employing combined pitch coils is elaborated to further increase conductor utilization and mitigate harmonic contents. A practical design example for 1/3 pole-pair is provided, including detailed implementation steps, along with a comparative analysis of coupling coefficients across different rotor configurations. Furthermore, finite element (FE) analysis of the 2/6-pole BDFG and 8-pole doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) with identical frame sizes are conducted to evaluate the difference in operational characteristics of the generators under the same load and rotor speed range. Finally, the experimental results validate the superiority of the proposed 2/6-pole BDFG rotor design across diverse loads and speeds.

title: Nonlinear loss-minimizing control of induction motors with inherent constraint satisfaction
abstract: In this paper, a novel nonlinear loss-minimizing control structure is proposed for induction motors that achieves field-oriented operation and minimization of the total copper and iron motor losses at the steady state, while inherently guaranteeing the required operating constraints (current and voltage). Opposed to the conventional loss-minimizing controllers that require the solution of a complex optimization problem and the continuous (online) update of the current reference values depending on the operating constraints, the proposed nonlinear loss-minimizing control (NLMC) introduces a novel structure that inherently limits the motor current and voltage inside the desired constraint set and requires the solution of a simplified optimization problem offline. Using nonlinear system theory (ultimate boundedness, vector field and invariant set theory), the boundedness of the motor currents and the entire constraint satisfaction are analytically proven for the proposed NLMC application, followed by a detailed closed-loop system stability analysis. In order to verify the theoretical contribution, the proposed NLMC is directly compared to the well-established field-oriented control and the conventional loss-minimizing control, using a digital Typhoon HIL real-time simulator and an experimental setup of a 1.5 kW Leroy Somer induction motor with varying speed reference and load torque values. Both the real-time simulation and the experimental procedure prove the NLMC capability of regulating the motor speed under speed reference values and torque load changes, while it achieves a minimum losses operation with inherent constraints satisfaction, by utilizing a simpler optimization problem.

title: Winding Arrangement and Performance Analyses of a Reverse-Salient Series I-Λ-Magnetic-Pole Variable-Flux Machine
abstract: With the advantages of good magnetization-manipulation ability and torque-output capability, the reverse- salient series I-Λ-magnetic-pole variable-flux machine (RSSIΛ-VFM) is considered as the candidate for electric machine field. In this paper, the magnetization-manipulation principle of RSSIΛ-VFM is introduced. The influence of winding arrangement of the machine on stator MMF is analyzed, by which the selection principle of pole-slot match is given. The influences of magnetization-state variation on the back electromotive force, inductance and electromagnetic torque are researched, and the relationship between inductance and distribution of d-axis magnetic field is investigated. The variation law of reverse-salient ratio of the machine is analyzed, and then the efficiency characteristics at different magnetization states are discussed. Finally, the prototype of RSSIΛ-VFM is manufactured, and the experiment is carried out to validate the theoretical analysis.

title: Impact of Shielding Configurations with Magnetic-Electrically Conductive Alloy on Multi-Physical Fields in the End Region of Air-Cooled Synchronous Condenser
abstract: In large-capacity air-cooled synchronous condensers (ACSCs) operating under deep leading-phase conditions, significant end leakage flux induces substantial losses and heating in the stator end components. Effective electromagnetic shielding is therefore a critical design consideration and a novel shielding configuration utilizing magnetic-electrical conductive alloys is proposed in this article. Using a 300 MVar ACSC as a case study, the three-dimensional transient electromagnetic field model of the end region is first established. The effects of four configurations (copper shield+magnetic shield, Fe-16%Cu alloy shield+magnetic shield, single Fe-20%Cu alloy shield, and single magnetic shield) on the leakage flux density and losses in end components are analyzed. Subsequently, a global ventilation network and a fluid-thermal coupling model for the end region are developed for each configuration. The results from network and aforementioned losses serve as boundary conditions for the fluid-thermal coupling model. The flow fields and the temperature distributions under different configurations are then determined. The findings demonstrate that each shielding configuration exhibits specific advantages and limitations. Experimental validation based on traditional scheme confirms the accuracy of the model and methodology. The simulation results elucidate the significant potential of the Fe-Cu alloy. The single Fe-20%Cu configuration reduces the hot-spot temperature of shield, and significantly lowers weight and cost while effectively protecting the end iron core.
