title: A Deadbeat Model Predictive Control of PMSM Drives for Eliminating Common Mode Voltage Spikes and Minimizing Switching Frequency
abstract: Deadbeat- based model predictive control (DB-MPC) with traditional space vector modulation (SVM) strategy is commonly applied in motor drives. Traditional SVM utilizes zero vectors, which generate large common-mode voltage (CMV). To reduce the amplitude of CMV, various modified SVM strategies that do not utilize zero vectors have been put forward in literature, and some of them can further eliminate CMV spikes caused by dead-time effect. However, with these modified SVM strategies, the switching frequency of the power devices is relatively high, which leads to large power losses. In this paper, a DB-MPC method with an enhanced SVM is proposed. A vector sequencing rule is established by analyzing the vector switching, the internal area of the vector hexagon is dynamically divided, and the optimal vector sequence with the least number of switching actions and no CMV spikes is selected. The advantage of the proposed method is that the switching frequency of the inverter is minimized on the premise of eliminating the CMV spikes. Experiments verified the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Analysis and Improvement of Reliability of Surface-Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Based on Subdivision Subdomain Models
abstract: The reliability of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) has become a crucial indicator for measuring their comprehensive performance. The existing researches on motor reliability analysis and improvement mainly focus on the study of a single reliability index, and the analysis mainly relies on time-consuming finite element method (FEM). Moreover, considering the global optimization of multiple physical properties of motors is tedious and irreversible demagnetization of permanent magnets (PMs) is often overlooked. In response to the shortcomings of existing researches, a precise analytical method (AM) for multiple reliability indicators of surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motors (SPMSMs) based on subdivision subdomain models is innovatively proposed in this paper, the key reliability indicators of SPMSMs, including irreversible demagnetization of PMs, torque ripple, and electromagnetic vibration, are comprehensively predicted, and the rapidity and accuracy of reliability analysis can be balanced. Compared with FEM, the proposed AM reduces the calculation time by about 93.75% while ensuring calculation accuracy. Afterwards, a multi-objective global analytical optimization model that combines particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm with proposed precise AM is established, and the optimal structural parameters of eccentric PMs that can effectively improve the reliability of SPMSMs are quickly determined, which provides a fast, accurate, convenient, and universal analysis method for the comprehensive improvement of multi physical properties. Finally, both finite element simulation and prototype testing results have demonstrated the accuracy of the proposed AM and the rationality of the optimization results.

title: High-Frequency Motor Models for Capacitively and Inductively Coupled Bearing Voltages: Comparison of a Model With and Without Considering the Inductance for Zero Sequence Components
abstract: The common mode voltage present at the output of the inverter causes bearing voltages through a capacitive or an inductive coupling path, which in turn can result in damaging bearing currents. Accurate high-frequency motor models able to predict both of these coupling paths are required for a proper system design. This paper proposes a new high-frequency motor model for capacitively and inductively coupled bearing voltages. The model comes in two versions: the first model considers the difference in inductance experienced by zero sequence components compared to positive or negative sequence components while the second model neglects this difference. A hybrid method to fit the motor parameters from impedance measurements is proposed, and the resulting impedances are compared to measured impedances. The models are validated by comparing the simulated bearing voltage to measurements on two different setups: an inverter-cable-motor setup and a pulse generator setup. It is shown that including the difference in inductance for zero sequence components compared to positive or negative sequence components improves the impedance match at lower frequencies and the resonance frequency for common mode signals and allows a more accurate simulation of high-frequency oscillations in the bearing voltage. However, to include the difference in inductance an additional impedance measurement that requires access to the neutral point of the motor is required, which is not always possible.

title: Short-Fault Diagnosis Method for CSI-Fed PMSM Drives Based on Dual-Scale Average Current Errors
abstract: This paper proposes a robust short-circuit fault diagnosis method based on dual-scale average current errors for the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive fed by the current source inverter (CSI). The method only employs the already exist motor currents and does not need additional sensors and circuits, which is simple and easy to implement. The current errors between the average values of the reference currents and that of the feedback currents in one cycle are calculated, and the ratios of the errors to the average absolute values of the reference currents are used as the diagnostic variables. In addition, two amplitude thresholds are set to determine the fault type by comparing the diagnostic variables with the amplitude thresholds. Then, the faulty switch is located according to the signs of the diagnostic variables. In order to avoid misdiagnosis in the transient processes, a time threshold as the second scale is set to enhance the robustness of the diagnostic algorithm. Finally, an experimental platform is built to verify the effectiveness and the robustness of the proposed diagnosis method.

title: Development of a Moving-Coil Linear PM Machine With Improved Thrust Profile Employing a Double-Sided Misaligned Hybrid Topology
abstract: High-performance servo instruments, such as mobile platforms of semiconductor lithography and galvo laser scanning systems, generally require high thrust force, low thrust ripple and low system mass of linear PM machines to improve the loading capability, position precision and dynamic performance of these servo instruments. However, most existing technologies of reducing thrust ripple generally result in the decreaseof thrust force. In this paper, a coreless moving-coil linear PM machine with double-sided misaligned hybrid (DSMH) topology consisting of two asymmetric-arranged hybrid magnet patterns is proposed to meet these requirements. The asymmetric combination of double-sided misaligned magnets with unequal width in the topology helps to enhance the air-gap flux density, while achieving approximately sinusoidal air-gap magnetic field and low thrust ripple. Firstly, the schematic structure and working principle of the DSMH linear machine are presented. Secondly, analytical models of air-gap magnetic field and thrust fore considering the irregular boundary condition of the hybrid magnet patterns are formulated. Then, the influence of the structural parameters on the output performance of the moving-coil linear machine is analyzed through the models, and one DSMH linear machine is designed. Thirdly, to confirm the merits of the DSMH machine, the quantitative electromagnetic performance of the proposed linear machine is compared with that of conventional designs typically used in servo instruments. Finally, one research prototype and two test-rigs are developed, and the experimental measurements of air-gap flux density, thrust force and ripple of the prototype are implemented to validate the design concept of the DSMH linear machine well.

title: S-Parameters as a Basis for Stator Model Parameter Extraction and SFRA Interpretation
abstract: Sweep Frequency Response Analysis (SFRA) is a widely used method for assessing the mechanical and electrical integrity of transformers and is increasingly applied to electrical rotating machines. To support fault diagnosis based on SFRA, a machine-specific model is required that captures the relevant physical behaviour. Up to now the parametrisation of this model is partly done with individual iterative curve fitting, for which a deep understanding of the machine and its parameters is necessary. A method exclusively based on measurements and calculation would help to overcome this need for expert knowledge. This paper introduces a measurement-based approach to parametrise a grey-box stator model using scattering parameters (S-parameters), where the parameters are derived analytically from measured data. The relationship between SFRA and S-parameters is analysed theoretically and experimentally and a conversion to derive the frequency response from S-parameter measurements is presented. The parameter extraction method is applied to three stators and verified through simulation and measurement. The results show that the SFRA response can be reproduced in simulation with a comparable accuracy to previous methods while significantly improving reproducibility and transparency. The approach offers a reliable foundation for model-based SFRA interpretation and future fault identification.

title: Impedance Variations in Random Wound Coils of Synchronous Motors: A Statistical Approach
abstract: Differential and Common Mode impedance characterization plays a crucial role in predicting Electromagnetic Interferences prediction in electric power drives. This paper illustrates, through direct impedance measurements, that random wound coils can exhibit notable impedance differences, even among coils manufactured under similar parameters, due to inconsistencies inherent in the winding process. Predictive impedance modeling combined with wire placement simulations is utilized to analyze the variability in randomly wound coils. The findings demonstrate that winding randomness significantly contributes to impedance uncertainties, while also confirming that wire placement follows non-fully stochastic patterns, likely influenced by repeatable aspects of the manufacturing process. To analyze further the influence of design parameters, the authors propose an approach using statistical repartition of impedances. This method allows quantifying the impact of studied design variables, considering initial variations present in studied samples. This paper aims at giving a better understanding of overall interactions induced by coils design parameters on a broad frequency spectrum for random wound motors.

title: Suspension Internal Model Control With Active Ripple Rejection of Single-Winding Bearingless Flux Switching Permanent Magnet Motor
abstract: Single-winding bearingless flux switching permanent magnet motor (BFSPMM), characterized by its frictionless operation, maintenance-free nature, and high efficiency, holds the potential to fundamentally address the issues of bearing erosion and failure in marine propulsion motors caused by harsh oceanic environments. However, the torque and suspension forces are strongly coupled, and the radial forces are complex and variable, resulting in significant rotor displacement ripples that severely impact the performance of electric drive systems. Herein, a suspension internal model control strategy with active ripple suppression is proposed. Firstly, based on the magnetic field modulation theory, the mechanism of unbalanced magnetic pull is analyzed in detail, and the corresponding expressions are established. Then, a rotor dynamic model is derived from the differential equations of a whirl for the suspended rotor, which facilitates the construction of the BFSPMM internal model. A linear extended state observer is employed to obtain smoother displacement error signals, differential signals, and account for unmodeled dynamics. Subsequently, an inverse system model for the controllable suspension force is derived, and the internal model controller is formulated and analyzed in an innovative PD-based structure. This approach not only enhances the controller’s performance but also simplifies the tuning process, requiring only two parameters to be adjusted. Finally, the performance of the proposed method is analyzed theoretically, and its effectiveness is validated through experimental verification.

title: Two-Stage Variable Universe Fuzzy Model-Free Sliding Mode Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Double-Power-Combination Reaching Law
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the parameter variation and external load disturbance of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) lead to the decrease of system control performance in actual operation, a two-stage variable universe fuzzy (TSVUF) model-free sliding mode control method of PMSM based on double-power-combination reaching law (DPCRL) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a new ultra-local model of the motor speed loop is established according to the mathematical model of the PMSM under parameter perturbation. Secondly, a model-free double-power-combination reaching law sliding mode controller (MFDPSMC) for the speed loop is designed, and a TSVUF extended sliding mode disturbance observer (ESMDO) is designed to observe the unknown part of the ultra-local model, and the observed value is used to compensate the system. The TSVUF control method is used to dynamically adjust the reaching law gain of the ESMDO, which improves the observation performance of the observer. Finally, the experimental results show that the proposed control method effectively improves the response speed and anti-interference ability of the system.

title: Research on Analytical Method of Parasitic Capacitance in Motor Windings Considering Impact of Distributed Disorder
abstract: The equivalent parasitic capacitance (Cp) of motor windings causes the voltage/current overshoot and ringing during the switching of wide-bandgap semiconductor devices. Therefore, it is necessary to model and calculate Cp to evaluate its impact on the switching devices. However, due to the winding deviations and spatial constraints of the slots, the arrangement of coils is disordered. Using the ideal single value of Cp may lead to the significant deviations in the evaluation of switching transients. To address the above issues, the analytical method of parasitic capacitance considering the impact of distributed disorder is studied in this paper. The impact of the winding model on the calculated value of Cp is investigated. The winding distribution patterns are categorized into three types: uniform, partially disordered, and fully disordered. An analytical method for the distributed capacitance is developed, incorporating the influence of random coil placement. A set of samples for the parasitic capacitance values of disordered windings is generated using a random sampling method. The sample distribution is determined through confidence intervals and the Chernoff bound to approximate the original distribution. The similarity between the two distributions is verified using the K-S test. The region with the highest frequency in the sample distribution is identified as the prediction interval for the winding's parasitic capacitance value. Finally, the measurements are performed on the disordered distribution winding samples. The results prove the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

title: A Study on Improving Superconducting Machine Performance by Focusing on End Windings
abstract: The current topology for superconducting machines aligns the effective stator length with the straight section of the rotor racetrack magnet, resulting in wasted superconducting material at the magnet's ends. Moreover, the ends of the superconducting magnet produce a substantial magnetic field, resulting in significant electromagnetic forces on the stator winding ends under rated operating conditions. This paper comprehensively analyzes and addresses the above issues in superconducting machines by proposing two improved stator end structures. Firstly, the difference between non-superconducting and superconducting machines on the stator side electromagnetic force is summarized by theoretical analysis. Then, based on the H-formulation, a three-dimensional numerical model reveals that the minimum critical current in traditional superconducting machines occurs at the end of the racetrack winding's straight section. The improved design in this paper increases it effectively. Moreover, it is demonstrated that without any modification of the high price of superconducting materials employed for the rotor, the output power of the proposed two structures can be effectively increased by 11.3% and 25.9%, respectively, while minimizing electromagnetic force at the stator end winding. A comprehensive comparison of the two proposed design modifications indicates that extending the stator's effective length and incorporating partial magnetic teeth at its ends is the more advantageous strategy. Finally, the experiment indicates that the proposed structure in this study enhances the critical current and mitigates the issue of stator end electromagnetic force.

title: Fine-Grained Optimal Allocation of Wind Farm Decoupled Models for CPU-GPU Parallel EMT Simulation
abstract: Parallel simulation based on CPU-GPU heterogeneous hardware, owing to its high speed-up ratio, has emerged as an effective approach for accelerating electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation of wind farms. However, most existing studies rely mainly on hardware multi-threading capabilities, with limited quantitative analysis of model-hardware adaptability, resulting in insufficient exploitation of the complementary advantages of CPUs and GPUs. To this end, this paper proposes a fine-grained optimal allocation method (FGOAM) that formulates the hardware assignment of each subsystem in wind farms as a constrained optimization problem for maximal simulation efficiency. Firstly, a bottom-up quantification method is developed to accurately assess the computational resources and solution time of decoupled models by decomposing the computation process into sequential and parallelizable steps. Secondly, a FGOAM for decoupled wind farm models is proposed, for the first time, by formulating an integer nonlinear programming (INLP) problem for step-level computation allocation. Finally, to further improve solution efficiency of FGOAM, an enhanced FGOAM (E-FGOAM) is derived via integer variable reduction without sacrificing allocation optimality. The accuracy of the proposed quantification method and the improvement on simulation efficiency after optimal allocation are validated. Simulation results demonstrate that the simulation speed is increased by two orders of magnitude for a wind farm consisting of 400 turbines.

title: Design of Cooling Structure for Yokeless and Segmented Armature Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Machine Based on Computational Fluid Dynamics
abstract: Yokeless and segmented armature (YASA) axial flux permanent magnet machine has a wide range of applications in electric vehicles, aerospace, and industrial robotics by virtue of its flat and compact structure, high power density, and high operating efficiency. However, when no cooling measures are adopted, such machine has the problem of poor heat dissipation conditions at the inner and outer ends of the windings, which seriously affects the further improvement of electromagnetic performance. Hence, based on fully utilizing the stator support’s interior space, this paper proposes two novel stator water-cooling structures, which are series internal and external circulating water-cooling structure (Series-IECWS) and parallel internal and external circulating water-cooling structure (Parallel-IECWS). Based on the theoretical foundation of computational fluid dynamics (CFD), the three-dimensional fluid field mathematical model and physical model of corresponding to the two cooling structures are established. The thermal and flow characteristics of the two water-cooling structures are investigated by the finite volume method. The Parallel-IECWS is preferred and its offset angle, rib width, and rounded corner radius parameters are optimized. Finally, a prototype of the principle type is manufactured and the temperature rise experiment is carried out. The experimental results verify the accuracy of theoretical analysis and simulation calculation. It is also verified that the Parallel-IECWS can effectively improve the temperature distribution of the inner and outer ends of the windings, improve the heat dissipation efficiency of the machine, and reduce the operating temperature.

title: Adaptive Current Control for High-Efficiency Motor Drive Operation in Transients
abstract: To ensure efficient operation of synchronous motors (SMs), it is essential to apply techniques that minimize losses. In most control systems, the maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control strategy is commonly used, as it offers a balance between simplicity and loss reduction. Developers typically focus on MTPA control during steady-state operation, which is the primary mode of most motor drives. However, in applications such as automotive systems and machine tools, motors often experience frequent transients, making it vital to incorporate MTPA control during these transients for optimal performance. This paper presents an algorithm designed to optimize current transients, aiming to guide the motor's current trajectory closer to the MTPA curve. Furthermore, considering that the Joule losses are proportional to squared currents, the proposed algorithm uses non-linear approximation, where approximation gains are proportional to squared currents. While the technique is inactive during steady-state operation, it becomes active when the control system detects a significant change in the current command and it dynamically modifies the gains of current controllers. When the transient is completed, the algorithm restores the original gains and deactivates. Experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed approach and show improved motor trajectories during transient operations.

title: Winding Process Simulation and Stress Analysis of Rotor Retained by Carbon Fiber Sleeve for High-Speed Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: Rotor stress analysis of high-speed permanent magnet machines (HSPMMs) is a crucial step in the early design stage, directly affecting the reliability and service life of the HSPMM. To accurately analyze the stress of the rotor retained by carbon fiber sleeve that is assembled by tension winding, this paper proposes an equivalent deformation method (EDM), aiming to simulate the process of winding the rotor with carbon fiber tow. Firstly, the stress model of rotor retained by multi-layer carbon fiber sleeve is analyzed. The EDM is proposed based on actual winding process. Then, taking a 300 kW, 50,000 r/min HSPMM as an example, the winding process is simulated. The results obtained by the proposed method are consistent with those of the existing methods. Further, the stresses of the rotor at four states after winding are analyzed. Finally, the static rotor contact pressure measurement and rotor overspeed test indicate the validity of the proposed method.

title: Robust Sliding Mode Control Strategy for Variable-Gear-Ratio Magnetic-Geared Machines
abstract: Variable-gear-ratio magnetic-geared machines (VGRMGMs) which could achieve adjustable gear ratios, shows substantial application prospects in driving systems. However, the VGRMGMs suffer from dynamic performance deficiencies such as slow dynamic responses and excessive speed overshoots. A robust sliding mode control (RSMC) strategy based on a load torque observer is proposed in this paper in order to improve the dynamic performance of the VGRMGM. A sliding mode speed controller and a torque observer for feedforward compensation in the current loop, is employed to improve the robustness and dynamic performance of the VGRMGM. Under speed-regulation conditions, the RSMC strategy achieves a 6% reduction in overshoot and a 25.4% improvement in response speed compared with conventional PI control. For load-variation conditions, the overshoot is reduced by 5%, and the response speed is improved by 32.1%, highlighting the VGRMGM superior transient performance. Experimental evaluations on a purpose-built test rig validate the enhancement of the RSMC strategy in terms of improved dynamic performance.

title: A Novel INFORM Strategy Based on Bidirectional Voltage-Vector Injection for Low-Speed Sensorless PMSM Control Considering Armature Reaction
abstract: The INFORM (INdirect Flux detection by Online Reactance Measurement) method is widely adopted for sensorless control of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) at low-speed. However, existing approaches either require additional voltage vector injection, increasing the switching frequency of power devices, or neglect the influence of stator current armature reaction, resulting in enlarged rotor position estimation errors. To address these issues, this paper proposes an INFORM-based rotor position estimation method that takes armature reaction into account without altering the switching frequency. By analyzing the mathematical expressions of stator current slopes under the action of voltage vectors, this method employs the current slope differences induced by the bidirectional voltage vectors of three phases for rotor position estimation, which can effectively reduce the position estimation errors caused by stator current armature reaction. Furthermore, a bidirectional voltage vector injection method was proposed, which generates six active voltage vectors within two or three PWM cycles without changing the switching frequency of the standard space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) method, thereby further improving the position estimation accuracy. The proposed method features a simple vector processing procedure and easy implementation for low-speed operations. An experimental platform is built to conduct experimental analysis and verification of the proposed algorithm. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively improve the rotor position estimation accuracy.

title: Hybrid Droop-Based Control for Parallel Operation of DC-DC Converters in a DC Microgrid
abstract: Connecting multiple converters in parallel to meet load demands in a DC microgrid leads to power sharing and circulating current issues. These issues are due to mismatches in the cables that connect the parallel converters to the load bus. Conventional droop control methods lack good dynamic performance and power sharing accuracy, requiring advanced methods to overcome these issues. This paper proposes a hybrid droop control strategy that uses an adaptive integral-based controller to improve the dynamic performance and overcome the power sharing issue. In this method, a correction term is integrated with the conventional droop method using the adaptive controller, which dynamically adjusts the reference voltage using only local measurements and a single data point over a low-bandwidth communication link. In addition, a delay compensation method is introduced to address the impacts of communication delay. The proposed controller combined with delay compensation reduces the settling time and overshoot in the current waveform. In addition, the impact of power sharing on circulating current is analyzed mathematically, and a solution is provided to reduce the circulating current. The proposed method is simple in design and easy to implement. Simulation and experimental studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Online Detection of Demagnetization Faults and Identification of Faulty Magnetic Poles Based on a Special Search Coil in PMSM
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) can experience demagnetization faults that negatively impact their performance and may result in serious consequences. However, current methods for detecting demagnetization in PMSMs cannot distinguish between uniform and partial demagnetization, making it challenging to accurately identify faulty poles in cases of partial demagnetization. To enable fast detection of partial demagnetization faults and expedite maintenance to reduce downtime, this paper proposes an online method for identifying the demagnetized poles using the segmented time-integral of the voltage from a specially designed search coil. The search coil is placed at the notches of the stator slots in PMSMs, and its terminal voltage is used to diagnose partial demagnetization faults, since the low-frequency fractional harmonic components in the coil voltage are distinctive characteristics of such faults. Furthermore, this paper introduces a criterion for identifying demagnetized poles, based on the segmented integral values of the search coil voltage, which correspond to the differences in the demagnetization degree of each pole. An experimental platform featuring a 10 kW, 8 pole PMSM driven by a PWM inverter has been established, and datasets of search coil voltages under various demagnetization fault conditions are constructed based on experiment data. The experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method for identifying the demagnetized poles.

title: Manufacturability Oriented Topology Optimization Framework for Electrical Machines Using NGnet
abstract: Topology optimization often produces unfeasible geometries, making manufacturing challenging. This paper addresses this limitation through the development of a methodology that utilizes a normalized Gaussian network (NGnet) with Gaussian functions of variable sizes unevenly distributed within an optimized space. The overlap of the Gaussian functions is analyzed for its impact on the final geometry. In addition, several modifications are applied to the NGnet output to achieve feasible geometries. Triangular elements are used to smooth the final geometry, enhancing its manufacturability. The matrix representation is used as a computational encoding for topology search and constraint checking, while the output is intended to be transferable to standard CAD and conventional manufacturing routes (laminated electrical steel).The main contribution is the integration of manufacturability constraints and geometry-repair operations before FEA evaluation, which reduces the number of infeasible candidates explored by the optimizer. The approach is demonstrated on a line-start synchronous reluctance machine rotor case study and can be extended to other electrical machine rotor topologies requiring multi-material feasibility constraints.

title: Flexible Virtual Impedance-based Fault Current Limitation and Harmonic Suppression Coordinated Control for Grid-forming Systems
abstract: For non-ideal grid-forming (GFM) systems with local nonlinear loads, effectively addressing both grid current harmonic distortion and system fault-ride-through remains a critical challenge due to inherent conflicts between conventional inverter overcurrent limitation and grid harmonic current suppression strategies. Additionally, GFM units are further required to limit transient fault overcurrent, provide timely fault current contribution, and maintain GFM characteristics for automatic fault recovery. These demands underscore the need for robust coordinated control strategies. To address these challenges, an inverter fault current limitation and grid harmonic current suppression coordinated control method is proposed, incorporating a harmonic control module and an adaptive virtual impedance (VI) module. The harmonic control module reduces inverter output impedance to absorb nonlinear load harmonics while increasing system total impedance to suppress grid background harmonics and inverter transient fault current. The adaptive VI module reduces inverter quasi-steady state fault current through fault-triggered VI and enhances system dynamic response to symmetrical and asymmetrical faults using Kalman Filter-based fault detection and a time-varying X/R ratio. The transient inverter output current limitation upon grid faults and grid harmonic current suppression under grid normal conditions can be both improved by simply increasing one feedback coefficient, greatly enhancing the coordinated control flexibility. The proposed method is validated through comparative experiments, demonstrating effective and robust coordinated control performance across different grid conditions and fault types.

title: Online Stator Inter-Turn Short Circuit Faults Detection in Interior PMSM Drives
abstract: In order to improve reliability and minimize maintenance effort of ac electric drives, online fault diagnosis represents an important tool. This paper proposes a detection algorithm for stator inter-turn short circuit (ITSC) faults in permanent magnet synchronous motor drives designed for online operation. Specifically, the focus is on main traction drive of a railway vehicle, where the emphasis is put on simple non-invasive implementation with no need for specialized hardware. Moreover, the goal is to achieve high reliability despite variable operational conditions which are typical in traction drive (load, speed, temperature, etc.). The algorithm is implemented using standard current sensors together with control hardware which combines the commonly available digital signal processor (DSP) and field programmable gate array (FPGA) to accelerate the calculations. Experimental testing is used to validate the proposed online detector on a laboratory prototype of an IPMSM drive, and the results are compared to selected state of the art diagnostic algorithm.

title: 3D On-Load Analytical Modeling of Iron-Core Axial-Flux Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Motor Through Coordinate Transformation
abstract: This paper presents a novel 3-dimensional coordinate transformed layer model (3D CTLM) for iron-core axial-flux permanent magnet synchronous motors (AFPMSMs). The proposed 3D CTLM initially transforms the cylindrical geometry of AFPMSMs into a 3D Cartesian coordinate system. The core advantage of such transformation lies in its ability to simplify complex 3D electromagnetic equations while maintaining the essential 3-dimensional field effects such as radial fringing and leakage fields. The equivalent transformation can be achieved using the 3D magnetic vector potential to represent on-load conditions and geometry functions, which account for the diverse permanent magnet and coil shapes. In addition, to overcome the non-homogeneous material problems due to iron-core teeth, a permeability matrix is utilized. The proposed modeling method is validated extensively by parametric studies, achieving an accuracy higher than 97% with two orders of magnitude faster in terms of calculation time as compared to a commercial FEM software. The validation manifests that the proposed modeling method is rapid and accurate enough to be used in the initial design and optimization phase of iron-cored AFPMSMs.

title: Mathematical Modeling for Collective Response of Photovoltaic Station Considering Intrinsic Dynamics Under Low Voltage Ride Through
abstract: Modern power system features growing complication and vulnerability with largely-penetrating renewable generation. The collective response of renewable power stations plays an important role in the dynamic study. However, the conventional disposal of an entire station as a one-off simultaneous trip-off oversimplifies the local intrinsic dynamics within station, probably resulting in unreliable estimation on system-level dynamics. In this paper, an external formulation describing the aggregation collective response of photovoltaic (PV) power station under grid disturbance is proposed, considering the multi-step-shaped in-station dynamics. Such a formulation is in a closed-form rather than dependent on iteration. It is achieved by decoupling the state variables in the voltage distribution model on the basis of reasonable simplification and correction afterwards. The proposed formulation is straightforward so that it can improve the simulation authenticity if integrated into system-level studies. It explicitly illustrates which variables dominate the local dynamics within PV station. The validation based on MATLAB platform confirms that the proposed model can efficiently and accurately describe the intrinsic multi-step-shaped dynamics of PV station during low voltage ride through.
